void Install(); void Uninstall(); bool Installed() const; void SetCommandMode(bool); bool CommandMode() const; void SetImeAllowed(bool); bool ImeAllowed() const; const KeyboardLayoutFacts& Layout() const; void RefreshLayout(std::uintptr_t); void PollFrame(void* hwnd); std::vector<TextInputEvent> TakeCommandModeEvents(); void DiscardUntakenEvents(); bool OnMessage(void* msg); }`. **TE5a-22 drives** `SetCommandMode` (Normal/Visual/operator-pending = true; false only while a LITERAL argument (`f t F T r`) waits, so dead keys compose; NAME arguments -- marks `m ' `` ` ``, registers `" q @`, Insert and command-line `Ctrl-R` -- keep command mode on, so names stay Latin on any layout; D-R1 as refined by D-R15. Insert `Ctrl-K` digraphs are outside v1's coverage, so nothing else waits for a literal) and `SetImeAllowed` (false on entering Normal/Visual/operator-pending, before the next key); TE2's view (TE2-13) reads `Layout()`, `ImeAllowed()`, `PollFrame(nullptr)` and `TakeCommandModeEvents()`, and consumes `TextInputFrame::events` front to back. No `AppendUtf8` of this chunk's own: characters are encoded with TE1's `Text::Utf8::Append` (CANON B13).

**The ordering source (D-R1, findings 2.3, 5a.17).** There is ONE stream: every named key, every Ctrl/Alt chord (`TextNamedKey::Chord`, rev-2 A12) and every character of a frame, in arrival order, each with a `seq` from `NextTextInputSeq()`. Outside command mode the reader takes them in ImGui's input-queue order: the frame's `InputEventsTrail` (what this `NewFrame` processed) followed by the still-queued tail of `InputEventsQueue` (what ImGui's trickling deferred to a later frame), each ImGui event read exactly once through an `EventId` cursor kept per ImGui context (reset by a `Shutdown` context hook). Reading the deferred tail too is what keeps a frame boundary clean: ImGui trickles a character that follows a non-character key to the NEXT frame, so a trail-only reader would hand `x<Esc>j` to vim as `x<Esc>` now and `j` a frame later -- after vim had already switched the hook into command mode, which then discards ImGui's text. The vendored ImGui (1.92.9) filters OS key repeats in `AddKeyAnalogEvent` (a repeated down is a duplicate), so typematic repeats are not in the queue: the reader appends ImGui's own repeats (`IsKeyPressed(key, repeat)` with `DownDuration > 0`) after the frame's queued events. In command mode the hook owns the whole stream: it records named keys and Ctrl/Alt chords (`WM_KEYDOWN` / `WM_SYSKEYDOWN`) AND characters (`WM_CHAR`, and `WM_DEADCHAR` as the bare symbol) in message order, and ImGui's copies of those keystrokes are read past and dropped for that frame. The view and vim consume `events` front to back; nothing is reordered by kind.

**Chords ride the stream (rev-2 A12).** A chord -- Ctrl and/or Alt with a letter, digit, US punctuation key or Space -- is a `Key` event whose `TextKeyPress::chordChar` names the key (`key` = `TextNamedKey::Chord`), recorded at its arrival position by the ImGui reader (from the key event, with the modifiers of its moment) and, in command mode, by the hook (`WM_KEYDOWN` / `WM_SYSKEYDOWN` with `GetKeyState(VK_CONTROL / VK_MENU)`). `chordChar` names the KEY (`ImGuiKey_R` / `'R'` -> `r`), never a layout character, so `Ctrl+R` reads the same on every layout. AltGr (Ctrl + Right Alt on a layout that has AltGr) is text, never a chord: `BuildTextInputFrame` drops Ctrl/Alt key events while AltGr is held, chords included, and the hook does not record one. A chord's control character (`WM_CHAR` 0x12 for Ctrl+R) still drops in the character filter. EditorActions keeps firing its action rows from ImGui's key state as before; the plain text view ignores chord events (`chordChar != 0`), and **TE5a-22** consumes them from the stream, so a Ctrl chord typed between two keys reaches vim between them (the residual "chords before the stream" order is gone).

**Layout and IME without SENT messages (D-R1, findings 2.1, 2.2, Review Focus F5).** `WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE` and `WM_SETFOCUS` are SENT messages: Windows dispatches them straight to the window procedure inside `PeekMessage`, so SDL's message hook -- and the chain behind it -- never sees them. The hook therefore POLLS: `PollFrame(hwnd)` compares `GetKeyboardLayout(0)` with the cached HKL (calling `RefreshLayout` on a change) and, while `!ImeAllowed()`, takes the input context away from `hwnd`, or from `GetFocus()` when `hwnd` is null, or from the window of the last posted key message when nothing has focus (`ImmAssociateContextEx(window, nullptr, 0)`); a focus move hands the window it left its context back. Disassociating on `WM_KEYDOWN` would be too late (IMM has processed that key already), and SDL3's `SDL_StartTextInput` re-associates the context whenever `imgui_impl_sdl3`'s `Platform_SetImeDataFn` asks for text input -- which ImGui 1.92.9 calls from `EndFrame` (imgui.cpp:6266-6275), not from `NewFrame`. So `PollFrame` runs twice a frame: at the start of the view's input step (TE2-13; the layout facts the frame's AltGr filter uses), and in `EditorApp::PumpFrameEvents` directly before the pump, i.e. after the previous frame's `EndFrame` and before IMM sees the next keystroke. `SetImeAllowed(false)` applies at once as well (TE5a-22 calls it on entering Normal mode, before the next key); `SetImeAllowed(true)` restores the default context (`IACE_DEFAULT`). The view still maps the flag to `ImGuiPlatformImeData::WantVisible`.

Notes the code relies on, read from the tree: SDL3 never delivers Tab/Enter/control characters as text (its `SDL_SendKeyboardText` drops unprintable characters), so Tab and Enter reach a text widget as named keys; the character filter still implements the spec's rule (drop 0x00-0x1F except Tab and Enter, and DEL 0x7F) for any other source -- the hook's `WM_CHAR` delivers 0x1B for Esc and 0x01 for Ctrl+A -- and drops a Tab/Enter character when the named key fired the same frame so nothing inserts twice. ImGui is built with 16-bit `ImWchar` (no `IMGUI_USE_WCHAR32` in imconfig.h or premake), so `ImTextCharFromUtf8` turns a typed non-BMP character into U+FFFD before it is queued (imgui.cpp:2673-2723, the out-of-range check at 2706 and the replacement at 2720); the stream drops it rather than inserting a replacement character, and reports it (see the self-review gap). The hook's `WM_CHAR` path joins UTF-16 surrogate pairs, so in command mode a non-BMP character arrives whole.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

`ArcaneTests/src/Text/TextInputStreamTest.cpp`:
```cpp
// Text editor TE2-10 (spec s5.5, D-R1): ONE ordered keyboard stream. Named keys,
// Ctrl/Alt chords (TextNamedKey::Chord, rev-2 A12) and characters come through
// here, in arrival order, each with a seq. Control characters drop (except Tab/Enter, never twice), AltGr makes a
// key event text instead of a chord, ImGui's queue is read once in order, and
// in command mode the hook owns the stream and turns WM_DEADCHAR into the bare
// symbol. The layout and the IME are POLLED (WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE / WM_SETFOCUS
// are sent messages the chain never sees) -- tested through the real queue.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "TextEditor/Core/Utf8.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextInput.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextInputHook.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Platform/WindowsMessageHooks.hpp>

#include <imgui.h>

#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#ifndef NOMINMAX
#define NOMINMAX
#endif
#include <windows.h>
#include <imm.h>
#pragma comment(lib, "imm32.lib")   // ImmGetContext / ImmCreateContext / ImmAssociateContext(Ex)

#include <algorithm>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

using namespace Arcane::Editor;

namespace
{
    TextInputEvent Ch(char32_t c)
    {
        TextInputEvent e;
        e.seq = NextTextInputSeq();
        e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Char;
        e.ch = c;
        return e;
    }

    TextInputEvent Key(TextNamedKey k, bool ctrl = false, bool shift = false, bool alt = false)
    {
        TextInputEvent e;
        e.seq = NextTextInputSeq();
        e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Key;
        e.key = TextKeyPress{ k, ctrl, shift, alt };
        return e;
    }

    // A Ctrl/Alt chord on the key `c` names (rev-2 A12).
    TextInputEvent Chord(char32_t c, bool ctrl, bool alt = false, bool shift = false)
    {
        TextInputEvent e = Key(TextNamedKey::Chord, ctrl, shift, alt);
        e.key.chordChar = c;
        return e;
    }

    // The frame as one string, in stream order: characters as UTF-8, keys as <Name>,
    // chords as <C-r> / <A-x> / <C-S-k> (modifiers, then the key).
    std::string Shape(const std::vector<TextInputEvent>& events)
    {
        static const char* const kNames[] = { "Left", "Right", "Up", "Down", "Home", "End", "PageUp", "PageDown",
                                              "Backspace", "Delete", "Enter", "Tab", "Escape", "Insert", "Chord" };
        std::string s;
        for (const TextInputEvent& e : events)
        {
            if (e.kind == TextInputEventKind::Char)
                Arcane::Text::Utf8::Append(s, e.ch);
            else if (e.key.chordChar != 0)
            {
                s += "<";
                if (e.key.ctrl) s += "C-";
                if (e.key.alt) s += "A-";
                if (e.key.shift) s += "S-";
                Arcane::Text::Utf8::Append(s, e.key.chordChar);
                s += ">";
            }
            else
                s += std::string("<") + kNames[static_cast<int>(e.key.key)] + ">";
        }
        return s;
    }

    // The calling thread's key state with Ctrl held, for the hook's GetKeyState
    // (SetKeyboardState changes this thread's state only); restored on exit.
    class ScopedCtrlHeld
    {
    public:
        ScopedCtrlHeld()
        {
            ::GetKeyboardState(m_saved);
            BYTE held[256];
            std::copy(std::begin(m_saved), std::end(m_saved), std::begin(held));
            held[VK_CONTROL] = 0x80;
            held[VK_LCONTROL] = 0x80;
            ::SetKeyboardState(held);
        }
        ~ScopedCtrlHeld() { ::SetKeyboardState(m_saved); }
        ScopedCtrlHeld(const ScopedCtrlHeld&) = delete;
        ScopedCtrlHeld& operator=(const ScopedCtrlHeld&) = delete;
    private:
        BYTE m_saved[256] = {};
    };

    std::string TextOf(const TextInputFrame& f)
    {
        std::string s;
        for (const TextInputEvent& e : f.events)
            if (e.kind == TextInputEventKind::Char)
                Arcane::Text::Utf8::Append(s, e.ch);
        return s;
    }

    std::size_t KeyCount(const TextInputFrame& f)
    {
        return static_cast<std::size_t>(std::count_if(f.events.begin(), f.events.end(),
            [](const TextInputEvent& e) { return e.kind == TextInputEventKind::Key; }));
    }

    struct ImGuiHarness
    {
        ImGuiContext* prev = ImGui::GetCurrentContext();
        ImGuiContext* ctx = ImGui::CreateContext();
        ImGuiHarness()
        {
            ImGui::SetCurrentContext(ctx);
            ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO();
            io.DisplaySize = ImVec2(800, 600);
            io.IniFilename = nullptr;
            unsigned char* px = nullptr;
            int w = 0, h = 0;
            io.Fonts->GetTexDataAsRGBA32(&px, &w, &h);
        }
        ~ImGuiHarness()
        {
            ImGui::DestroyContext(ctx);
            ImGui::SetCurrentContext(prev);
        }
        // One frame: NewFrame, read the stream, Render.
        RawTextInput Read(std::vector<TextInputEvent> commandModeEvents = {})
        {
            ImGui::GetIO().DeltaTime = 1.0f / 60.0f;
            ImGui::NewFrame();
            RawTextInput r = ReadImGuiTextInput(false, std::move(commandModeEvents));
            ImGui::Render();
            return r;
        }
    };

    bool HasInputContext(HWND hwnd)
    {
        const HIMC himc = ::ImmGetContext(hwnd);
        if (!himc)
            return false;
        ::ImmReleaseContext(hwnd, himc);
        return true;
    }

    class ScopedLayout
    {
    public:
        ScopedLayout(const wchar_t* klid, WORD expectedLanguage)
        {
            const int count = ::GetKeyboardLayoutList(0, nullptr);
            std::vector<HKL> before(static_cast<std::size_t>(count));
            ::GetKeyboardLayoutList(count, before.data());
            m_hkl = ::LoadKeyboardLayoutW(klid, KLF_NOTELLSHELL);
            m_loadedHere = m_hkl && std::find(before.begin(), before.end(), m_hkl) == before.end();
            m_ok = m_hkl && LOWORD(reinterpret_cast<UINT_PTR>(m_hkl)) == expectedLanguage;
        }
        ~ScopedLayout() { if (m_loadedHere) ::UnloadKeyboardLayout(m_hkl); }
        ScopedLayout(const ScopedLayout&) = delete;
        ScopedLayout& operator=(const ScopedLayout&) = delete;
        [[nodiscard]] bool Ok() const { return m_ok; }
        [[nodiscard]] std::uintptr_t Id() const { return reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(m_hkl); }
    private:
        HKL  m_hkl = nullptr;
        bool m_loadedHere = false;
        bool m_ok = false;
    };

    // The thread's active layout, restored on scope exit (ActivateKeyboardLayout
    // without KLF_SETFORPROCESS changes this thread only).
    class ScopedActiveLayout
    {
    public:
        explicit ScopedActiveLayout(std::uintptr_t layout)
            : m_previous(::ActivateKeyboardLayout(reinterpret_cast<HKL>(layout), 0)) {}
        ~ScopedActiveLayout() { if (m_previous) ::ActivateKeyboardLayout(m_previous, 0); }
        ScopedActiveLayout(const ScopedActiveLayout&) = delete;
        ScopedActiveLayout& operator=(const ScopedActiveLayout&) = delete;
    private:
        HKL m_previous = nullptr;
    };

    // A hidden window whose procedure counts what reaches it.
    struct WindowProbe
    {
        int chars = 0;          // WM_CHAR dispatched to the window
        int compositions = 0;   // WM_IME_STARTCOMPOSITION / WM_IME_COMPOSITION
    };

    LRESULT CALLBACK ProbeProc(HWND hwnd, UINT msg, WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam)
    {
        if (auto* probe = reinterpret_cast<WindowProbe*>(::GetWindowLongPtrW(hwnd, GWLP_USERDATA)))
        {
            if (msg == WM_CHAR) ++probe->chars;
            if (msg == WM_IME_STARTCOMPOSITION || msg == WM_IME_COMPOSITION) ++probe->compositions;
        }
        return ::DefWindowProcW(hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam);
    }

    class ProbeWindow
    {
    public:
        ProbeWindow()
        {
            static const ATOM kClass = []
            {
                WNDCLASSW wc{};
                wc.lpfnWndProc = &ProbeProc;
                wc.hInstance = ::GetModuleHandleW(nullptr);
                wc.lpszClassName = L"ArcaneTextInputProbe";
                return ::RegisterClassW(&wc);
            }();
            m_hwnd = ::CreateWindowExW(0, reinterpret_cast<LPCWSTR>(static_cast<ULONG_PTR>(kClass)), L"text-input-probe",
                                       WS_OVERLAPPED, 0, 0, 64, 64, nullptr, nullptr, ::GetModuleHandleW(nullptr), nullptr);
            if (m_hwnd)
                ::SetWindowLongPtrW(m_hwnd, GWLP_USERDATA, reinterpret_cast<LONG_PTR>(&m_probe));
        }
        ~ProbeWindow() { if (m_hwnd) ::DestroyWindow(m_hwnd); }
        ProbeWindow(const ProbeWindow&) = delete;
        ProbeWindow& operator=(const ProbeWindow&) = delete;
        [[nodiscard]] HWND Get() const { return m_hwnd; }
        [[nodiscard]] const WindowProbe& Probe() const { return m_probe; }
    private:
        HWND        m_hwnd = nullptr;
        WindowProbe m_probe;
    };

    // SDL3's WIN_PumpEvents, message for message: the chained hook first (false
    // swallows), then TranslateMessage + DispatchMessage.
    void PumpLikeSdl(HWND hwnd)
    {
        MSG msg{};
        while (::PeekMessageW(&msg, hwnd, 0, 0, PM_REMOVE))
        {
            if (!Arcane::RunWindowsMessageHooks(&msg))
                continue;
            ::TranslateMessage(&msg);
            ::DispatchMessageW(&msg);
        }
    }

    // A key press through the real queue: PostMessage, then the pump. Only the
    // WM_KEYDOWN is posted; TranslateMessage posts its WM_CHAR, which the same
    // pump delivers (posting a WM_CHAR as well would deliver the character twice).
    void PostKey(HWND hwnd, UINT vk)
    {
        const UINT scan = ::MapVirtualKeyW(vk, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC);
        ::PostMessageW(hwnd, WM_KEYDOWN, vk, static_cast<LPARAM>(1u | (scan << 16)));
        PumpLikeSdl(hwnd);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("text input: control characters drop except Tab and Enter, never twice with the named key", "[text-input]")
{
    RawTextInput raw;
    raw.events = { Ch(U'a'), Ch(0x01), Ch(0x16), Ch(U'b'), Ch(0x7F), Ch(U'\t'), Ch(U'c'), Ch(U'\r'), Ch(0x00), Ch(U'\n') };
    TextInputFrame f = BuildTextInputFrame(raw);
    CHECK(TextOf(f) == "ab\tc\n\n");                         // Ctrl+A / Ctrl+V's 0x01 / 0x16, DEL and NUL gone; CR -> LF

    raw.events.push_back(Key(TextNamedKey::Tab));
    raw.events.push_back(Key(TextNamedKey::Enter));
    f = BuildTextInputFrame(raw);
    CHECK(TextOf(f) == "abc");                               // the named keys own Tab and Enter this frame
    CHECK(Shape(f.events) == "abc<Tab><Enter>");
}

TEST_CASE("text input: AltGr is text, never a chord -- only on a layout that has AltGr", "[text-input]")
{
    RawTextInput raw;
    raw.layoutHasAltGr = true;
    raw.rightAltDown = true;
    raw.events = { Key(TextNamedKey::Up, true, false, true),   // Ctrl+Alt+Up while AltGr is held
                   Key(TextNamedKey::Left),                    // a plain arrow still moves
                   Ch(U'{') };
    TextInputFrame f = BuildTextInputFrame(raw);
    CHECK(f.altGrHeld);
    CHECK(Shape(f.events) == "<Left>{");

    raw.events.push_back(Chord(U'q', true, true));             // Ctrl+Alt+Q under AltGr: text (@ on German), never a chord
    f = BuildTextInputFrame(raw);
    CHECK(Shape(f.events) == "<Left>{");

    raw.rightAltDown = false;                                  // Left Alt + Ctrl: a real chord
    f = BuildTextInputFrame(raw);
    CHECK_FALSE(f.altGrHeld);
    CHECK(KeyCount(f) == 3u);
    CHECK(Shape(f.events) == "<Up><Left>{<C-A-q>");
    raw.events.pop_back();

    raw.rightAltDown = true;
    raw.layoutHasAltGr = false;                                // US: Right Alt is just Alt
    f = BuildTextInputFrame(raw);
    CHECK_FALSE(f.altGrHeld);
    CHECK(KeyCount(f) == 2u);
}

TEST_CASE("text input: one stream -- UTF-8 out, U+FFFD dropped, arrival order kept across kinds, merged by seq", "[text-input]")
{
    RawTextInput utf;
    utf.events = { Ch(U'\u00e9'), Ch(U'\u20ac'), Ch(U'\U0001F600') };   // encoded by Text::Utf8::Append
    CHECK(TextOf(BuildTextInputFrame(utf)) == "\xC3\xA9\xE2\x82\xAC\xF0\x9F\x98\x80");

    // 5a.17: `x<Esc>j` in one slow frame is x, then Esc, then j -- never "xj" then Esc.
    RawTextInput raw;
    raw.events = { Ch(U'x'), Key(TextNamedKey::Escape), Ch(U'j'), Ch(0xFFFD), Key(TextNamedKey::Left) };
    const TextInputFrame f = BuildTextInputFrame(raw);
    CHECK(Shape(f.events) == "x<Escape>j<Left>");
    CHECK(f.droppedUnsupported);

    // Rev-2 A12: a chord is an event at its place -- `i`, Ctrl+R, `a` is i, <C-r>, a --
    // and its control character (0x12) still drops.
    RawTextInput chord;
    chord.events = { Ch(U'i'), Chord(U'r', true), Ch(0x12), Ch(U'a') };
    CHECK(Shape(BuildTextInputFrame(chord).events) == "i<C-r>a");

    // Two sources merge by seq, whatever order the vector holds them in.
    const TextInputEvent a = Ch(U'a');
    const TextInputEvent esc = Key(TextNamedKey::Escape);
    const TextInputEvent b = Ch(U'b');
    RawTextInput mixed;
    mixed.events = { b, a, esc };
    CHECK(Shape(BuildTextInputFrame(mixed).events) == "a<Escape>b");
    CHECK(a.seq < esc.seq);
    CHECK(esc.seq < b.seq);
}

TEST_CASE("text input: ReadImGuiTextInput reads ImGui's queue in order, each event once, with the modifiers of its moment", "[text-input]")
{
    ImGuiHarness h;
    ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO();
    h.Read();
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiMod_Shift, true);
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_LeftArrow, true);
    io.AddInputCharacter('x');
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_Escape, true);
    io.AddInputCharacter('j');
    const RawTextInput first = h.Read();                       // ONE frame: the trail AND the trickled tail
    CHECK(Shape(first.events) == "<Left>x<Escape>j");
    REQUIRE(first.events.size() == 4u);
    CHECK(first.events[0].key.shift);
    CHECK(first.events[2].key.shift);
    CHECK_FALSE(first.events[0].fromCommandHook);
    for (std::size_t i = 1; i < first.events.size(); ++i)
        CHECK(first.events[i - 1].seq < first.events[i].seq);
    CHECK(io.InputQueueCharacters.Size == 0);                  // drained: no other widget types it again

    CHECK(h.Read().events.empty());                            // the next frame processes the tail: nothing is read twice

    // Insert is a named key too (TE5's vim layer maps it to <Insert>).
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiMod_Shift, false);
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_LeftArrow, false);
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_Escape, false);
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_Insert, true);
    const RawTextInput ins = h.Read();
    REQUIRE(ins.events.size() == 1u);
    CHECK(ins.events[0].key.key == TextNamedKey::Insert);
    CHECK_FALSE(ins.events[0].key.shift);

    // Rev-2 A12: a Ctrl chord is read at its place in the queue, named by its key;
    // a plain or Shift-only letter is not a chord (it arrives as a character).
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_Insert, false);
    io.AddInputCharacter('i');
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiMod_Ctrl, true);
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_R, true);
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_R, false);
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiMod_Ctrl, false);
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_A, true);
    io.AddInputCharacter('a');
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_A, false);
    const RawTextInput chords = h.Read();
    CHECK(Shape(chords.events) == "i<C-r>a");
    REQUIRE(chords.events.size() == 3u);
    CHECK(chords.events[1].kind == TextInputEventKind::Key);
    CHECK(chords.events[1].key.key == TextNamedKey::Chord);
    CHECK(chords.events[1].key.chordChar == U'r');
    CHECK(chords.events[0].seq < chords.events[1].seq);
    CHECK(chords.events[1].seq < chords.events[2].seq);
}

TEST_CASE("text input: a held key repeats at ImGui's typematic rate, the press itself counted once", "[text-input]")
{
    ImGuiHarness h;
    ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO();
    h.Read();
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_Backspace, true);
    int presses = 0;
    for (int frame = 0; frame < 60; ++frame)                   // one second held
        for (const TextInputEvent& e : h.Read().events)
            if (e.kind == TextInputEventKind::Key && e.key.key == TextNamedKey::Backspace)
                ++presses;
    CHECK(presses > 5);                                        // repeats after KeyRepeatDelay (0.275 s) at KeyRepeatRate (0.05 s)
    CHECK(presses < 30);                                       // ...never one per frame
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_Backspace, false);
    h.Read();
    CHECK(h.Read().events.empty());
}

TEST_CASE("text input: command-mode events replace ImGui's copy of the same keystrokes, which is never replayed", "[text-input]")
{
    ImGuiHarness h;
    ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO();
    h.Read();
    io.AddKeyEvent(ImGuiKey_J, true);                          // what SDL gave ImGui for the keystroke...
    io.AddInputCharacter('j');
    TextInputEvent fromHook = Ch(U'j');                        // ...and what the hook recorded for it
    fromHook.fromCommandHook = true;
    const RawTextInput r = h.Read({ fromHook });
    REQUIRE(r.events.size() == 1u);
    CHECK(r.events[0].fromCommandHook);
    CHECK(Shape(r.events) == "j");
    CHECK(h.Read().events.empty());                            // ImGui's 'j' was read past, not deferred
}

TEST_CASE("text input hook: in command mode the hook records keys and characters in message order; WM_DEADCHAR becomes the bare symbol", "[text-input]")
{
    TextInputHook hook;
    MSG dead{};
    dead.message = WM_DEADCHAR;
    dead.wParam = L'^';
    CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&dead));                              // text-entry mode: composition is left alone
    CHECK(hook.TakeCommandModeEvents().empty());

    hook.SetCommandMode(true);
    CHECK(hook.CommandMode());
    MSG f{};
    f.message = WM_CHAR;
    f.wParam = L'f';
    CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&f));                                 // passed on (SDL still sees it), and recorded
    dead.wParam = L'"';
    CHECK_FALSE(hook.OnMessage(&dead));                        // swallowed; the dead state is consumed
    MSG esc{};
    esc.message = WM_KEYDOWN;
    esc.wParam = VK_ESCAPE;
    CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&esc));
    MSG high{}, low{};
    high.message = low.message = WM_CHAR;
    high.wParam = 0xD83D;                                      // U+1F600 as a surrogate pair
    low.wParam = 0xDE00;
    CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&high));
    CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&low));

    {
        const ScopedCtrlHeld ctrl;                             // rev-2 A12: Ctrl+R in command mode is a chord event at its place
        MSG r{};
        r.message = WM_KEYDOWN;
        r.wParam = 'R';
        CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&r));
        MSG ctrlChar{};
        ctrlChar.message = WM_CHAR;
        ctrlChar.wParam = 0x12;                                // TranslateMessage's control character for Ctrl+R
        CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&ctrlChar));
    }

    const std::vector<TextInputEvent> ev = hook.TakeCommandModeEvents();
    REQUIRE(ev.size() == 6u);
    for (const TextInputEvent& e : ev)
        CHECK(e.fromCommandHook);
    for (std::size_t i = 1; i < ev.size(); ++i)
        CHECK(ev[i - 1].seq < ev[i].seq);
    CHECK(ev[3].ch == U'\U0001F600');                          // joined: the hook has no 16-bit limit
    CHECK(ev[4].kind == TextInputEventKind::Key);
    CHECK(ev[4].key.key == TextNamedKey::Chord);
    CHECK(ev[4].key.ctrl);
    CHECK(ev[4].key.chordChar == U'r');
    RawTextInput raw;
    raw.events = ev;
    CHECK(Shape(BuildTextInputFrame(raw).events) == "f\"<Escape>\xF0\x9F\x98\x80<C-r>");   // finding 2.3: never "\"f"; 0x12 dropped
    CHECK(hook.TakeCommandModeEvents().empty());

    hook.SetCommandMode(false);
    CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&f));
    CHECK(hook.TakeCommandModeEvents().empty());               // outside command mode ImGui's queue is the source

    hook.SetCommandMode(true);
    CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&f));
    hook.DiscardUntakenEvents();                               // no text view took them this frame
    CHECK(hook.TakeCommandModeEvents().empty());
}

TEST_CASE("text input hook: a REAL pending dead key is consumed in command mode, so the next key comes out uncomposed (finding 2.4)", "[text-input]")
{
    const ScopedLayout intl(L"00020409", 0x0409);
    if (!intl.Ok()) SKIP("the US-International layout could not be loaded");
    const HKL hkl = reinterpret_cast<HKL>(intl.Id());
    const BYTE none[256] = {};
    wchar_t buf[8] = {};
    // flags 0: the call CHANGES the thread's keyboard state, as TranslateMessage does
    const auto press = [&](UINT vk) { return ::ToUnicodeEx(vk, ::MapVirtualKeyExW(vk, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC, hkl), none, buf, 8, 0, hkl); };

    REQUIRE(press(VK_OEM_7) < 0);                              // control: ' is dead here...
    REQUIRE(press('E') == 1);
    REQUIRE(buf[0] == L'\u00e9');                              // ...and composes with e

    TextInputHook hook;
    hook.RefreshLayout(intl.Id());
    hook.SetCommandMode(true);
    REQUIRE(press(VK_OEM_7) < 0);                              // a dead key is pending in the thread's state
    MSG dead{};
    dead.message = WM_DEADCHAR;
    dead.wParam = L'\'';
    CHECK_FALSE(hook.OnMessage(&dead));
    CHECK(press('E') == 1);
    CHECK(buf[0] == L'e');                                     // uncomposed: `'e` in vim is mark e, never é
    const std::vector<TextInputEvent> ev = hook.TakeCommandModeEvents();
    REQUIRE(ev.size() == 1u);
    CHECK(ev[0].ch == U'\'');
}

TEST_CASE("text input hook (F5): with the IME disallowed PollFrame takes the context away every frame; `j` through the real queue is a character, never a composition", "[text-input]")
{
    const ProbeWindow window;
    REQUIRE(window.Get() != nullptr);
    const bool hadDefault = HasInputContext(window.Get());
    // A Japanese IME when the system has one; either way an open context stands in for SDL3's own.
    const ScopedLayout ja(L"00000411", 0x0411);
    std::optional<ScopedActiveLayout> japanese;
    if (ja.Ok()) japanese.emplace(ja.Id()); else WARN("no Japanese layout on this system: a test input context stands in");
    const HIMC himc = ::ImmCreateContext();
    REQUIRE(himc != nullptr);
    ::ImmAssociateContext(window.Get(), himc);
    ::ImmSetOpenStatus(himc, TRUE);                            // the IME is ON, as a Japanese user leaves it
    REQUIRE(HasInputContext(window.Get()));

    TextInputHook hook;
    hook.Install();
    hook.SetCommandMode(true);                                 // vim Normal mode (TE5a-22)...
    hook.SetImeAllowed(false);                                 // ...the IME off BEFORE the next key
    hook.PollFrame(window.Get());
    CHECK_FALSE(HasInputContext(window.Get()));

    ::ImmAssociateContext(window.Get(), himc);                 // SDL_StartTextInput re-associates (Platform_SetImeDataFn, EndFrame)
    REQUIRE(HasInputContext(window.Get()));
    hook.PollFrame(window.Get());                              // the next frame, before the pump
    CHECK_FALSE(HasInputContext(window.Get()));

    PostKey(window.Get(), 'J');                                // PostMessage -> PeekMessage -> the chain -> TranslateMessage
    const std::vector<TextInputEvent> ev = hook.TakeCommandModeEvents();
    REQUIRE(ev.size() == 1u);
    CHECK(ev[0].kind == TextInputEventKind::Char);
    CHECK(ev[0].ch == U'j');
    CHECK(ev[0].fromCommandHook);
    CHECK(window.Probe().chars == 1);
    CHECK(window.Probe().compositions == 0);

    hook.SetImeAllowed(true);                                  // Insert mode: the window's default context is back
    CHECK(HasInputContext(window.Get()) == hadDefault);
    hook.Uninstall();
    ::ImmAssociateContext(window.Get(), nullptr);
    ::ImmDestroyContext(himc);
}

TEST_CASE("text input hook: PollFrame picks up a layout switch; a SENT WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE never reaches the chain (finding 2.1)", "[text-input]")
{
    const ScopedLayout de(L"00000407", 0x0407);
    const ScopedLayout us(L"00000409", 0x0409);
    if (!de.Ok() || !us.Ok()) SKIP("the German or US layout could not be loaded");
    const ProbeWindow window;
    REQUIRE(window.Get() != nullptr);
    std::optional<ScopedActiveLayout> active;
    active.emplace(us.Id());
    TextInputHook hook;
    hook.Install();
    hook.PollFrame(window.Get());
    CHECK(hook.Layout().layout == us.Id());
    CHECK_FALSE(hook.Layout().hasAltGr);

    // What Windows does on a switch: the message is SENT to the window procedure.
    ::SendMessageW(window.Get(), WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE, 0, static_cast<LPARAM>(de.Id()));
    PumpLikeSdl(window.Get());
    CHECK(hook.Layout().layout == us.Id());                    // the chain never saw it: which is why the hook polls

    active.reset();
    active.emplace(de.Id());
    hook.PollFrame(window.Get());
    CHECK(hook.Layout().layout == de.Id());
    CHECK(hook.Layout().hasAltGr);
    hook.Uninstall();
}

    REQUIRE(ev.size() == 1u);

    CHECK_FALSE(hook.Installed());
    CHECK(Arcane::RunWindowsMessageHooks(&m));
}

```cpp
#pragma once

// The text editor's keyboard stream (spec s5.5, D-R1). This file turns one
// frame of keyboard input into ONE ordered stream of NAMED KEYS (the navigation
// and editing keys a text widget handles itself), CHORDS (Ctrl and/or Alt with a
// letter, digit, punctuation key or Space -- TextNamedKey::Chord, rev-2 A12) and
// CHARACTERS (what the OS layout produced), in arrival order, each stamped with a
// seq from one process-wide counter. The consumer (the view, vim) reads `events`
// front to back; nothing is grouped by kind. EditorActions still fires its action
// rows from ImGui's key state; the plain view ignores Chord events, vim (TE5a-22)
// consumes them at their place.
// The character filter drops 0x00-0x1F except Tab and Enter (and DEL), so a
// Ctrl+letter's control character never doubles its chord.

#include <cstdint>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    enum class TextNamedKey : std::uint8_t
    {
        Left, Right, Up, Down, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Backspace, Delete, Enter, Tab, Escape,
        Insert,   // ImGuiKey_Insert / VK_INSERT: TE2's view ignores it; TE5's vim layer maps it to <Insert>
        Chord,    // rev-2 A12: Ctrl and/or Alt + a non-named key; TextKeyPress::chordChar names the key
    };

    struct TextKeyPress
    {
        TextNamedKey key = TextNamedKey::Left;
        bool ctrl = false, shift = false, alt = false;
        // Rev-2 A12: non-zero = a CHORD event (key == Chord): the key it names, a-z 0-9
        // ' , - . / ; = [ \ ] ` or space, from the key, never the layout's character.
        char32_t chordChar = 0;
    };

    enum class TextInputEventKind : std::uint8_t { Key, Char };

    struct TextInputEvent
    {
        std::uint64_t      seq = 0;                       // NextTextInputSeq(): arrival order across both sources
        TextInputEventKind kind = TextInputEventKind::Char;
        TextKeyPress       key;                           // kind == Key
        char32_t           ch = 0;                        // kind == Char
        bool               fromCommandHook = false;       // recorded by TextInputHook in command mode
    };

    // The ONE counter both the ImGui reader and TextInputHook stamp events with.
    [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t NextTextInputSeq();

    struct RawTextInput
    {
        std::vector<TextInputEvent> events;   // this frame's keys and characters, in arrival order
        bool rightAltDown = false;            // Right Alt was held at some point this frame
        bool layoutHasAltGr = false;
    };

    struct TextInputFrame
    {
        std::vector<TextInputEvent> events;   // filtered, merged by seq; consume front to back
        bool altGrHeld = false;               // this frame's Ctrl+Alt key events are text, never chords
        bool droppedUnsupported = false;      // a U+FFFD from ImGui's 16-bit queue was dropped
    };

    // The key a chord names (rev-2 A12): a-z, 0-9, the US punctuation keys and
    // Space, lowercase; nullopt for any other key (F-keys, named keys, modifiers).
    [[nodiscard]] std::optional<char32_t> ChordKeyChar(int imguiKey);
    [[nodiscard]] std::optional<char32_t> ChordKeyCharForVirtualKey(std::uintptr_t virtualKey);

    // Merges by seq (stable) and filters per event: AltGr drops Ctrl/Alt key
    // events, chords included; characters drop 0x00-0x1F except Tab/Enter, DEL and U+FFFD; a
    // Tab/Enter character drops when its named key is in the frame; CR -> LF.
    [[nodiscard]] TextInputFrame BuildTextInputFrame(const RawTextInput& raw);

    // Every ImGui keyboard event since the last read, in ImGui's queue order: the
    // frame's InputEventsTrail, then the still-queued (trickled) tail -- each read
    // exactly once (an EventId cursor per ImGui context) -- plus ImGui's typematic
    // repeats of held named keys. DRAINS io.InputQueueCharacters (the widget that
    // owns the keyboard consumes it, as InputText does). When `commandModeEvents`
    // is not empty the hook recorded this frame's keystrokes in command mode: they
    // ARE the stream, and ImGui's copies are read past and dropped. Needs a frame.
    [[nodiscard]] RawTextInput ReadImGuiTextInput(bool layoutHasAltGr, std::vector<TextInputEvent> commandModeEvents);
}

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/TextInput.cpp`:
```cpp
#include "TextEditor/View/TextInput.hpp"

#include "TextEditor/Core/Utf8.hpp"   // Text::Utf8::Append: the one UTF-8 encoder (CANON B13)

#include <imgui.h>
#include <imgui_internal.h>   // ImGuiContext::InputEventsTrail / InputEventsQueue, ImGuiInputEvent, GetKeyData, AddContextHook

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <optional>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    namespace
    {
        bool HasKey(const std::vector<TextInputEvent>& events, TextNamedKey k)
        {
            return std::any_of(events.begin(), events.end(),
                               [&](const TextInputEvent& e) { return e.kind == TextInputEventKind::Key && e.key.key == k; });
        }

        struct KeyMap
        {
            ImGuiKey     imgui;
            TextNamedKey named;
        };
        constexpr KeyMap kKeyMap[] = {
            { ImGuiKey_LeftArrow, TextNamedKey::Left },    { ImGuiKey_RightArrow, TextNamedKey::Right },
            { ImGuiKey_UpArrow, TextNamedKey::Up },        { ImGuiKey_DownArrow, TextNamedKey::Down },
            { ImGuiKey_Home, TextNamedKey::Home },         { ImGuiKey_End, TextNamedKey::End },
            { ImGuiKey_PageUp, TextNamedKey::PageUp },     { ImGuiKey_PageDown, TextNamedKey::PageDown },
            { ImGuiKey_Backspace, TextNamedKey::Backspace }, { ImGuiKey_Delete, TextNamedKey::Delete },
            { ImGuiKey_Enter, TextNamedKey::Enter },       { ImGuiKey_KeypadEnter, TextNamedKey::Enter },
            { ImGuiKey_Tab, TextNamedKey::Tab },           { ImGuiKey_Escape, TextNamedKey::Escape },
            { ImGuiKey_Insert, TextNamedKey::Insert },
        };

        std::optional<TextNamedKey> Named(ImGuiKey key)
        {
            for (const KeyMap& m : kKeyMap)
                if (m.imgui == key)
                    return m.named;
            return std::nullopt;
        }

        // Rev-2 A12: the punctuation keys a chord may name (the letters and digits
        // are the contiguous ImGuiKey_A..Z / ImGuiKey_0..9 ranges).
        struct ChordPunct
        {
            ImGuiKey imgui;
            char32_t ch;
        };
        constexpr ChordPunct kChordPunct[] = {
            { ImGuiKey_Apostrophe, U'\'' }, { ImGuiKey_Comma, U',' },        { ImGuiKey_Minus, U'-' },
            { ImGuiKey_Period, U'.' },      { ImGuiKey_Slash, U'/' },        { ImGuiKey_Semicolon, U';' },
            { ImGuiKey_Equal, U'=' },       { ImGuiKey_LeftBracket, U'[' },  { ImGuiKey_Backslash, U'\\' },
            { ImGuiKey_RightBracket, U']' }, { ImGuiKey_GraveAccent, U'`' }, { ImGuiKey_Space, U' ' },
        };

        // Every key a chord may name, for the typematic sweep.
        template <class F>
        void ForEachChordKey(F&& f)
        {
            for (int k = ImGuiKey_0; k <= ImGuiKey_9; ++k) f(static_cast<ImGuiKey>(k));
            for (int k = ImGuiKey_A; k <= ImGuiKey_Z; ++k) f(static_cast<ImGuiKey>(k));
            for (const ChordPunct& p : kChordPunct) f(p.imgui);
        }

        TextInputEvent ChordEvent(char32_t key, bool ctrl, bool shift, bool alt)
        {
            TextInputEvent ev;
            ev.seq = NextTextInputSeq();
            ev.kind = TextInputEventKind::Key;
            ev.key = TextKeyPress{ TextNamedKey::Chord, ctrl, shift, alt, key };
            return ev;
        }

        // Which ImGui events the stream has read, per ImGui context. EventId is
        // unique and increasing within a context; a destroyed context forgets its
        // cursor (a new context at the same address starts from zero).
        struct ImGuiReadCursor
        {
            ImGuiContext* context = nullptr;
            ImU32         lastEventId = 0;
            bool          ctrl = false, shift = false, alt = false, rightAlt = false;   // as of lastEventId
        };

        std::vector<ImGuiReadCursor>& Cursors()
        {
            static std::vector<ImGuiReadCursor> cursors;
            return cursors;
        }

        void ForgetContext(ImGuiContext* ctx, ImGuiContextHook*)
        {
            std::erase_if(Cursors(), [ctx](const ImGuiReadCursor& c) { return c.context == ctx; });
        }

        ImGuiReadCursor& CursorFor(ImGuiContext& g)
        {
            for (ImGuiReadCursor& c : Cursors())
                if (c.context == &g)
                    return c;
            ImGuiContextHook hook;
            hook.Type = ImGuiContextHookType_Shutdown;
            hook.Callback = &ForgetContext;
            ImGui::AddContextHook(&g, &hook);
            ImGuiReadCursor fresh;
            fresh.context = &g;
            Cursors().push_back(fresh);
            return Cursors().back();
        }

        // The modifier state just BEFORE `first` (the oldest unread event): an
        // event for a modifier flips it (ImGui drops duplicate downs/ups), so the
        // state before its first unread event is the opposite; with none unread,
        // the processed key state is current.
        bool StateBefore(ImGuiContext& g, const std::vector<const ImGuiInputEvent*>& unread, ImGuiKey mod)
        {
            for (const ImGuiInputEvent* e : unread)
                if (e->Type == ImGuiInputEventType_Key && e->Key.Key == mod)
                    return !e->Key.Down;
            return ImGui::GetKeyData(&g, mod)->Down;
        }
    }

    std::uint64_t NextTextInputSeq()
    {
        static std::atomic<std::uint64_t> counter{ 0 };
        return ++counter;
    }

    std::optional<char32_t> ChordKeyChar(int imguiKey)
    {
        if (imguiKey >= ImGuiKey_A && imguiKey <= ImGuiKey_Z)
            return static_cast<char32_t>(U'a' + (imguiKey - ImGuiKey_A));
        if (imguiKey >= ImGuiKey_0 && imguiKey <= ImGuiKey_9)
            return static_cast<char32_t>(U'0' + (imguiKey - ImGuiKey_0));
        for (const ChordPunct& p : kChordPunct)
            if (p.imgui == imguiKey)
                return p.ch;
        return std::nullopt;
    }

    std::optional<char32_t> ChordKeyCharForVirtualKey(std::uintptr_t vk)
    {
        if (vk >= 'A' && vk <= 'Z')
            return static_cast<char32_t>(U'a' + (vk - 'A'));
        if (vk >= '0' && vk <= '9')
            return static_cast<char32_t>(U'0' + (vk - '0'));
        switch (vk)   // the VK_OEM_* codes (winuser.h values; this file stays free of windows.h)
        {
        case 0xDE: return U'\'';   // VK_OEM_7
        case 0xBC: return U',';    // VK_OEM_COMMA
        case 0xBD: return U'-';    // VK_OEM_MINUS
        case 0xBE: return U'.';    // VK_OEM_PERIOD
        case 0xBF: return U'/';    // VK_OEM_2
        case 0xBA: return U';';    // VK_OEM_1
        case 0xBB: return U'=';    // VK_OEM_PLUS
        case 0xDB: return U'[';    // VK_OEM_4
        case 0xDC: return U'\\';   // VK_OEM_5
        case 0xDD: return U']';    // VK_OEM_6
        case 0xC0: return U'`';    // VK_OEM_3
        case 0x20: return U' ';    // VK_SPACE
        default:   return std::nullopt;
        }
    }

    TextInputFrame BuildTextInputFrame(const RawTextInput& raw)
    {
        TextInputFrame f;
        f.altGrHeld = raw.layoutHasAltGr && raw.rightAltDown;
        std::vector<TextInputEvent> ordered = raw.events;
        std::stable_sort(ordered.begin(), ordered.end(),
                         [](const TextInputEvent& a, const TextInputEvent& b) { return a.seq < b.seq; });   // merge by seq
        std::vector<TextInputEvent> keys;
        for (const TextInputEvent& e : ordered)
            if (e.kind == TextInputEventKind::Key && !(f.altGrHeld && (e.key.ctrl || e.key.alt)))
                keys.push_back(e);
        const bool tabKey = HasKey(keys, TextNamedKey::Tab);
        const bool enterKey = HasKey(keys, TextNamedKey::Enter);
        for (const TextInputEvent& e : ordered)
        {
            if (e.kind == TextInputEventKind::Key)
            {
                if (f.altGrHeld && (e.key.ctrl || e.key.alt))
                    continue;   // AltGr (Left Ctrl + Right Alt) is text: never a chord
                f.events.push_back(e);
                continue;
            }
            char32_t c = e.ch;
            if (c == 0xFFFD) { f.droppedUnsupported = true; continue; }
            if (c == U'\t') { if (tabKey) continue; }
            else if (c == U'\r' || c == U'\n') { if (enterKey) continue; c = U'\n'; }
            else if (c < 0x20 || c == 0x7F) continue;
            TextInputEvent out = e;
            out.ch = c;
            f.events.push_back(out);
        }
        return f;
    }

    RawTextInput ReadImGuiTextInput(bool layoutHasAltGr, std::vector<TextInputEvent> commandModeEvents)
    {
        RawTextInput raw;
        raw.layoutHasAltGr = layoutHasAltGr;
        ImGuiContext& g = *ImGui::GetCurrentContext();
        ImGuiIO& io = g.IO;
        ImGuiReadCursor& cursor = CursorFor(g);

        // The unread events, in queue order: what this NewFrame processed (the
        // trail), then what ImGui's trickling left queued for a later frame.
        std::vector<const ImGuiInputEvent*> unread;
        for (const ImGuiInputEvent& e : g.InputEventsTrail)
            if (e.EventId > cursor.lastEventId)
                unread.push_back(&e);
        for (const ImGuiInputEvent& e : g.InputEventsQueue)
            if (e.EventId > cursor.lastEventId)
                unread.push_back(&e);

        // A gap (the view did not read for a while, or a fresh cursor): the
        // carried modifiers are stale, so derive them again.
        if (!unread.empty() && unread.front()->EventId != cursor.lastEventId + 1)
        {
            cursor.ctrl = StateBefore(g, unread, ImGuiMod_Ctrl);
            cursor.shift = StateBefore(g, unread, ImGuiMod_Shift);
            cursor.alt = StateBefore(g, unread, ImGuiMod_Alt);
            cursor.rightAlt = StateBefore(g, unread, ImGuiKey_RightAlt);
        }

        const bool commandFrame = !commandModeEvents.empty();
        bool rightAltSeen = cursor.rightAlt;
        for (const ImGuiInputEvent* e : unread)
        {
            cursor.lastEventId = e->EventId;
            if (e->Type == ImGuiInputEventType_Key)
            {
                const ImGuiKey k = e->Key.Key;
                if (k == ImGuiMod_Ctrl)       { cursor.ctrl = e->Key.Down; continue; }
                if (k == ImGuiMod_Shift)      { cursor.shift = e->Key.Down; continue; }
                if (k == ImGuiMod_Alt)        { cursor.alt = e->Key.Down; continue; }
                if (k == ImGuiKey_RightAlt)   { cursor.rightAlt = e->Key.Down; rightAltSeen = rightAltSeen || e->Key.Down; continue; }
                if (!e->Key.Down || commandFrame)
                    continue;
                if (const std::optional<TextNamedKey> named = Named(k))
                {
                    TextInputEvent ev;
                    ev.seq = NextTextInputSeq();
                    ev.kind = TextInputEventKind::Key;
                    ev.key = TextKeyPress{ *named, cursor.ctrl, cursor.shift, cursor.alt };
                    raw.events.push_back(ev);
                }
                else if (cursor.ctrl || cursor.alt)   // rev-2 A12: a chord, at its place in the queue
                    if (const std::optional<char32_t> key = ChordKeyChar(k))
                        raw.events.push_back(ChordEvent(*key, cursor.ctrl, cursor.shift, cursor.alt));
            }
            else if (e->Type == ImGuiInputEventType_Text && !commandFrame)
            {
                TextInputEvent ev;
                ev.seq = NextTextInputSeq();
                ev.kind = TextInputEventKind::Char;
                ev.ch = static_cast<char32_t>(e->Text.Char);
                raw.events.push_back(ev);
            }
        }

        if (commandFrame)
            raw.events = std::move(commandModeEvents);   // the hook owns the stream; ImGui's copies are dropped
        else
            // Typematic repeats: ImGui filters repeated OS downs as duplicates, so a
            // held key repeats only through ImGui's own KeyRepeatDelay/Rate. The press
            // itself (DownDuration == 0) came from the queue above.
        {
            for (const KeyMap& m : kKeyMap)
                if (ImGui::GetKeyData(&g, m.imgui)->DownDuration > 0.0f && ImGui::IsKeyPressed(m.imgui, true))
                {
                    TextInputEvent ev;
                    ev.seq = NextTextInputSeq();
                    ev.kind = TextInputEventKind::Key;
                    ev.key = TextKeyPress{ m.named, io.KeyCtrl, io.KeyShift, io.KeyAlt };
                    raw.events.push_back(ev);
                }
            if (io.KeyCtrl || io.KeyAlt)   // a held chord repeats too (vim's Ctrl-D, Ctrl-E ...)
                ForEachChordKey([&](ImGuiKey key)
                {
                    if (ImGui::GetKeyData(&g, key)->DownDuration > 0.0f && ImGui::IsKeyPressed(key, true))
                        raw.events.push_back(ChordEvent(*ChordKeyChar(key), io.KeyCtrl, io.KeyShift, io.KeyAlt));
                });
        }

        io.InputQueueCharacters.resize(0);
        raw.rightAltDown = rightAltSeen || ImGui::IsKeyDown(ImGuiKey_RightAlt);
        return raw;
    }
}

```cpp
#pragma once

// The text editor's hook on SDL's Windows message hook (spec s5.5, D-R1),
// chained through Arcane::AddWindowsMessageHook (TE2-8). Its jobs:
//  - COMMAND MODE (vim Normal / Visual / operator-pending -- TE5a-22 sets it):
//    the hook owns the keyboard stream. It records named keys and Ctrl/Alt
//    chords (WM_KEYDOWN / WM_SYSKEYDOWN; a chord as TextNamedKey::Chord, rev-2
//    A12) and characters (WM_CHAR) in message order, stamped from
//    NextTextInputSeq(); WM_DEADCHAR becomes the bare symbol, the layout's
//    dead-key state is consumed and the message swallowed, so `"a` on
//    US-International selects register a instead of composing a-umlaut. In the
//    text-entry modes it records nothing and composition works normally.
//  - The LAYOUT and the IME are POLLED by PollFrame, never learnt from
//    messages: WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE and WM_SETFOCUS are SENT to the window
//    procedure and never pass SDL's hook (finding 2.1).
//  - The IME-allowed flag TE5a-22 sets (spec s5.1, s5.5). Disallowing TRULY
//    disables the IME: the focused window's input context is taken away
//    (ImmAssociateContextEx(hwnd, nullptr, 0)), at once and again by every
//    PollFrame (SDL3's SDL_StartTextInput re-associates it from
//    Platform_SetImeDataFn), so a Japanese/Chinese IME never turns vim Normal
//    mode's `j` into a composition; allowing restores the default context
//    (IACE_DEFAULT). The view additionally maps the flag to WantVisible.

#include "TextEditor/View/TextInput.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextKeyboardLayout.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    class TextInputHook
    {
    public:
        static TextInputHook& Get();   // the editor's instance (EditorApp installs it at boot)

        void Install();                // registers the chained hook + queries the active layout; idempotent
        void Uninstall();
        [[nodiscard]] bool Installed() const noexcept { return m_installed; }

        void SetCommandMode(bool on) noexcept { m_commandMode = on; }
        [[nodiscard]] bool CommandMode() const noexcept { return m_commandMode; }
        // On a state change: false takes the focused window's IME context away at
        // once (PollFrame keeps it away); true gives the default context back.
        void SetImeAllowed(bool allowed);
        [[nodiscard]] bool ImeAllowed() const noexcept { return m_imeAllowed; }

        [[nodiscard]] const KeyboardLayoutFacts& Layout() const noexcept { return m_layout; }
        void RefreshLayout(std::uintptr_t layout);

        // Once per frame, after ImGui's Platform_SetImeDataFn ran (EditorApp, right
        // before the pump) and at the start of the view's input step: re-reads
        // GetKeyboardLayout(0) (RefreshLayout on a change) and, while the IME is
        // disallowed, takes the context away from `hwnd` -- or GetFocus(), or the
        // window of the last posted key message, when `hwnd` is null.
        void PollFrame(void* hwnd);

        // The command-mode events recorded since the last take, in message order.
        [[nodiscard]] std::vector<TextInputEvent> TakeCommandModeEvents();
        // Drops what no text view took (EditorApp, before each pump): keystrokes
        // typed while no text view owned the keyboard never replay later.
        void DiscardUntakenEvents();

        // The hook body. `msg` is a MSG*; false swallows it. Public for tests.
        bool OnMessage(void* msg);

    private:
        static bool Thunk(void* user, void* msg);
        void Record(TextInputEvent event);
        void RecordUtf16(char16_t unit);
        void TakeImeFrom(void* hwnd);
        [[nodiscard]] void* FocusedWindow() const;

        KeyboardLayoutFacts         m_layout;
        std::vector<TextInputEvent> m_events;
        void*                       m_imeWindow = nullptr;       // the window whose context we took away
        void*                       m_lastKeyWindow = nullptr;   // hwnd of the last posted WM_KEYDOWN / WM_SYSKEYDOWN
        char16_t                    m_highSurrogate = 0;
        bool                        m_installed = false;
        bool                        m_commandMode = false;
        bool                        m_imeAllowed = true;
    };
}
```

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/TextInputHook.cpp`:
```cpp
#include "TextEditor/View/TextInputHook.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Platform/WindowsMessageHooks.hpp>

#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#ifndef NOMINMAX
#define NOMINMAX
#endif
#include <windows.h>
#include <imm.h>
#pragma comment(lib, "imm32.lib")   // ImmGetContext / ImmReleaseContext / ImmAssociateContextEx

#include <optional>
#include <utility>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    namespace
    {
        bool WindowHasInputContext(HWND hwnd)
        {
            const HIMC himc = ::ImmGetContext(hwnd);
            if (!himc)
                return false;
            ::ImmReleaseContext(hwnd, himc);
            return true;
        }

        // ImmAssociateContextEx(hwnd, nullptr, 0) leaves the window with NO input
        // context: the IME cannot compose there at all. IACE_DEFAULT gives the
        // window's default context back.
        void AssociateIme(void* window, bool allowed)
        {
            const HWND hwnd = static_cast<HWND>(window);
            if (!hwnd || !::IsWindow(hwnd))
                return;
            ::ImmAssociateContextEx(hwnd, nullptr, allowed ? IACE_DEFAULT : 0);
        }

        // ToUnicodeEx WITHOUT the keep-state flag on Space consumes a pending
        // dead key (it returns the spacing accent), so the next keystroke is
        // translated on its own.
        void ConsumeDeadKeyState(std::uintptr_t layout)
        {
            const HKL hkl = reinterpret_cast<HKL>(layout);
            const BYTE state[256] = {};
            wchar_t buf[8] = {};
            const UINT scan = ::MapVirtualKeyExW(VK_SPACE, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC, hkl);
            (void)::ToUnicodeEx(VK_SPACE, scan, state, buf, 8, 0, hkl);
        }

        std::optional<TextNamedKey> NamedKeyForVirtualKey(WPARAM vk)
        {
            switch (vk)
            {
            case VK_LEFT:   return TextNamedKey::Left;
            case VK_RIGHT:  return TextNamedKey::Right;
            case VK_UP:     return TextNamedKey::Up;
            case VK_DOWN:   return TextNamedKey::Down;
            case VK_HOME:   return TextNamedKey::Home;
            case VK_END:    return TextNamedKey::End;
            case VK_PRIOR:  return TextNamedKey::PageUp;
            case VK_NEXT:   return TextNamedKey::PageDown;
            case VK_BACK:   return TextNamedKey::Backspace;
            case VK_DELETE: return TextNamedKey::Delete;
            case VK_RETURN: return TextNamedKey::Enter;
            case VK_TAB:    return TextNamedKey::Tab;
            case VK_ESCAPE: return TextNamedKey::Escape;
            case VK_INSERT: return TextNamedKey::Insert;
            default:        return std::nullopt;
            }
        }
    }

    TextInputHook& TextInputHook::Get()
    {
        static TextInputHook hook;
        return hook;
    }

    void TextInputHook::Install()
    {
        if (m_installed)
            return;
        RefreshLayout(ActiveKeyboardLayout());
        Arcane::AddWindowsMessageHook(&TextInputHook::Thunk, this);
        m_installed = true;
    }

    void TextInputHook::Uninstall()
    {
        if (!m_installed)
            return;
        Arcane::RemoveWindowsMessageHook(&TextInputHook::Thunk, this);
        m_installed = false;
    }

    void TextInputHook::RefreshLayout(std::uintptr_t layout)
    {
        m_layout = QueryKeyboardLayoutFacts(layout);
    }

    std::vector<TextInputEvent> TextInputHook::TakeCommandModeEvents()
    {
        return std::exchange(m_events, std::vector<TextInputEvent>{});
    }

    void TextInputHook::DiscardUntakenEvents()
    {
        m_events.clear();
        m_highSurrogate = 0;
    }

    void* TextInputHook::FocusedWindow() const
    {
        if (const HWND focus = ::GetFocus())
            return focus;
        return m_lastKeyWindow;
    }

    void TextInputHook::TakeImeFrom(void* window)
    {
        if (!window)
            return;
        if (window != m_imeWindow)
        {
            AssociateIme(m_imeWindow, true);   // focus moved: the window we left gets its IME back
            m_imeWindow = window;
        }
        if (WindowHasInputContext(static_cast<HWND>(window)))
            AssociateIme(window, false);       // first time, or SDL_StartTextInput gave it back
    }

    void TextInputHook::SetImeAllowed(bool allowed)
    {
        if (allowed == m_imeAllowed)
            return;   // only a state change touches the input context here
        m_imeAllowed = allowed;
        if (allowed)
        {
            AssociateIme(m_imeWindow, true);
            m_imeWindow = nullptr;
        }
        else
            TakeImeFrom(FocusedWindow());   // at once: TE5a-22 calls this before the next key
    }

    void TextInputHook::PollFrame(void* hwnd)
    {
        const std::uintptr_t active = ActiveKeyboardLayout();
        if (active != m_layout.layout)
            RefreshLayout(active);         // WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE is sent, never seen: poll (finding 2.1)
        if (!m_imeAllowed)
            TakeImeFrom(hwnd ? hwnd : FocusedWindow());   // undo SDL's re-association every frame (finding 2.2)
    }

    void TextInputHook::Record(TextInputEvent event)
    {
        event.seq = NextTextInputSeq();
        event.fromCommandHook = true;
        m_events.push_back(event);
    }

    void TextInputHook::RecordUtf16(char16_t unit)
    {
        TextInputEvent e;
        e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Char;
        if (unit >= 0xD800 && unit <= 0xDBFF)
        {
            m_highSurrogate = unit;   // waits for its low half
            return;
        }
        if (unit >= 0xDC00 && unit <= 0xDFFF)
        {
            e.ch = m_highSurrogate != 0
                ? 0x10000 + ((static_cast<char32_t>(m_highSurrogate) - 0xD800) << 10) + (static_cast<char32_t>(unit) - 0xDC00)
                : char32_t{ 0xFFFD };   // a lone low half
            m_highSurrogate = 0;
            Record(e);
            return;
        }
        m_highSurrogate = 0;
        e.ch = unit;
        Record(e);
    }

    bool TextInputHook::Thunk(void* user, void* msg)
    {
        return static_cast<TextInputHook*>(user)->OnMessage(msg);
    }

    bool TextInputHook::OnMessage(void* msgPtr)
    {
        const MSG& msg = *static_cast<const MSG*>(msgPtr);
        switch (msg.message)
        {
        case WM_KEYDOWN:
        case WM_SYSKEYDOWN:
            if (msg.hwnd)
                m_lastKeyWindow = msg.hwnd;
            if (m_commandMode)
            {
                // GetKeyState answers as of the message just retrieved.
                const bool ctrl = ::GetKeyState(VK_CONTROL) < 0;
                const bool shift = ::GetKeyState(VK_SHIFT) < 0;
                const bool alt = ::GetKeyState(VK_MENU) < 0;
                if (const std::optional<TextNamedKey> named = NamedKeyForVirtualKey(msg.wParam))
                {
                    TextInputEvent e;
                    e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Key;
                    e.key = TextKeyPress{ *named, ctrl, shift, alt };
                    Record(e);
                }
                else if ((ctrl || alt) && !(m_layout.hasAltGr && ::GetKeyState(VK_RMENU) < 0))   // AltGr is text, never a chord
                    if (const std::optional<char32_t> key = ChordKeyCharForVirtualKey(static_cast<std::uintptr_t>(msg.wParam)))
                    {
                        TextInputEvent e;   // rev-2 A12: the chord at its place in the stream
                        e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Key;
                        e.key = TextKeyPress{ TextNamedKey::Chord, ctrl, shift, alt, *key };
                        Record(e);
                    }
            }
            return true;   // SDL still updates its key state and the chords
        case WM_CHAR:
            if (m_commandMode)
                RecordUtf16(static_cast<char16_t>(msg.wParam));
            return true;
        case WM_DEADCHAR:
            if (!m_commandMode)
                return true;   // text-entry modes: composition is left alone
            {
                TextInputEvent e;
                e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Char;
                e.ch = static_cast<char32_t>(msg.wParam);
                Record(e);
            }
            ConsumeDeadKeyState(m_layout.layout != 0 ? m_layout.layout : ActiveKeyboardLayout());
            return false;   // swallowed: nothing composes with the next key
        default:
            return true;
        }
    }
}

TE4-12 adds `folds`, `editing`, `followForeignEdits`, `markerGeneration` and replaces `SyncDisplay`'s body with `Text::SyncDisplay(folds, display, buffer.Text())`; TE4-18 adds `indent`); `Text::EditContext DefaultEditContext(TextModel&)` (calls `model.SyncDisplay()`, fills the context from `Settings<TextSettings>()` through `ApplyEditSettings`, points `display` at `model.display`; TE4-18 adds `model.indent`); `class GlyphAdvances { virtual float Advance(char32_t) const; virtual float HexBoxAdvance() const; virtual float SpaceAdvance() const; }`; `enum class ClusterKind { Text, Tab, HexBox }`; `struct LayoutCluster { std::uint32_t byte, length; float x, width; ClusterKind kind; }`; `struct LineLayout { std::vector<Checkpoint> checkpoints; std::uint32_t bytes; float width; }`; `kLayoutCheckpointStride` (64); `void WalkClusters(...)`; `LineLayout BuildLineLayout(std::string_view, const GlyphAdvances&, std::uint32_t tabSize)`; `class LineCursor { float XForColumn(std::uint32_t); std::uint32_t ColumnForX(float); void ForEachVisible(float x0, float x1, fn); }`; `class LineLayoutCache { void Sync(const Text::TextBuffer&, std::uint64_t glyphGeneration, std::uint32_t tabSize); const LineLayout& Get(const Text::Rope&, std::uint32_t row, const GlyphAdvances&); void Clear(); }`; `float GutterWidth(std::uint32_t lineCount, float digitAdvance, TextLineNumbers)`; `std::optional<std::uint32_t> GutterNumber(std::uint32_t row, std::uint32_t cursorRow, TextLineNumbers)`; `struct RowRange { std::uint32_t first, last; }`; `RowRange VisibleDisplayRows(float scrollY, float viewHeight, float lineHeight, std::uint32_t displayRowCount)`. TE4's split view and soft-wrap layer reuse `LineCursor`.

Every command runs through TE1's `Text::TextCommands` class constructed over the model: `Text::TextCommands cmds(model.buffer, model.selections, DefaultEditContext(model));` (CANON A3: there is no `TextCommandContext` and no free-function `TextCommands` namespace).

Design: a line's layout stores only a checkpoint `{byte, x}` every `kLayoutCheckpointStride` clusters. `XForColumn` / `ColumnForX` binary-search the checkpoints and walk at most one stride of clusters, copying just that window out of the rope; drawing walks only the windows that intersect the visible x range. A line's layout is built once (one walk) and survives edits to other rows: `Sync` replays the buffer's edit log, dropping touched rows and shifting the rest by `rowDelta`.

`ArcaneTests/src/Text/TextLayoutTest.cpp`:
```cpp
// Text editor TE2-11 (spec s5.1, s3.5): cluster widths (tabs to the next stop,
// invalid bytes and control characters as hex boxes, combining marks inside
// their cluster), the x-prefix checkpoints, column <-> x through them, and the
// cache surviving edits to other rows.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
#include <rapidcheck.h>
#include <rapidcheck/catch.h>

#include "TextEditor/TextSettings.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextLayout.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextModel.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Config/Settings.hpp>

#include <string>
#include <vector>

using namespace Arcane::Editor;
using Arcane::Text::Rope;

namespace
{
    // 10 px per code point, CJK 20, combining marks 0; hex box 24; space 10.
    struct FixedGlyphs final : GlyphAdvances
    {
        float Advance(char32_t cp) const override
        {
            if (cp >= 0x0300 && cp <= 0x036F) return 0.0f;
            if (cp >= 0x4E00 && cp <= 0x9FFF) return 20.0f;
            return 10.0f;
        }
        float HexBoxAdvance() const override { return 24.0f; }
        float SpaceAdvance() const override { return 10.0f; }
    };

    std::vector<LayoutCluster> Clusters(std::string_view line, std::uint32_t tab = 4)
    {
        std::vector<LayoutCluster> out;
        WalkClusters(line, 0, 0.0f, FixedGlyphs{}, tab, [&](const LayoutCluster& c) { out.push_back(c); return true; });
        return out;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("text layout: tabs stop on the grid, invalid bytes and controls are hex boxes, marks join their base", "[text-view]")
{
    const auto a = Clusters("ab\tc");
    REQUIRE(a.size() == 4u);
    CHECK(a[2].kind == ClusterKind::Tab);
    CHECK(a[2].x == 20.0f);
    CHECK(a[2].width == 20.0f);                 // 20 -> the next 40 px stop
    CHECK(a[3].x == 40.0f);
    CHECK(BuildLineLayout("ab\tc", FixedGlyphs{}, 4).width == 50.0f);
    CHECK(Clusters("\t")[0].width == 40.0f);    // a tab at a stop advances a full stop

    const auto b = Clusters("a\xE9" "b");       // an invalid byte: its own cluster, a hex box
    REQUIRE(b.size() == 3u);
    CHECK(b[1].kind == ClusterKind::HexBox);
    CHECK(b[1].length == 1u);
    CHECK(b[1].width == 24.0f);
    CHECK(b[2].x == 34.0f);

    CHECK(Clusters("\x01")[0].kind == ClusterKind::HexBox);   // a control character
    const auto c = Clusters("e\xCC\x81x");      // e + U+0301 combining acute: one cluster
    REQUIRE(c.size() == 2u);
    CHECK(c[0].length == 3u);
    CHECK(c[0].width == 10.0f);
    CHECK(Clusters("\xE4\xB8\xAD")[0].width == 20.0f);       // a wide CJK glyph
}

TEST_CASE("text layout: checkpoints every stride; column <-> x through them", "[text-view]")
{
    const std::string longLine(1000, 'x');
    const LineLayout L = BuildLineLayout(longLine, FixedGlyphs{}, 4);
    CHECK(L.bytes == 1000u);
    CHECK(L.width == 10000.0f);
    CHECK(L.checkpoints.size() == 16u);         // clusters 0, 64, ..., 960
    CHECK(L.checkpoints[3].byte == 3u * kLayoutCheckpointStride);
    CHECK(L.checkpoints[3].x == 10.0f * 3u * kLayoutCheckpointStride);

    const Rope rope = Rope::FromUtf8("first\n" + longLine + "\nlast");
    const FixedGlyphs g;
    LineCursor cur(rope, 1, L, g, 4);
    CHECK(cur.XForColumn(130) == 1300.0f);
    CHECK(cur.XForColumn(5000) == 10000.0f);     // past the end: the line's width
    CHECK(cur.ColumnForX(1304.0f) == 130u);      // nearer the left edge of cluster 130
    CHECK(cur.ColumnForX(1306.0f) == 131u);      // nearer its right edge
    CHECK(cur.ColumnForX(-5.0f) == 0u);
    CHECK(cur.ColumnForX(99999.0f) == 1000u);
    std::vector<std::uint32_t> seen;
    cur.ForEachVisible(2000.0f, 2100.0f, [&](const LayoutCluster& c, std::string_view bytes)
    {
        seen.push_back(c.byte);
        CHECK(bytes == "x");
    });
    REQUIRE(seen.size() == 10u);
    CHECK(seen.front() == 200u);
    CHECK(seen.back() == 209u);
}

TEST_CASE("text layout: ColumnForX inverts XForColumn at every cluster boundary (property)", "[text-view]")
{
    rc::prop("round trip", [] {
        const std::vector<int> picks = *rc::gen::container<std::vector<int>>(rc::gen::inRange(0, 6));
        std::string line;
        for (const int p : picks)
            line += p == 0 ? "a" : p == 1 ? "\t" : p == 2 ? "\xC3\xA9" : p == 3 ? "\xE9" : p == 4 ? "\xE4\xB8\xAD" : "e\xCC\x81";
        const FixedGlyphs g;
        const LineLayout L = BuildLineLayout(line, g, 4);
        const Rope rope = Rope::FromUtf8(line);
        LineCursor cur(rope, 0, L, g, 4);
        float lastX = -1.0f;
        WalkClusters(line, 0, 0.0f, g, 4, [&](const LayoutCluster& c)
        {
            RC_ASSERT(cur.XForColumn(c.byte) == c.x);
            RC_ASSERT(cur.ColumnForX(c.x + 0.25f) == c.byte);
            RC_ASSERT(c.x > lastX);
            lastX = c.x;
            return true;
        });
        RC_ASSERT(cur.XForColumn(L.bytes) == L.width);
    });
}

TEST_CASE("text layout: the cache keeps rows an edit did not touch and shifts the rows below it", "[text-view]")
{
    TextModel model(Rope::FromUtf8("aaaa\nbbbb\ncccc\ndddd"));
    const FixedGlyphs g;
    LineLayoutCache cache;
    cache.Sync(model.buffer, 1, 4);
    const Rope& before = model.buffer.Text();
    for (std::uint32_t row = 0; row < 4; ++row) (void)cache.Get(before, row, g);
    CHECK(cache.Size() == 4u);

    // Insert a new line inside row 1: row 1 is touched, rows 2..3 move down by one.
    {
        Arcane::Text::TextCommands cmds(model.buffer, model.selections, DefaultEditContext(model));
        cmds.SetSelections({ Arcane::Text::Selection{ 0, 7, 7, std::nullopt } });
        cmds.InsertText("X\nY");
    }
    cache.Sync(model.buffer, 1, 4);
    CHECK(cache.Size() == 3u);                   // rows 0, 3, 4 (old 0, 2, 3)
    const Rope& after = model.buffer.Text();
    CHECK(cache.Get(after, 4, g).width == 40.0f);   // old row 3, kept and shifted
    cache.Sync(model.buffer, 2, 4);              // a font change
    CHECK(cache.Size() == 0u);
}

TEST_CASE("text model: owns a buffer built from text and line endings; the display map is synced at once", "[text-view]")
{
    TextModel model(Rope::FromUtf8("a\nb\nc"), Arcane::Text::EolMap(Arcane::Text::Eol::CRLF));
    REQUIRE(model.owned != nullptr);
    CHECK(&model.buffer == model.owned.get());
    CHECK(model.buffer.Eols().Dominant() == Arcane::Text::Eol::CRLF);
    CHECK_FALSE(model.buffer.Dirty());
    CHECK(model.display.DisplayRowCount() == 3u);    // the constructor ran SyncDisplay

    const Arcane::Text::EditContext ctx = DefaultEditContext(model);
    CHECK(ctx.display == &model.display);
    CHECK(ctx.tabSize == Arcane::Settings<TextSettings>().tabSize);
    CHECK(ctx.insertSpaces == Arcane::Settings<TextSettings>().insertSpaces);

    TextModel lf(Rope::FromUtf8("x"));                 // the default EolMap: LF
    CHECK(lf.buffer.Eols().Dominant() == Arcane::Text::Eol::LF);
}

TEST_CASE("text model: two models over one buffer see each other's edits and keep their own selections", "[text-view]")
{
    TextModel first(Rope::FromUtf8("one\ntwo"));
    TextModel second(first.buffer);
    CHECK(second.owned == nullptr);
    CHECK(&second.buffer == &first.buffer);

    {
        Arcane::Text::TextCommands cmds(first.buffer, first.selections, DefaultEditContext(first));
        cmds.SetSelections({ Arcane::Text::Selection{ 0, 3, 3, std::nullopt } });
        cmds.InsertText("!");
    }
    CHECK(second.buffer.Text().ToString() == "one!\ntwo");
    CHECK(second.selections.Primary().head == 0u);    // its own cursor, untouched

    {
        Arcane::Text::TextCommands cmds(second.buffer, second.selections, DefaultEditContext(second));
        cmds.MoveDocumentEnd(false);
        cmds.InsertText("\nthree");
    }
    CHECK(first.buffer.Text().ToString() == "one!\ntwo\nthree");
    CHECK(first.selections.Primary().head == 4u);
    first.SyncDisplay();                               // the version moved: the row count follows
    CHECK(first.display.DisplayRowCount() == 3u);
}

TEST_CASE("text layout: gutter width, gutter numbers and the visible row window", "[text-view]")
{
    CHECK(GutterWidth(10, 8.0f, TextLineNumbers::Absolute) == 40.0f);      // 3 digits minimum + 2 padding
    CHECK(GutterWidth(123456, 8.0f, TextLineNumbers::Relative) == 64.0f);  // 6 digits + 2
    CHECK(GutterWidth(10, 8.0f, TextLineNumbers::Off) == 8.0f);
    CHECK(GutterNumber(4, 9, TextLineNumbers::Absolute) == 5u);
    CHECK(GutterNumber(4, 9, TextLineNumbers::Relative) == 5u);
    CHECK(GutterNumber(9, 9, TextLineNumbers::Relative) == 0u);
    CHECK(GutterNumber(9, 9, TextLineNumbers::Hybrid) == 10u);
    CHECK(GutterNumber(12, 9, TextLineNumbers::Hybrid) == 3u);
    CHECK_FALSE(GutterNumber(4, 9, TextLineNumbers::Off).has_value());
    const RowRange r = VisibleDisplayRows(45.0f, 100.0f, 20.0f, 1000);
    CHECK(r.first == 2u);
    CHECK(r.last == 9u);                         // rows 2..7 visible, one row of margin
    CHECK(VisibleDisplayRows(0.0f, 100.0f, 20.0f, 3).last == 3u);
    CHECK(VisibleDisplayRows(0.0f, 100.0f, 0.0f, 3).last == 0u);
}

#pragma once

// The text a view shows and edits (text editor spec s2, s3): a buffer, this
// view's selections and the buffer-row <-> display-row map. TextDocument's
// primary model owns its buffer; a split view (TE4-17) builds a second model
// over the SAME buffer with the shared-buffer constructor, with its own
// SelectionSet + DisplayMap (CANON A7).

#include "TextEditor/Core/DisplayMap.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Core/EolMap.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Core/Rope.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Core/Selection.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Core/TextBuffer.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Core/TextCommands.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    struct TextModel
    {
        // A model that owns a new buffer over `text` (history empty, clean).
        explicit TextModel(Text::Rope text, Text::EolMap eols = {});
        // A model over a buffer someone else owns (a split view's second model).
        explicit TextModel(Text::TextBuffer& shared);
        TextModel(const TextModel&) = delete;
        TextModel& operator=(const TextModel&) = delete;

        std::unique_ptr<Text::TextBuffer> owned;   // declared BEFORE `buffer`; null when shared
        Text::TextBuffer&  buffer;
        Text::SelectionSet selections;
        Text::DisplayMap   display;

        // Rebuilds `display` when the buffer's version (TE4-12: or the fold
        // set) changed since the last call. Called at the start of
        // TextEditorView::Draw and by DefaultEditContext before every command.
        void SyncDisplay();

        // SyncDisplay's bookkeeping.
        std::uint64_t displaySyncedVersion = 0;
        bool          displaySynced = false;
    };

    // The EditContext every command over `model` takes: model.SyncDisplay(),
    // then today's editor.text.* editing settings (ApplyEditSettings) and the
    // model's display map. TE4-24's TextDocument::MakeEditContext builds on it.
    [[nodiscard]] Text::EditContext DefaultEditContext(TextModel& model);
}

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/TextModel.cpp`:
```cpp
#include "TextEditor/View/TextModel.hpp"

#include "TextEditor/TextSettings.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Config/Settings.hpp>

#include <utility>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    TextModel::TextModel(Text::Rope text, Text::EolMap eols)
        : owned(std::make_unique<Text::TextBuffer>(std::move(text), std::move(eols))), buffer(*owned)
    {
        SyncDisplay();
    }

    TextModel::TextModel(Text::TextBuffer& shared) : owned(), buffer(shared)
    {
        SyncDisplay();
    }

    void TextModel::SyncDisplay()
    {
        if (displaySynced && displaySyncedVersion == buffer.Version())
            return;
        display.SetFolds({}, buffer.Text().LineCount());   // no folds before TE4-12
        displaySyncedVersion = buffer.Version();
        displaySynced = true;
    }

    Text::EditContext DefaultEditContext(TextModel& model)
    {
        model.SyncDisplay();
        Text::EditContext ctx;
        ApplyEditSettings(Arcane::Settings<TextSettings>(), ctx);
        ctx.display = &model.display;
        return ctx;
    }
}
