`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/ScopeTest.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/ScopeTest.hpp"

#include "TextEditor/Syntax/StateTable.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Tokenizer.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    namespace
    {
        std::vector<std::string_view> SplitLines(std::string_view text)
        {
            std::vector<std::string_view> out;
            while (!text.empty())
            {
                const std::size_t nl = text.find('\n');
                std::string_view line = text.substr(0, nl);
                if (!line.empty() && line.back() == '\r') line.remove_suffix(1);
                out.push_back(line);
                if (nl == std::string_view::npos) break;
                text.remove_prefix(nl + 1);
            }
            return out;
        }

        bool Quoted(std::string_view& s, std::string_view key, std::string& value)
        {
            if (!s.starts_with(key)) return false;
            s.remove_prefix(key.size());
            const std::size_t q = s.find('"');
            if (q == std::string_view::npos) return false;
            value = std::string(s.substr(0, q));
            s.remove_prefix(q + 1);
            return true;
        }

        ScopeId ScopeAt(const LineTokens& t, std::uint32_t col)
        {
            const auto it = std::upper_bound(t.runs.begin(), t.runs.end(), col,
                                             [](std::uint32_t c, const TokenRun& r) { return c < r.byteStart; });
            return it == t.runs.begin() ? 0 : std::prev(it)->scope;
        }

        bool Matches(std::string_view expected, ScopeId actualId, const std::string& actual)
        {
            if (expected == "none") return actualId == 0;
            return actual == expected || (actual.size() > expected.size() && actual.starts_with(expected) && actual[expected.size()] == '.');
        }
    }

    std::string ScopeTestResult::Report() const
    {
        std::string out = "grammar \"" + grammar + "\": " + std::to_string(assertions) + " assertions";
        if (!error.empty()) out += "; error: " + error;
        for (const ScopeTestFailure& f : failures)
            out += "\n  sample line " + std::to_string(f.fileLine) + " (source line " + std::to_string(f.sourceLine) + ", col " +
                   std::to_string(f.column) + "): expected " + f.expected + ", got " + (f.actual.empty() ? "none" : f.actual) +
                   (f.note.empty() ? "" : " [" + f.note + "]");
        return out;
    }

    ScopeTestResult RunScopeTest(std::string_view fileText, const GrammarRegistry& registry, MatchScratch& scratch)
    {
        ScopeTestResult out;
        const std::vector<std::string_view> lines = SplitLines(fileText);
        std::string marker;
        {
            std::string_view head = lines.empty() ? std::string_view() : lines[0];
            if (!Quoted(head, "#! arcsyntax-test grammar=\"", out.grammar) || !Quoted(head, " marker=\"", marker) || marker.empty())
            {
                out.error = "line 1 must be: #! arcsyntax-test grammar=\"<name>\" marker=\"<marker>\"";
                return out;
            }
        }
        const GrammarSnapshot g = registry.Find(out.grammar);
        if (!g)
        {
            out.error = "grammar \"" + out.grammar + "\" is not loaded";
            return out;
        }
        StateTable states;
        Tokenizer tokenizer(*g, states, scratch);
        LineTokens tokens;
        std::string_view source;
        bool haveSource = false;
        std::uint32_t sourceLine = 0;
        StateId state = StateTable::kRoot;

        for (std::size_t i = 1; i < lines.size(); ++i)
        {
            const auto fileLine = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i + 1);
            const std::string_view l = lines[i];
            if (!l.starts_with(marker))
            {
                source = l;
                haveSource = true;
                sourceLine = fileLine;
                tokens = tokenizer.TokenizeLine(source, state);
                state = tokens.endState;
                continue;
            }
            std::string_view rest = l.substr(marker.size());
            const std::size_t spaces = rest.find_first_not_of(' ');
            const auto malformed = [&](std::string note) {
                out.failures.push_back({ fileLine, sourceLine, 0, "<assertion>", std::string(l), std::move(note) });
            };
            if (spaces == std::string_view::npos) { malformed("malformed"); continue; }
            rest.remove_prefix(spaces);
            std::uint32_t firstCol = 0, count = 0;
            if (rest.starts_with("<-"))
            {
                count = 1;
                rest.remove_prefix(2);
            }
            else
            {
                const std::size_t carets = rest.find_first_not_of('^');
                count = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(carets == std::string_view::npos ? rest.size() : carets);
                if (count == 0) { malformed("malformed"); continue; }
                firstCol = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(marker.size() + spaces);
                rest.remove_prefix(count);
            }
            if (rest.empty() || rest.front() != ' ') { malformed("malformed: a space must separate the marks from the scope"); continue; }
            rest.remove_prefix(rest.find_first_not_of(' ') == std::string_view::npos ? rest.size() : rest.find_first_not_of(' '));
            bool negate = false;
            if (rest.starts_with("- "))
            {
                negate = true;
                rest.remove_prefix(2);
                rest.remove_prefix(std::min(rest.size(), rest.find_first_not_of(' ')));
            }
            const std::size_t scopeEnd = rest.find(' ');
            const std::string expected(rest.substr(0, scopeEnd));
            if (expected.empty() || (scopeEnd != std::string_view::npos && rest.find_first_not_of(' ', scopeEnd) != std::string_view::npos))
            {
                malformed("malformed");
                continue;
            }
            if (!haveSource)
            {
                out.failures.push_back({ fileLine, 0, firstCol, expected, {}, "assertion before any source line" });
                continue;
            }
            for (std::uint32_t c = firstCol; c < firstCol + count; ++c)
            {
                ++out.assertions;
                if (c >= source.size())
                {
                    out.failures.push_back({ fileLine, sourceLine, c, expected, {}, "column past the end of the source line" });
                    continue;
                }
                const ScopeId id = ScopeAt(tokens, c);
                const std::string actual = registry.Scopes().Name(id);
                if (Matches(expected, id, actual) == negate)
                    out.failures.push_back({ fileLine, sourceLine, c, (negate ? "- " : "") + expected, actual, {} });
            }
        }
        if (out.assertions == 0 && out.error.empty()) out.error = "the sample has no assertions";
        return out;
    }
}
```

`ArcaneTests/src/Helpers/TextShippedGrammars.hpp`:

```cpp
#pragma once

// The repo's data/Syntaxes grammars, loaded once per test run, and the
// per-grammar checks every grammar task uses (spec s4.7, s11.2).

#include "Helpers/ConstantScan.hpp"   // RepoRoot()
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/GrammarRegistry.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/ScopeTest.hpp"

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <iterator>
#include <map>
#include <string>

namespace Arcane::Test
{
    struct ShippedGrammarSet
    {
        Arcane::Text::GrammarRegistry registry;
        std::map<std::string, std::vector<Arcane::Text::GrammarProblem>> problems;
        ShippedGrammarSet()
        {
            registry.SetProblemSink([this](std::string_view key, std::span<const Arcane::Text::GrammarProblem> rows) {
                if (rows.empty()) problems.erase(std::string(key));
                else problems[std::string(key)].assign(rows.begin(), rows.end());
            });
            registry.SetSearchDirs({ { RepoRoot() / "data" / "Syntaxes", Arcane::Text::GrammarOrigin::Engine } });
            registry.Reload();
        }
    };

    inline ShippedGrammarSet& ShippedGrammars()
    {
        static ShippedGrammarSet set;
        return set;
    }

    inline void RequireScopeTest(std::string_view sampleFile)
    {
        const std::filesystem::path path = RepoRoot() / "data" / "Syntaxes" / "tests" / std::string(sampleFile);
        std::ifstream in(path, std::ios::binary);
        INFO(path.generic_string());
        REQUIRE(in.good());
        const std::string text((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
        Arcane::Text::MatchScratch scratch{ Arcane::Text::RegexLimits{} };
        const Arcane::Text::ScopeTestResult r = Arcane::Text::RunScopeTest(text, ShippedGrammars().registry, scratch);
        INFO(r.Report());
        CHECK(r.Passed());
    }

    inline void RequireNoGrammarProblems(std::string_view grammarFile)
    {
        const std::string key = "text.grammar:" + (RepoRoot() / "data" / "Syntaxes" / std::string(grammarFile)).generic_string();
        const auto& p = ShippedGrammars().problems;
        INFO(key);
        CHECK(ShippedGrammars().registry.Names().size() > 1u);   // the directory held at least one grammar
        if (const auto it = p.find(key); it != p.end())
            for (const auto& row : it->second)
            {
                INFO(row.rulePath + ": " + row.message);
                CHECK(false);
            }
    }
}
```

### Task TE3-21: JSON grammar and the Arcane JSON assets (spec s4.1, s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/JSON.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_json.json`
- Create: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammar `"JSON"` in the engine search directory

The spec's s4.1 example, completed: the key rule is a single-line `match` with a lookahead, listed **before** the string region so it wins the tie at the same position (s4.1, "context-dependent scopes use ordinary rules"). Arcane's JSON assets are listed by extension: `.arcmat .arcproj .arcscene .arctheme .arcsyntax .arcmesh .arcsprite .arcinput .arcdiag .arcplugin .meta` (every JSON-backed extension in the engine and ReferenceProject; `.arcart` is a binary artifact and is not listed). `//` and `/* */` comments are accepted (JSONC), which is also what lets the sample carry `//` assertion lines; an escape inside a string is coloured by a nested rule, an invalid escape is `invalid.illegal`. `firstLine` claims a line only when its first bracket opens a JSON value: `{` followed by a quote, `}` or the line end; `[` followed by a bracket, a quote, a number or literal that is followed by `,` or `]`, or the line end. A bare `^\s*[\[{]` would claim Arcane log headers (`[2026-10-06 ...]`) and INI sections, and JSON's firstLine is tried before the Arcane Log grammar's because `JSON.arcsyntax` sorts after `ArcaneLog.arcsyntax` (plan rev 2 finding 3.8).

### Task TE3-22: Plain Text and INI/cfg (line-local) grammars (spec s4.1, s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/PlainText.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/INI.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_plaintext.txt`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_ini.ini`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammars `"Plain Text"`, `"INI"` in the engine search directory

`PlainText.arcsyntax` is the data-file form of the built-in fallback (TE3-8's `MakePlainTextGrammar`; a valid file replaces it, TE3-12): line-local, no rules, `.txt`/`.text`. INI is **line-local** (s4.1): every line starts at the root and a quote left open at the end of a line is force-closed there -- the sample's `title = "Arcane \"Editor\"` line leaves its string open and the next line's key still colours as a key. Comments are `;` or `#` at line start, or after whitespace; sections, `key = value` / `key: value`, quoted strings, booleans (`true/false/yes/no/on/off`, any case) and numbers.

### Task TE3-23: Arcane log grammar (line-local; Console level colours) (spec s4.1, s4.4, s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/ArcaneLog.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_arcanelog.log`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammar `"Arcane Log"` in the engine search directory

The line format is the engine logger's (`ArcaneCore/src/Arcane/Base/Log.cpp:236`, `Util/LogServerSettingsData.hpp:25-26`): file sinks write `[%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%e] [%n] [%l] %v` (e.g. `[2026-10-06 03:34:40.538] [Arcane] [warning] ...`), the console pattern `[%H:%M:%S.%e] [%n] [%l] %v`; spdlog's `%l` names are `trace debug info warning error critical`; messages often start with `[tag]` (`[nri]`, `[nri-graph]`, `[foreign-module]`). Scopes: `constant.other.timestamp.log`, `entity.name.logger.log`, `markup.log.level.<level>.log` on the `[level]` token and `markup.log.message.<level>.log` on the rest of the line (a region from the level to the end of the line -- line-local force-close keeps it to that line), `entity.name.tag.log` on message tags. The Dark/Light/built-in syntax colours (TE3-6) map warning/error/critical to the palette's `warning`/`error` tokens -- the colours the Console uses (`Panels/EditorPanels.cpp:1269-1270`). Lines without the header (stack frames, continuation lines) are plain. Line-local, so a 400 MB log stays coloured at any scroll position (s4.4).

Written fresh (lite-xl ships no HLSL). Covers line/block comments, `#include` (path scoped as a string), the other preprocessor directives, strings, attributes (`[numthreads(...)]`, `[unroll]`, ...), `SV_*` and classic semantics, vector/matrix types (`float4x4`, `min16float3`, ...), numbers with HLSL suffixes, function calls (`name(` -- with intrinsics, control keywords and types picked out by the rule's keyword table), identifiers (storage modifiers, types incl. textures/buffers/samplers, constants) and operators. `foldMarkers` are `#pragma region` / `#pragma endregion` (TE3-19). Files: `.hlsl .hlsli .fx .fxh .usf .ush` (Arcane's shaders are `.hlsl`/`.hlsli`, `data/shaders/`).

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Grammar HLSL: loads clean, passes its scope test, marks #pragma region folds", "[text-grammar-hlsl][text-syntax-data]")
{
    RequireNoGrammarProblems("HLSL.arcsyntax");
    RequireScopeTest("syntax_test_hlsl.hlsl");
    auto& reg = ShippedGrammars().registry;
    for (const char* f : { "a.hlsl", "b.hlsli", "c.fx" }) CHECK(reg.Detect(f, "", {})->Name() == "HLSL");
    REQUIRE(reg.Find("HLSL") != nullptr);
    REQUIRE(reg.Find("HLSL")->Rules().FoldBegin() != nullptr);
    Arcane::Text::StateTable states;
    Arcane::Text::MatchScratch scratch{ Arcane::Text::RegexLimits{} };
    Arcane::Text::Tokenizer t(*reg.Find("HLSL"), states, scratch);
    CHECK(t.TokenizeLine("#pragma region Lighting", Arcane::Text::StateTable::kRoot).foldMarker == Arcane::Text::FoldMarker::Begin);
    CHECK(t.TokenizeLine("  #pragma endregion", Arcane::Text::StateTable::kRoot).foldMarker == Arcane::Text::FoldMarker::End);
}
```

### Task TE3-25: Lua grammar, ported from lite-xl (MIT) (spec s4.7, s10)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/Lua.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_lua.lua`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/NOTICE-lite-xl.txt` (lite-xl's `LICENSE`, verbatim)
- Modify: `NOTICE.md` (after the "Reimplemented (not vendored)" list: a "Ported grammar content" entry)
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammar `"Lua"` in the engine search directory

Translated from lite-xl's `data/plugins/language_lua.lua` (`D:\dev\_reference\lite-xl-master`, MIT; the spec's s4.7 instruction): lite-xl's Lua patterns become PCRE2 (`%a`->`[A-Za-z]`, `%w`->`[A-Za-z0-9]`, `%d`->`[0-9]`, the `%f[...]` frontier for call names -> a `(?=\s*[("'{])` lookahead, `{ start, end, escape }` triples -> `begin`/`end`/`escape` regions), and its `symbols` table becomes the identifier rules' `keywords` (split into control / logical-operator / storage / `self` / literal scopes instead of lite-xl's two "keyword" kinds). Additions over the original: long-bracket strings and comments with one and two `=` levels (`[=[ ]=]`, `--[==[ ]==]`; lite-xl only has level 0), escape colouring inside strings, `::label::`. Covers premake scripts (`.lua`). The attribution is in the file's `"notice"` field, the full MIT text in `data/Syntaxes/NOTICE-lite-xl.txt`, and a `NOTICE.md` entry.

### Task TE3-26: TOML and YAML grammars (spec s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/TOML.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/YAML.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_toml.toml`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_yaml.yaml`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammars `"TOML"`, `"YAML"` in the engine search directory

Both written fresh. TOML: comments, `[table]` / `[[array of tables]]` headers, bare/quoted/dotted keys (a key is whatever precedes `=`, by lookahead), the four string forms (basic and literal, single- and triple-quoted; triple-quoted ones span lines), escapes, offset date-times, numbers (hex/octal/binary, `_` separators, `inf`/`nan`), booleans. YAML: comments (`#` at line start or after whitespace), document markers, `%` directives, list dashes, keys (plain or quoted, before `: `; only where YAML puts a key -- at the line start after indentation and an optional list dash, or right after `{`/`,` in a flow mapping -- because an unanchored lazy key rule rescans a long value from every position, O(L^2) per line, and a long `description:` line would hit the regex limit and raise a spurious Problems row; plan rev 2 finding 3.10), anchors/aliases, tags, block-scalar indicators, double-quoted strings with escapes, single-quoted strings with `''`, the YAML 1.1 boolean/null spellings, numbers (not when glued to `:`/`/`, so `host:8080/x` stays plain). Known limit: a block scalar's content lines are not distinguished from plain text (it needs indentation tracking, which a pattern grammar cannot do); they draw as plain scalars.

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Grammar TOML and YAML: load clean and pass their scope tests", "[text-grammar-toml][text-syntax-data]")
{
    RequireNoGrammarProblems("TOML.arcsyntax");
    RequireNoGrammarProblems("YAML.arcsyntax");
    RequireScopeTest("syntax_test_toml.toml");
    RequireScopeTest("syntax_test_yaml.yaml");
    auto& reg = ShippedGrammars().registry;
    CHECK(reg.Detect("Cargo.toml", "", {})->Name() == "TOML");
    CHECK(reg.Detect("ci.yml", "", {})->Name() == "YAML");
    CHECK(reg.Detect("ci.yaml", "", {})->Name() == "YAML");
    CHECK(reg.Detect("spec.unknownext", "%YAML 1.2", {})->Name() == "YAML");

    // The key rules stay linear on long values (finding 3.10). An unanchored lazy key rule costs ~L^2/2 steps
    // on a 16 KiB prose value (~10^8) and hits a 1M match limit; the anchored ones cost a few steps per byte.
    std::string prose;
    while (prose.size() < 16384) prose += "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog with its friends. ";
    Arcane::Text::MatchScratch scratch{ Arcane::Text::RegexLimits{ 1000000, 0 } };
    Arcane::Text::StateTable states;
    Arcane::Text::Tokenizer t(*reg.Find("YAML"), states, scratch);
    for (const std::string& line : { "description: " + prose, "  - item: " + prose, "map: {a: 1, note: " + prose + ", b: 2}" })
    {
        const Arcane::Text::LineTokens tokens = t.TokenizeLine(line, Arcane::Text::StateTable::kRoot);
        CHECK_FALSE(tokens.runs.empty());
    }
    CHECK(scratch.LimitHits() == 0u);
}
```

```json
{
  "format": "arcsyntax",
  "version": 1,
  "name": "TOML",
  "scope": "source.toml",
  "files": [".toml"],
  "comment": { "line": "#" },
  "brackets": [["[", "]"], ["{", "}"]],
  "autoClose": [["\"", "\""], ["'", "'"], ["[", "]"], ["{", "}"]],
  "indent": { "increase": "[\\[{]\\s*$", "decrease": "^\\s*[\\]}]" },
  "wordChars": "A-Za-z0-9_-",
  "symbols": [ { "match": "^\\s*\\[\\[?\\s*([^\\]]+?)\\s*\\]\\]?", "name": 1, "kind": "table" } ],
  "lineLocal": false,
  "patterns": [
    { "match": "#.*$", "scope": "comment.line.number-sign.toml" },
    { "match": "^\\s*(\\[\\[?)([^\\]]*)(\\]\\]?)",
      "captures": { "1": "punctuation.definition.table.toml", "2": "entity.name.section.toml", "3": "punctuation.definition.table.toml" } },
    { "match": "(?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+|\"(?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*\"|'[^']*')(?:\\s*\\.\\s*(?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+|\"(?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*\"|'[^']*'))*(?=\\s*=)",
      "scope": "entity.name.key.toml" },
    { "begin": "\"\"\"", "end": "\"\"\"(?!\")", "escape": "\\\\.", "scope": "string.quoted.triple.basic.toml",
      "patterns": [ { "match": "\\\\(?:[btnfr\"\\\\]|u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}|U[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})", "scope": "constant.character.escape.toml" } ] },
    { "begin": "'''", "end": "'''(?!')", "scope": "string.quoted.triple.literal.toml" },
    { "begin": "\"", "end": "\"", "escape": "\\\\.", "scope": "string.quoted.double.basic.toml",
      "patterns": [ { "match": "\\\\(?:[btnfr\"\\\\]|u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}|U[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})", "scope": "constant.character.escape.toml" } ] },
    { "begin": "'", "end": "'", "scope": "string.quoted.single.literal.toml" },
    { "match": "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}(?:[Tt ]\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}(?:\\.\\d+)?(?:[Zz]|[+-]\\d{2}:\\d{2})?)?|\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}(?:\\.\\d+)?",
      "scope": "constant.other.datetime.toml" },
    { "match": "(?<![\\w.-])(?:true|false)(?![\\w.-])", "scope": "constant.language.boolean.toml" },
    { "match": "(?<![\\w.-])[+-]?(?:0x[0-9A-Fa-f_]+|0o[0-7_]+|0b[01_]+|inf|nan|[0-9][0-9_]*(?:\\.[0-9][0-9_]*)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9][0-9_]*)?)(?![\\w.-])",
      "scope": "constant.numeric.toml" },
    { "match": "=", "scope": "keyword.operator.assignment.toml" },

}
```

```json
    { "begin": "<\\?", "end": "\\?>", "scope": "meta.tag.preprocessor.xml",
```

### Task TE3-28: Batch, PowerShell and shell grammars (spec s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/Batch.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/PowerShell.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/Shell.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_batch.bat`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_powershell.ps1`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_shell.sh`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammars `"Batch"`, `"PowerShell"`, `"Shell"` in the engine search directory

All three written fresh. **Batch** is line-local (cmd parses line by line): `REM`/`::` comments, labels, `%var%`/`%%f`/`%~1`/`!delayed!` variables (also inside strings), control keywords and builtin commands (case-insensitive, via `(?i)` -- keyword tables are exact-match), `@`, redirection/pipe operators, numbers. **PowerShell** (stateful): `<# #>` block and `#` line comments, here-strings (`@"`...`"@`, `@'`...`'@`), double-quoted strings with backtick escapes and `$variable` interpolation, single-quoted strings with `''`, `$true/$false/$null`, variables (scoped `$env:X`, `${...}`), `-eq`-style operators, `Verb-Noun` cmdlets, `[type]` literals, `-Parameter` names, numbers with `KB/MB/...` suffixes, control keywords (case-insensitive). **Shell** (stateful): shebang, `#` comments (only at a word start), double-quoted strings with escapes and `$var`/`${...}` interpolation, single-quoted strings, `$(`/`$((`/backtick substitution openers, heredoc operators, control keywords, `local/export/...`, builtins, assignments (`NAME=`), operators, numbers. Known limit: a heredoc's body is not recognised (its terminator is a back-reference across lines, which `.arcsyntax` regions cannot express).

### Task TE3-29: Markdown grammar, ported from lite-xl (MIT), embedding the v1 languages in fenced code (spec s4.1, s4.7, s10)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/Markdown.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_markdown.md`
- Modify: `NOTICE.md` (the TE3-25 "Ported grammar content" entry gains Markdown)
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (two cases appended: the Markdown case, and the shipped-grammars wordChars contract -- rev-2 D-R12 / S4; TE7-16/17 add their `C` / `C++` rows to its `extraAscii` map)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12); `Regex::Compile` (TE3-2)
- Produces: the grammar `"Markdown"` in the engine search directory; the wordChars contract case (its `extraAscii` map is extended by TE7-16 with `{ "C", "" }` and TE7-17 with `{ "C++", "" }`)

Translated from lite-xl's `data/plugins/language_md.lua` (MIT): headings, thematic breaks (lite-xl colours them as comments; here `meta.separator`), bullets and numbered lists, block quotes, reference definitions, inline code (single and double backticks), bold/italic/bold-italic with `*` and `_` (underscore emphasis only at word boundaries, so `snake_case_name` stays plain), strikethrough, links and images, reference links, autolinks and bare URLs, inline HTML tags and entities, HTML comments, emoji shortcodes, `$$` math. lite-xl's fence list (40+ languages via `syntax = ".ext"`) becomes **`embed`** regions (s4.1) for the v1 grammars only -- `json/jsonc`, `hlsl`, `lua`, `xml/html/svg`, `yaml/yml`, `toml`, `ini/cfg`, `sh/bash/shell/zsh`, `powershell/ps1/pwsh`, `bat/batch/cmd`, `log` -- plus a generic fence drawn as `markup.raw.block`. The fence's `end` is an embed **boundary** (TE3-10): an unterminated string inside fenced JSON still ends at the closing fence. Single-line emphasis only (lite-xl's multi-line emphasis regions would colour the rest of a document after one stray `*`). Because it embeds every other grammar, this task is last; its test also asserts the whole shipped set loads with zero Problems rows.

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Grammar Markdown: loads clean, passes its scope test (with embedded JSON and Lua), resolves every embed", "[text-grammar-markdown][text-syntax-data]")
{
    RequireNoGrammarProblems("Markdown.arcsyntax");
    RequireScopeTest("syntax_test_markdown.md");
    auto& reg = ShippedGrammars().registry;
    CHECK(reg.Detect("README.md", "", {})->Name() == "Markdown");
    const auto md = reg.Find("Markdown");
    REQUIRE(md != nullptr);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < md->Embeds().size(); ++i)
    {
        INFO(md->Rules().EmbedNames()[i]);
        CHECK(md->Embeds()[i] != nullptr);   // every fence language is a shipped grammar
    }
    CHECK(md->Rules().Desc().notice.find("lite-xl") != std::string::npos);
}

TEST_CASE("Shipped grammars: the thirteen v1 languages load with no Problems rows", "[text-syntax-data]")
{
    auto& set = ShippedGrammars();
    CHECK(set.registry.Names() == std::vector<std::string>{ "Arcane Log", "Batch", "HLSL", "INI", "JSON", "Lua", "Markdown",
                                                            "Plain Text", "PowerShell", "Shell", "TOML", "XML", "YAML" });
    for (const auto& [key, rows] : set.problems)
        for (const auto& row : rows)
        {
            INFO(key + " " + row.rulePath + ": " + row.message);
            CHECK(false);
        }
}

TEST_CASE("Shipped grammars: wordChars is a plain ASCII class body; its extra ASCII is what vim's iskeyword adds", "[text-syntax-data]")
{
    // Plan rev 2 D-R12 / finding 4.2. Every consumer embeds or parses wordChars as a regex character-class BODY:
    // TE3-8 compiles "[" + wordChars + "]"; TE4-4's whole-word search compiles "(?:[" + wordChars + "]|[\p{L}\p{N}])"
    // (rev-2 4.2 / S4: valid whenever "[" + wordChars + "]" is, a leading or trailing '-' included);
    // TE4 (WordChars) and TE5 (VimCharClass) parse it into an ASCII bitset; the vim oracle (TE5a-7, O-4) sets
    // iskeyword=@,48-57,_,192-255 plus the grammar's extra ASCII word characters. So a shipped wordChars is
    // printable ASCII with no escape, no nested class and no negation; a '-' is either a range between two
    // alphanumerics or the last character (a literal); it covers A-Za-z0-9_; and its extra ASCII -- the
    // characters beyond letters, digits and '_' -- is exactly the iskeyword addition below.
    const std::map<std::string, std::string> extraAscii{
        { "Arcane Log", "" }, { "Batch", "" }, { "HLSL", "" }, { "INI", "-." },   // INI: iskeyword+=45,46
        { "JSON", "" }, { "Lua", "" }, { "Markdown", "" }, { "Plain Text", "" },
        { "PowerShell", "-" }, { "Shell", "" }, { "TOML", "-" }, { "XML", "-.:" }, { "YAML", "-" } };
    auto& reg = ShippedGrammars().registry;
    for (const std::string& name : reg.Names())
    {
        INFO(name);
        REQUIRE(extraAscii.contains(name));
        const std::string& w = reg.Find(name)->Rules().Desc().wordChars;
        REQUIRE_FALSE(w.empty());
        CHECK(w.front() != '^');
        std::bitset<128> ascii;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < w.size(); ++i)
        {
            const auto c = static_cast<unsigned char>(w[i]);
            REQUIRE(c >= 0x20u);
            REQUIRE(c < 0x7Fu);
            CHECK(c != '\\');
            CHECK(c != '[');
            CHECK(c != ']');
            if (c == '-' && i > 0 && i + 1 < w.size())   // a range: both ends alphanumeric, in order
            {
                const auto lo = static_cast<unsigned char>(w[i - 1]);
                const auto hi = static_cast<unsigned char>(w[i + 1]);
                REQUIRE(std::isalnum(lo));
                REQUIRE(std::isalnum(hi));
                REQUIRE(lo <= hi);
                for (unsigned v = lo; v <= hi; ++v) ascii.set(v);
                ++i;
                continue;
            }
            ascii.set(c);
        }
        for (unsigned v = 0; v < 128; ++v)
            if (std::isalnum(static_cast<int>(v)) || v == '_') CHECK(ascii.test(v));   // the @,48-57,_ base
        std::string extra;
        for (unsigned v = 0; v < 128; ++v)
            if (ascii.test(v) && !std::isalnum(static_cast<int>(v)) && v != '_') extra += static_cast<char>(v);
        CHECK(extra == extraAscii.at(name));
        // Both embeddings compile: TE3-8's class and TE4-4's TextSearch::WordClass form (rev-2 S4).
        CHECK(Arcane::Text::Regex::Compile("[" + w + "]").has_value());
        CHECK(Arcane::Text::Regex::Compile("(?:[" + w + "]|[\\p{L}\\p{N}])").has_value());
    }
}
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: everything above; `Arcane::Diagnostics::Publish`, `Arcane::Diagnostic`, `DiagLocator::File` (`ArcaneCore/src/Arcane/Base/Diagnostics.hpp:702-776`); `Arcane::Project::Root()`, `ActivePluginRoots()` (`ArcaneCore/src/Arcane/Project/Project.hpp:79,88`); `ModuleBuild::ExeDir()` (`Project/ModuleBuild.hpp`, as `ThemePresetDir` uses it); `AssetBrowserSettings::watchPollSeconds` (the asset-watch cadence, `EditorAppProject.cpp:436`); `EditorSyntaxThemeSettings`, `ActiveSyntaxRules` (TE3-5/6); `Theme::Live()` (`Widgets/EditorTheme.hpp:150`); `TextSettings`, `ToSyntaxLimits` (TE3-3); TE2-15 `TextDocument::{Open, Buffer, CanonicalPath (by value), Model, View, Draw}`, TE2-16 `TextDocumentServices::afterSave`, TE2-13 `TextEditorView::{SetRowColorRuns, Facts}` + `ViewColorRun`/`RowColorRunsFn`, TE2-11 `TextModel::{display, SyncDisplay}`, TE2-20's text-route wiring in `EditorApp.cpp` (TE3-30 adds the service there and assigns no `afterSave`: `ComposeTextAfterSave`, TE6-12, is the only place it is assigned -- plan rev 2 D-R7)
- Produces:
  - `struct Arcane::Text::StyledSpan { std::uint32_t begin, end; ScopeStyle style; }`; `void StyleLine(std::uint32_t lineBytes, const LineTokens* tokens, ScopeMap& styles, std::vector<StyledSpan>& out)`
  - `Arcane::Editor::TextSyntaxService` -- `SetProject`, `Tick(double)`, `NotifySaved(path)`, `Registry()`, `Styles()`, `Limits()`, `DetectFor(path, firstLine)`, `CreateCache(text, grammar)`, `StylesGeneration()`; `Arcane::Diagnostic ToDiagnostic(const GrammarProblem&)`; `std::filesystem::path EngineSyntaxDir()`
  - the grammar-reload step for the after-save composition: `void TextSyntaxService::NotifySaved(const std::filesystem::path& file)` -- `ComposeTextAfterSave` (TE6-12) calls it with the saved document's `CanonicalPath()` (plan rev 2 D-R7)
  - `TextSyntaxService* TextDocumentServices::syntax = nullptr` (**NEW member**, CANON A6: null = no highlighting -- `Highlight()` returns nullptr, the picker lists Plain Text only)
  - `Arcane::Text::HighlightCache* TextDocument::Highlight()` (the document's cache, for TE4's brackets/folds/status strip; canonical, there is no `Highlights()`), `void TextDocument::SetLanguage(std::string_view grammarName)` (TE4's language picker), `void TextDocument::UpdateHighlight(std::uint32_t firstVisibleRow, std::uint32_t lastVisibleRow)` (called once per frame by the document with the union of its views' visible rows; TE4-17 supplies the union when split)

One `TextSyntaxService` per editor: the `GrammarRegistry` (engine `data/Syntaxes` staged beside the exe, the project's `Config/Syntaxes`, each active plugin root's `Syntaxes`), one `ThreadedHighlightExecutor` shared by every document, the UI thread's `MatchScratch` (limits refreshed each tick from `editor.text.regexMatchLimit/regexDepthLimit`), the `ScopeMap` rebuilt whenever `editor.theme.syntax.rules` or the live palette changes, Problems rows through `Arcane::Diagnostics::Publish` (code `text.grammar.invalid` Error / `text.grammar.embed` Warning / `text.grammar.regexLimit` Warning, locator = the grammar file), and grammar files polled on the asset-watch cadence. The service reaches documents as `TextDocumentServices::syntax` (set by the app's text routes; null = no highlighting). Each `TextDocument` with a service owns a `HighlightCache` over its `TextBuffer`, colours its view through `View().SetRowColorRuns` (each token run resolved through the `ScopeMap`; bold/italic are carried but not drawn), calls `UpdateHighlight` once per frame before its views draw, and re-resolves its grammar by name when the registry's `Generation()` moves (a reload re-highlights open documents, s4.1). Saving reaches `NotifySaved` through `TextDocumentServices::afterSave`, which is assigned only by `ComposeTextAfterSave` (TE6-12; plan rev 2 D-R7): this task provides the grammar-reload step, `TextSyntaxService::NotifySaved(path)`, as a function the composition calls, and assigns no `afterSave` itself. So saving a grammar in the text editor reloads it live once TE6-12 has composed the hook; before that, the asset-watch poll (`Tick` -> `PollChanges`) picks the saved file up.

```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "TextEditor/Syntax/StyleLine.hpp"

using namespace Arcane::Text;

namespace
{
    LineTokens Runs(std::vector<TokenRun> runs)
    {
        LineTokens t;
        t.runs = std::move(runs);
        return t;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("StyleLine: plain, styled, merged, partial and capped lines", "[text-view]")
{
    ScopeTable scopes;
    const ScopeId str = scopes.Intern("string.quoted.x"), num = scopes.Intern("constant.numeric.x"), kw = scopes.Intern("keyword.x");
    const ScopeStyle red{ PackRgba(255, 0, 0, 255), true, false, false };
    ScopeMap map(scopes, { { "string", red }, { "constant", red }, { "keyword", { PackRgba(0, 0, 255, 255), true, false, true } } });
    std::vector<StyledSpan> out;

    StyleLine(10, nullptr, map, out);   // not ready: one plain span
    REQUIRE(out.size() == 1u);
    CHECK(out[0].begin == 0u); CHECK(out[0].end == 10u); CHECK_FALSE(out[0].style.hasColor);

    StyleLine(0, nullptr, map, out);
    CHECK(out.empty());

    const LineTokens t = Runs({ { 0, kw }, { 2, 0 }, { 3, str }, { 6, num } });
    StyleLine(8, &t, map, out);         // string and number share red: merged
    REQUIRE(out.size() == 3u);
    CHECK(out[0].begin == 0u); CHECK(out[0].end == 2u); CHECK(out[0].style.bold);
    CHECK(out[1].begin == 2u); CHECK(out[1].end == 3u); CHECK_FALSE(out[1].style.hasColor);
    CHECK(out[2].begin == 3u); CHECK(out[2].end == 8u); CHECK(out[2].style == red);

    LineTokens partial = t;
    partial.partial = true;
    partial.resumeAt = 4;
    StyleLine(8, &partial, map, out);   // tokenized up to 4; the rest plain
    REQUIRE(out.size() == 4u);
    CHECK(out[2].end == 4u);
    CHECK(out[3].begin == 4u); CHECK(out[3].end == 8u); CHECK_FALSE(out[3].style.hasColor);

    const LineTokens capped = Runs({ { 0, str }, { 5, 0 } });
    StyleLine(100, &capped, map, out);  // a capped line's last run is plain to the end
    REQUIRE(out.size() == 2u);
    CHECK(out[1].begin == 5u); CHECK(out[1].end == 100u); CHECK_FALSE(out[1].style.hasColor);
}
```

```cpp
    store.InstallAsEngineSink();
    Editor::TextSyntaxService svc(std::make_unique<Text::ManualHighlightExecutor>(), dir.path / "engine");
    const std::uint64_t gen = svc.Registry().Generation();
    Write(file, R"({"format":"arcsyntax","version":1,"name":"Test","scope":"source.t","files":[".tst"],"patterns":[{"match":"(bad"}]})");
    svc.NotifySaved(file);
    CHECK(svc.Registry().Generation() > gen);
    CHECK(svc.Registry().Find("Test") == svc.Registry().PlainText());
    bool found = false;
    for (const Diagnostic& d : store.Snapshot()) found |= d.code == "text.grammar.invalid";
    CHECK(found);
    Write(file, kGood);
    svc.NotifySaved(file);
    found = false;
    for (const Diagnostic& d : store.Snapshot()) found |= d.code == "text.grammar.invalid";
    CHECK_FALSE(found);   // fixed: retracted
    store.UninstallEngineSink();
}
```

```cpp
    {
        ImGuiContext* prev = ImGui::GetCurrentContext();
        ImGuiContext* ctx = ImGui::CreateContext();
        ImGui::SetCurrentContext(ctx);
        ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO();
        io.DisplaySize = ImVec2(1024, 768);
        io.IniFilename = nullptr;
        unsigned char* px = nullptr;
        int w = 0, h = 0;
        io.Fonts->GetTexDataAsRGBA32(&px, &w, &h);
        for (int i = 0; i < frames; ++i)
        {
            io.DeltaTime = 1.0f / 60.0f;
            ImGui::NewFrame();
            bool close = false;
            doc.Draw(close);
            ImGui::Render();
        }
        ImGui::DestroyContext(ctx);
        ImGui::SetCurrentContext(prev);
    }

    std::unique_ptr<Editor::TextDocument> OpenWith(const fs::path& p, Editor::TextDocumentServices services)
    {
        std::string error;
        auto doc = Editor::TextDocument::Open(p, std::move(services), error);
        INFO(error);
        REQUIRE(doc != nullptr);
        return doc;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("TextDocument: the syntax service detects, and the view asks the cache for its visible rows", "[text-view]")
{
    Test::TempDir dir("syntax_doc_view");
    Write(dir.path / "engine" / "Test.arcsyntax", kGood);
    Write(dir.path / "a.tst", "12 // c\nx\n");
    Editor::TextSyntaxService svc(std::make_unique<Text::ManualHighlightExecutor>(), dir.path / "engine");
    Editor::TextDocumentServices services;
    services.syntax = &svc;
    auto doc = OpenWith(dir.path / "a.tst", services);
    REQUIRE(doc->Highlight() != nullptr);
    REQUIRE(doc->Highlight()->Grammar() != nullptr);
    CHECK(doc->Highlight()->Grammar()->Name() == "Test");
    CHECK(doc->Highlight()->Peek(0) == nullptr);   // nothing tokenized before a frame
    DrawFrames(*doc, 2);
    const Text::LineTokens* row = doc->Highlight()->Peek(0);   // tokenized because the view's colour runs asked
    REQUIRE(row != nullptr);
    CHECK_FALSE(row->runs.empty());
    doc->SetLanguage("Plain Text");
    CHECK(doc->Highlight()->Grammar()->Name() == "Plain Text");
}

TEST_CASE("TextDocument: the grammar-reload step reloads a grammar saved in the editor", "[text-view]")
{
    // The step ComposeTextAfterSave (TE6-12) calls with the saved document (plan rev 2 D-R7). TE3-30 assigns no
    // afterSave and adds nothing to Save(); the composition itself is tested by TE6-12's F4 test.
    Test::TempDir dir("syntax_doc_save");
    const fs::path grammar = dir.path / "engine" / "Test.arcsyntax";
    Write(grammar, kGood);
    Editor::TextSyntaxService svc(std::make_unique<Text::ManualHighlightExecutor>(), dir.path / "engine");
    Editor::TextDocumentServices services;
    services.syntax = &svc;
    auto doc = OpenWith(grammar, services);
    const std::uint64_t gen = svc.Registry().Generation();
    Text::TextCommands(doc->Buffer(), doc->Model().selections).InsertText(" ");   // leading whitespace: still valid JSON
    REQUIRE(doc->Dirty());
    REQUIRE(doc->Save());
    CHECK(svc.Registry().Generation() == gen);   // Save() alone never reaches the service
    svc.NotifySaved(doc->CanonicalPath());       // the step, called as the composition calls it
    CHECK(svc.Registry().Generation() > gen);    // the saved grammar was re-read
    CHECK(svc.Registry().Find("Test") != svc.Registry().PlainText());
}
```

```cpp
#pragma once

// A row's tokens -> spans to draw (spec s4.3, s4.5): runs resolved through
// the theme's ScopeMap, adjacent equal styles merged, and everything not
// (yet) tokenized -- a not-ready row, the tail of a partial row, the part of a
// capped row past the cap -- in the default style.

#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Scope.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/SyntaxTypes.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    struct StyledSpan
    {
        std::uint32_t begin = 0;
        std::uint32_t end = 0;
        ScopeStyle style;   // hasColor false = the default text colour
    };

    void StyleLine(std::uint32_t lineBytes, const LineTokens* tokens, ScopeMap& styles, std::vector<StyledSpan>& out);
}
```

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/StyleLine.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/StyleLine.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    namespace
    {
        void Push(std::vector<StyledSpan>& out, std::uint32_t begin, std::uint32_t end, const ScopeStyle& style)
        {
            if (begin >= end) return;
            if (!out.empty() && out.back().end == begin && out.back().style == style)
            {
                out.back().end = end;
                return;
            }
            out.push_back({ begin, end, style });
        }
    }

    void StyleLine(std::uint32_t lineBytes, const LineTokens* tokens, ScopeMap& styles, std::vector<StyledSpan>& out)
    {
        out.clear();
        if (lineBytes == 0) return;
        if (!tokens || tokens->runs.empty())
        {
            Push(out, 0, lineBytes, ScopeStyle{});
            return;
        }
        const std::uint32_t covered = tokens->partial ? std::min(tokens->resumeAt, lineBytes) : lineBytes;
        Push(out, 0, std::min(tokens->runs.front().byteStart, covered), ScopeStyle{});
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < tokens->runs.size(); ++i)
        {
            const std::uint32_t b = std::min(tokens->runs[i].byteStart, covered);
            const std::uint32_t e = i + 1 < tokens->runs.size() ? std::min(tokens->runs[i + 1].byteStart, covered) : covered;
            Push(out, b, e, styles.Style(tokens->runs[i].scope));
        }
        Push(out, covered, lineBytes, ScopeStyle{});
    }
}
```

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/View/TextSyntaxService.hpp"

#include "Project/ModuleBuild.hpp"
#include "Settings/AssetBrowserSettings.hpp"
#include "Settings/SyntaxThemeSettings.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/LanguageOverrides.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/TextSettings.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Config/Settings.hpp>
#include <Arcane/Project/Project.hpp>

#include <cstring>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    Arcane::Diagnostic ToDiagnostic(const Arcane::Text::GrammarProblem& p)
    {
        using Kind = Arcane::Text::GrammarProblem::Kind;
        Arcane::Diagnostic d;
        d.scope = Arcane::DiagScope::Project;
        switch (p.kind)
        {
            case Kind::Invalid:
                d.severity = Arcane::DiagSeverity::Error;
                d.code = "text.grammar.invalid";
                d.detail = p.grammar.empty() ? "The file is ignored." : "Files in this language open as Plain Text until it is fixed.";
                break;
            case Kind::EmbedMissing:
                d.severity = Arcane::DiagSeverity::Warning;
                d.code = "text.grammar.embed";
                d.detail = "That embedded region draws without highlighting.";
                break;
            case Kind::RegexLimit:
                d.severity = Arcane::DiagSeverity::Warning;
                d.code = "text.grammar.regexLimit";
                d.detail = "Lines where it happens draw partly unhighlighted.";
                break;
        }
        const std::string who = p.grammar.empty() ? std::filesystem::path(p.source).filename().string() : p.grammar;
        d.message = who + (p.rulePath.empty() ? std::string() : " (" + p.rulePath + ")") + ": " + p.message;
        if (p.kind != Kind::RegexLimit && !p.source.starts_with("plugin:")) d.locator = Arcane::DiagLocator::File(p.source);
        return d;
    }

    std::filesystem::path EngineSyntaxDir() { return ModuleBuild::ExeDir() / "data" / "Syntaxes"; }

    TextSyntaxService::TextSyntaxService()
        : TextSyntaxService(std::make_unique<Arcane::Text::ThreadedHighlightExecutor>(), EngineSyntaxDir())
    {
    }

    TextSyntaxService::TextSyntaxService(std::unique_ptr<Arcane::Text::IHighlightExecutor> executor, std::filesystem::path engineDir)
        : m_executor(std::move(executor)), m_engineDir(std::move(engineDir))
    {
        m_registry.SetProblemSink([](std::string_view key, std::span<const Arcane::Text::GrammarProblem> rows) {
            std::vector<Arcane::Diagnostic> diags;
            diags.reserve(rows.size());
            for (const Arcane::Text::GrammarProblem& p : rows) diags.push_back(ToDiagnostic(p));
            Arcane::Diagnostics::Publish(key, diags);
        });
        SetProject(nullptr);
        RebuildStylesIfChanged();
    }

    TextSyntaxService::~TextSyntaxService() = default;

    void TextSyntaxService::SetProject(const Arcane::Project* project)
    {
        std::vector<Arcane::Text::GrammarSearchDir> dirs{ { m_engineDir, Arcane::Text::GrammarOrigin::Engine } };
        if (project)
        {
            dirs.push_back({ project->Root() / "Config" / "Syntaxes", Arcane::Text::GrammarOrigin::Project });
            for (const std::filesystem::path& plugin : project->ActivePluginRoots())
                dirs.push_back({ plugin / "Syntaxes", Arcane::Text::GrammarOrigin::Plugin });
        }
        m_registry.SetSearchDirs(std::move(dirs));
        m_registry.Reload();
    }

    Arcane::Text::SyntaxLimits TextSyntaxService::Limits() const { return ToSyntaxLimits(Arcane::Settings<TextSettings>()); }

    void TextSyntaxService::Tick(double editorClockSeconds)
    {
        m_uiScratch.SetLimits(Limits().regex);
        m_registry.PumpProblems();
        RebuildStylesIfChanged();
        if (editorClockSeconds >= m_nextPoll)
        {
            m_nextPoll = editorClockSeconds + Arcane::Settings<AssetBrowserSettings>().watchPollSeconds;   // the asset-watch cadence
            m_registry.PollChanges();
        }
    }

    void TextSyntaxService::NotifySaved(const std::filesystem::path& file) { m_registry.NotifySaved(file); }

    Arcane::Text::GrammarSnapshot TextSyntaxService::DetectFor(const std::filesystem::path& file, std::string_view firstLine) const
    {
        const std::vector<Arcane::Text::LanguageOverride> overrides =
            Arcane::Text::ParseLanguageOverrides(Arcane::Settings<TextSettings>().languageByExtension);
        return m_registry.Detect(file, firstLine, overrides);
    }

    std::unique_ptr<Arcane::Text::HighlightCache> TextSyntaxService::CreateCache(const Arcane::Text::IHighlightText& text,
                                                                                 Arcane::Text::GrammarSnapshot grammar)
    {
        Arcane::Text::HighlightCache::Services services;
        services.uiScratch = &m_uiScratch;
        services.executor = m_executor.get();
        services.problems = &m_registry;
        return std::make_unique<Arcane::Text::HighlightCache>(text, std::move(grammar), std::move(services), Limits());
    }

    void TextSyntaxService::RebuildStylesIfChanged()
    {
        const std::string& rules = Arcane::Settings<EditorSyntaxThemeSettings>().rules;
        const Theme::Palette& palette = Theme::Live();
        if (m_stylesBuilt && rules == m_appliedRules && std::memcmp(&palette, &m_appliedPalette, sizeof palette) == 0) return;
        m_styles = Arcane::Text::ScopeMap(m_registry.Scopes(), ActiveSyntaxRules(rules, palette));
        m_appliedRules = rules;
        m_appliedPalette = palette;
        m_stylesBuilt = true;
        ++m_stylesGeneration;
    }
}
```

In TE2-15's `TextDocument::InitAfterLoad()` (D-R2; rev-2 E4), append `InitHighlight();` after the test probe. `InitAfterLoad` is the single place `InitHighlight` runs: `Open` calls it once, after the model, buffer and view exist and `AdoptDecoded` ran; `AdoptDecoded` itself only updates metadata (Reopen with Encoding and TE2-17's reload call it again), the buffer, model and view are created once in `Open`, and Reopen with Encoding and Reload decode into the same `TextBuffer` (CANON TE2 #9c, TE2-17), so the cache follows them through the edit log, and the cache and the view's colour function made here live as long as the document. Never call it from `Open` directly or from the constructor (D-R2: the model and the view do not exist there). Definitions (`TextDocument.cpp`):

```cpp
    void TextDocument::InitHighlight()
    {
        if (!m_services.syntax)
            return;   // no highlighting (CANON A6)
        TextSyntaxService& syntax = *m_services.syntax;
        m_highlightText = std::make_unique<Arcane::Text::BufferHighlightText>(Buffer());
        m_highlight = syntax.CreateCache(*m_highlightText, syntax.DetectFor(CanonicalPath(), FirstLineForDetection()));
        m_grammarGeneration = syntax.Registry().Generation();
        View().SetRowColorRuns([this](std::uint32_t row, std::vector<ViewColorRun>& out) { return SyntaxRowColors(row, out); });
    }

    bool TextDocument::SyntaxRowColors(std::uint32_t row, std::vector<ViewColorRun>& out)
    {
        if (!m_highlight || !m_services.syntax)
            return false;
        const Arcane::Text::LineTokens* tokens = m_highlight->Line(row);   // nullptr: not ready, the row draws plain (s4.4)
        if (!tokens)
            return false;
        const Arcane::Text::Rope& text = Buffer().Text();
        const auto lineBytes = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(text.LineEnd(row) - text.LineStart(row));
        Arcane::Text::StyleLine(lineBytes, tokens, m_services.syntax->Styles(), m_spans);
        // A ViewColorRun lasts until the next run, so a default-styled span carries the text colour explicitly.
        const ImU32 plain = ImGui::GetColorU32(ImGuiCol_Text);
        for (const Arcane::Text::StyledSpan& s : m_spans)
            out.push_back({ s.begin, s.style.hasColor ? s.style.color : plain });
        return true;   // bold/italic are carried in ScopeStyle but draw in the regular face (only JetBrains Mono Regular ships)
    }

    std::string TextDocument::FirstLineForDetection()
    {
        std::string line;
        Arcane::Text::CopyRowForTokenize(Buffer().Text(), 0, m_services.syntax->Limits().longLineMaxBytes, line);
        return line;
    }

    void TextDocument::SetLanguage(std::string_view grammarName)
    {
        if (!m_highlight || !m_services.syntax)
            return;
        if (Arcane::Text::GrammarSnapshot g = m_services.syntax->Registry().Find(grammarName))
            m_highlight->SetGrammar(std::move(g));
    }

    void TextDocument::UpdateHighlight(std::uint32_t firstVisibleRow, std::uint32_t lastVisibleRow)
    {
        if (!m_highlight || !m_services.syntax)
            return;
        TextSyntaxService& syntax = *m_services.syntax;
        if (syntax.Registry().Generation() != m_grammarGeneration)   // a grammar was reloaded (spec s4.1)
        {
            m_grammarGeneration = syntax.Registry().Generation();
            const Arcane::Text::GrammarSnapshot& current = m_highlight->Grammar();
            Arcane::Text::GrammarSnapshot next = current ? syntax.Registry().Find(current->Name()) : nullptr;
            if (!next)
                next = syntax.DetectFor(CanonicalPath(), FirstLineForDetection());
            m_highlight->SetGrammar(std::move(next));   // a no-op when the snapshot is unchanged
        }
        m_highlight->SetLimits(syntax.Limits());
        m_highlight->BeginFrame(firstVisibleRow, std::max(firstVisibleRow, lastVisibleRow));
    }

    void TextDocument::UpdateHighlightForViews()
    {
        // The primary view's visible buffer rows, from its last frame's facts (the scroll a frame
        // behind costs nothing: Line() still serves any visible row within syncCatchUpLines).
        // TE4-17 extends this to min(first) / max(last) over both views when split.
        const TextViewFacts& f = View().Facts();
        Model().SyncDisplay();
        const Arcane::Text::DisplayMap& d = Model().display;
        const std::uint32_t firstDisplay = d.BufferRowToDisplay(f.firstVisibleRow);
        const std::uint32_t lastDisplay =
            std::min(firstDisplay + std::max<std::uint32_t>(f.visibleRows, 1u) - 1u, std::max<std::uint32_t>(d.DisplayRowCount(), 1u) - 1u);
        UpdateHighlight(f.firstVisibleRow, d.DisplayRowToBuffer(lastDisplay));
    }
```

The s11.2 regex-limit test needs no new product code -- TE3-2 (limits), TE3-11 (skip and report) and TE3-12 (dedupe and publish) already carry it -- so this task is its own reviewable test unit, validated by mutation in Step 2. The "find query" half is tested here at the engine level (a line-by-line `MatchScratch` scan, the shape s4.2 prescribes for find, returns `LimitHit` promptly and the scan goes on); the find bar's "stopped: pattern too complex" message belongs to TE4's `TextSearch`, which must surface `MatchStatus::LimitHit` (handed over in Produces of TE3-2).

```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Helpers/TextHighlightFixtures.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/GrammarRegistry.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightCache.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightWorker.hpp"

#include <chrono>
#include <map>

using namespace Arcane::Text;
using namespace Arcane::Test;

namespace
{
    constexpr std::string_view kCatastrophic = R"({"format":"arcsyntax","version":1,"name":"Evil","scope":"source.evil","files":[".evil"],
        "patterns":[{"match":"(a+)+$","scope":"invalid.evil"},{"match":"[0-9]+","scope":"constant.numeric.evil"}]})";

    std::string EvilLines(int n)
    {
        std::string s;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) s += "7 " + std::string(48, 'a') + "b 9\n";
        return s;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("Regex limits: a catastrophic grammar rule is skipped and reported once; UI and worker keep running", "[text-regex][text-highlight]")
{
    std::map<std::string, std::vector<GrammarProblem>> problems;
    GrammarRegistry reg;
    reg.SetProblemSink([&](std::string_view key, std::span<const GrammarProblem> rows) {
        problems[std::string(key)].assign(rows.begin(), rows.end());
    });
    reg.RegisterPluginGrammar("tests", "Evil", std::string(kCatastrophic));
    reg.Reload();
    const GrammarSnapshot g = reg.Find("Evil");
    REQUIRE(g != nullptr);

    FakeHighlightText text(EvilLines(60));
    MatchScratch ui{ RegexLimits{ 20000, 0 } };
    ManualHighlightExecutor exec;
    HighlightCache::Services s;
    s.uiScratch = &ui;
    s.executor = &exec;
    s.problems = &reg;
    SyntaxLimits l;
    l.syncCatchUpLines = 30;   // rows 0..29 on the UI thread, the rest on the worker
    l.regex = RegexLimits{ 20000, 0 };
    HighlightCache cache(text, g, s, l);

    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 59);
    REQUIRE(cache.Line(20) != nullptr);
    for (int i = 0; i < 10 && cache.Frontier() < cache.RowCount(); ++i)
    {
        exec.RunAll();
        cache.BeginFrame(0, 59);
    }
    const auto elapsed = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0;
    CHECK(cache.Frontier() == cache.RowCount());
    CHECK(elapsed < std::chrono::seconds(5));   // bounded: no hang (the unbounded match takes minutes)
    CHECK(ui.LimitHits() > 0u);

    // Every line still coloured its numbers.
    REQUIRE(cache.Peek(40) != nullptr);
    CHECK(cache.Peek(40)->runs.front().scope == *reg.Scopes().Find("constant.numeric.evil"));

    reg.PumpProblems();
    REQUIRE(problems.contains("text.grammar.limit:Evil"));
    REQUIRE(problems["text.grammar.limit:Evil"].size() == 1u);   // once, though 60 lines on two threads hit it
    CHECK(problems["text.grammar.limit:Evil"][0].rulePath == "patterns[0].match");
}

TEST_CASE("Regex limits: a threaded worker survives the same rule", "[text-regex][text-worker]")
{
    GrammarRegistry reg;
    reg.RegisterPluginGrammar("tests", "Evil", std::string(kCatastrophic));
    reg.Reload();
    FakeHighlightText text(EvilLines(200));
    MatchScratch ui{ RegexLimits{ 20000, 0 } };
    ThreadedHighlightExecutor exec;
    HighlightCache::Services s;
    s.uiScratch = &ui;
    s.executor = &exec;
    s.problems = &reg;
    SyntaxLimits l;
    l.regex = RegexLimits{ 20000, 0 };
    HighlightCache cache(text, reg.Find("Evil"), s, l);
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(10);
    while (cache.Frontier() < cache.RowCount() && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline)
    {
        cache.BeginFrame(0, 199);
        exec.WaitIdle();
    }
    CHECK(cache.Frontier() == cache.RowCount());
}

TEST_CASE("Regex limits: a find-style line scan with a catastrophic pattern stops each line promptly and goes on", "[text-regex]")
{
    MatchScratch scratch{ RegexLimits{ 20000, 0 } };
    // Not "(x+x+)+y" over x's: PCRE2 records the required last code unit 'y' and returns NoMatch at once on a
    // subject without one, so that pattern never reaches the limit (finding 3.9). ^(a+)+$ has no required
    // literal after the a's; over 64 a's and a 'b' it backtracks ~2^64 ways from its one start position.
    const auto re = Regex::Compile("^(a+)+$");
    REQUIRE(re.has_value());
    const std::string line = std::string(64, 'a') + "b";
    int limitHits = 0;
    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    for (int row = 0; row < 100; ++row)
        if (scratch.Match(**re, line, 0) == MatchStatus::LimitHit) ++limitHits;
    CHECK(limitHits == 100);
    CHECK(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0 < std::chrono::seconds(2));
    CHECK(scratch.Match(**re, "aaaa", 0) == MatchStatus::Match);    // the scratch is still usable
    CHECK(scratch.Match(**re, "aaab", 0) == MatchStatus::NoMatch);  // a short subject fails cleanly, under the limit
}
```

### Task TE3-32: Measure and set the syntax budget and limit defaults (spec s4.2-s4.4, s8, s11.5; settings rule)

**Files:**
- Create: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/SyntaxMeasureTest.cpp` (hidden tag `[.text-measure]`: never runs in the suite)
- Modify: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/TextSettings.hpp` (six initializers), `ArcaneTests/src/SweepTextSyntaxTest.cpp` (the matching `CHECK` and `RequireDefault` lines), the inventory's six `editor.text.*` rows ("(TE3-32 measures)" -> the measured value and its rule)
- Test: the existing `[sweep][text]` cases (re-pinned to the measured values)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: everything in TE3-2..TE3-29 (the shipped grammars as the corpus)
- Produces: the measured defaults of `editor.text.tokenizeLineBudgetUs`, `syncCatchUpBudgetUs`, `highlightFrameBudgetMs`, `regexMatchLimit`, `regexDepthLimit`, `bracketScanMaxLines`; the task report records every printed number and the machine (CPU model, Release build)

Each default is computed by a fixed rule from a measurement, so the step that sets it is mechanical and the reasoning is reviewable:

| Setting | Measured | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `tokenizeLineBudgetUs` | `T64`: median of 7 runs, tokenizing one 64 KiB minified-JSON line (the densest legitimate line at the cap) with the shipped JSON grammar | `clamp(roundUp100(2 x T64), 250, 8000)` -- a legitimate capped line never goes partial |
| `syncCatchUpBudgetUs` | `T200`: for each sample corpus (JSON, HLSL, Lua, Markdown samples repeated to 2,000 lines) the median of 7 runs tokenizing 200 consecutive lines; the max over corpora | `clamp(roundUp100(1.25 x T200), 500, 4000)` -- `syncCatchUpLines` of typical lines fit in one frame's allowance |
| `highlightFrameBudgetMs` | `R`: single-thread throughput (MB/s) tokenizing a generated 30 MB JSON document end to end | `clamp(ceil(1000 x (30 / R) / 600), 2, 8)` -- the slice that colours a 30 MB file within 10 s at 60 fps (the s11.5 "Ctrl+End in 30 MB" budget) |
| `regexMatchLimit` | `M0`: the smallest value in {100k, 250k, 500k, 1M, 2.5M, 5M, 10M} at which every shipped grammar tokenizes the whole corpus (all samples + the 30 MB JSON's first 10,000 lines) with zero limit hits; `H(V)`: JIT time to fail `^(a+)+$` on 40 `a` + `b` at limit V | the smallest ladder value >= `10 x M0`; then check `H(default) <= tokenizeLineBudgetUs / 2` -- if it fails, report both numbers (do not lower the headroom silently) |
| `regexDepthLimit` | `D0`: the smallest value in {1k, 2k, 5k, 10k, 20k, 50k, 100k} at which the corpus tokenizes with zero limit hits when every grammar is compiled `RegexOptions::NoJit` (the interpreter, the only place the depth limit applies) | the smallest ladder value >= `10 x D0` |
| `bracketScanMaxLines` | `S`: lines per millisecond `FindEnclosingBrackets` scans over the 10,000-line JSON corpus from a cursor with no enclosing pair (a full scan) | `clamp(floorTo1000(S x 1 ms), 1000, 100000)` -- a cursor move never spends more than about 1 ms looking for brackets |

`roundUp100(x)` rounds up to a multiple of 100; `floorTo1000` rounds down to a multiple of 1,000.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the measurement** -- `ArcaneTests/src/Text/SyntaxMeasureTest.cpp`:

```cpp
// TE3-32: measures the syntax budgets and limits and prints the derived
// defaults (hidden tag: run by hand, in Release, from the exe dir).

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Helpers/TextShippedGrammars.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Brackets.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/StateTable.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Tokenizer.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <fstream>
#include <iterator>

using namespace Arcane::Text;
using namespace Arcane::Test;
using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;

namespace
{
    double Us(Clock::duration d) { return std::chrono::duration<double, std::micro>(d).count(); }

    template <class F>
    double MedianUs(int runs, F&& f)
    {
        std::vector<double> t;
        for (int i = 0; i < runs; ++i)
        {
            const auto a = Clock::now();
            f();
            t.push_back(Us(Clock::now() - a));
        }
        std::sort(t.begin(), t.end());
        return t[t.size() / 2];
    }

    std::string JsonDocument(std::size_t targetBytes)
    {
        std::string s = "[\n";
        for (int i = 0; s.size() < targetBytes; ++i)
            s += "  {\"id\": " + std::to_string(i) + ", \"name\": \"item " + std::to_string(i) +
                 "\", \"tags\": [\"a\", \"b\\n\"], \"value\": -12.5e3, \"ok\": true, \"next\": null},\n";
        s += "  {}\n]";
        return s;
    }

    std::string MinifiedLine(std::size_t bytes)
    {
        std::string s = "[";
        while (s.size() < bytes) s += "{\"k\":\"v\\u0041\",\"n\":[1,2.5,-3e4,true,null]},";
        s.resize(bytes);
        return s;
    }

    // The sample's lines after its header line, repeated to `lines` lines.
    std::string Sample(std::string_view file, std::size_t lines)
    {
        std::ifstream in(RepoRoot() / "data" / "Syntaxes" / "tests" / std::string(file), std::ios::binary);
        const std::string text((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
        std::vector<std::string> body;
        std::size_t p = text.find('\n');
        while (p != std::string::npos && p + 1 < text.size())
        {
            const std::size_t q = text.find('\n', p + 1);
            body.push_back(text.substr(p + 1, (q == std::string::npos ? text.size() : q) - p - 1));
            p = q;
        }
        std::string out;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lines && !body.empty(); ++i)
        {
            out += body[i % body.size()];
            out += '\n';
        }
        return out;
    }

    // Tokenizes every line of `text`; returns the scratch's limit hits.
    std::uint64_t TokenizeAll(const CompiledGrammar& g, std::string_view text, MatchScratch& scratch)
    {
        StateTable states;
        Tokenizer t(g, states, scratch);
        const std::uint64_t before = scratch.LimitHits();
        StateId state = StateTable::kRoot;
        std::size_t p = 0;
        while (p <= text.size())
        {
            const std::size_t q = std::min(text.find('\n', p), text.size());
            state = t.TokenizeLine(text.substr(p, q - p), state).endState;
            p = q + 1;
        }
        return scratch.LimitHits() - before;
    }

    void Print(const char* name, double measured, const char* unit, std::uint64_t derived)
    {
        std::printf("MEASURE %s measured=%.3f %s derived_default=%llu\n", name, measured, unit, static_cast<unsigned long long>(derived));
    }
}

TEST_CASE("TE3-32: measure the syntax budgets and limits", "[.text-measure]")
{
    auto& reg = ShippedGrammars().registry;
    const GrammarSnapshot json = reg.Find("JSON");
    REQUIRE(json != nullptr);
    MatchScratch scratch{ RegexLimits{} };

    // tokenizeLineBudgetUs
    const std::string line64 = MinifiedLine(64 * 1024);
    StateTable states;
    Tokenizer jt(*json, states, scratch);
    const double t64 = MedianUs(7, [&] { (void)jt.TokenizeLine(line64, StateTable::kRoot); });
    const auto lineBudget = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::clamp(std::ceil(2.0 * t64 / 100.0) * 100.0, 250.0, 8000.0));
    Print("tokenizeLineBudgetUs", t64, "us(T64)", lineBudget);

    // syncCatchUpBudgetUs
    double t200 = 0.0;
    for (const auto& [name, file] : { std::pair{ "JSON", "syntax_test_json.json" }, std::pair{ "HLSL", "syntax_test_hlsl.hlsl" },
                                      std::pair{ "Lua", "syntax_test_lua.lua" }, std::pair{ "Markdown", "syntax_test_markdown.md" } })
    {
        const GrammarSnapshot g = reg.Find(name);
        REQUIRE(g != nullptr);
        std::string corpus = Sample(file, 200);
        t200 = std::max(t200, MedianUs(7, [&] { (void)TokenizeAll(*g, corpus, scratch); }));
    }
    const auto catchUp = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::clamp(std::ceil(1.25 * t200 / 100.0) * 100.0, 500.0, 4000.0));
    Print("syncCatchUpBudgetUs", t200, "us(T200)", catchUp);

    // highlightFrameBudgetMs
    const std::string big = JsonDocument(30u << 20);
    const auto a = Clock::now();
    (void)TokenizeAll(*json, big, scratch);
    const double seconds = Us(Clock::now() - a) / 1e6;
    const double mbps = 30.0 / seconds;
    const auto frameMs = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::clamp(std::ceil(1000.0 * (30.0 / mbps) / 600.0), 2.0, 8.0));
    Print("highlightFrameBudgetMs", mbps, "MB/s", frameMs);

    // regexMatchLimit
    std::string corpus;
    for (const char* f : { "syntax_test_json.json", "syntax_test_hlsl.hlsl", "syntax_test_lua.lua", "syntax_test_markdown.md",
                           "syntax_test_ini.ini", "syntax_test_toml.toml", "syntax_test_yaml.yaml", "syntax_test_xml.xml",
                           "syntax_test_batch.bat", "syntax_test_powershell.ps1", "syntax_test_shell.sh", "syntax_test_arcanelog.log" })
        corpus += Sample(f, 2000);
    corpus += big.substr(0, big.find('\n', 1u << 20));
    // Long legitimate prose lines (finding 3.10): a 4 KiB YAML description, the same text as a TOML string value
    // and as a Markdown paragraph. A key rule that rescans a line from every position is O(L^2) here: it would
    // inflate M0 (or, at the shipped default, raise spurious limit rows), so the corpus must hold such lines.
    std::string prose;
    while (prose.size() < 4096) prose += "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog with its friends. ";
    corpus += "description: " + prose + "\nsummary = \"" + prose + "\"\n" + prose + "\n";
    const std::uint32_t ladder[] = { 100000, 250000, 500000, 1000000, 2500000, 5000000, 10000000 };
    std::uint32_t m0 = 0;
    for (const std::uint32_t v : ladder)
    {
        MatchScratch s{ RegexLimits{ v, 0 } };
        std::uint64_t hits = 0;
        for (const std::string& name : reg.Names()) hits += TokenizeAll(*reg.Find(name), corpus, s);
        if (hits == 0) { m0 = v; break; }
    }
    REQUIRE(m0 != 0u);
    std::uint32_t matchDefault = ladder[std::size(ladder) - 1];
    for (const std::uint32_t v : ladder)
        if (v >= 10ull * m0) { matchDefault = v; break; }
    const auto evil = Regex::Compile("^(a+)+$");
    REQUIRE(evil.has_value());
    MatchScratch es{ RegexLimits{ matchDefault, 0 } };
    const std::string evilSubject = std::string(40, 'a') + 'b';
    const double hitUs = MedianUs(7, [&] { (void)es.Match(**evil, evilSubject, 0); });
    Print("regexMatchLimit", static_cast<double>(m0), "M0", matchDefault);
    std::printf("MEASURE regexMatchLimit H(default)=%.1f us, tokenizeLineBudgetUs/2=%.1f us -> %s\n", hitUs, lineBudget / 2.0,
                hitUs <= lineBudget / 2.0 ? "ok" : "CONFLICT (report both numbers)");

    // regexDepthLimit (interpreter only)
    const std::uint32_t depthLadder[] = { 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000, 50000, 100000 };
    std::uint32_t d0 = 0;
    {
        // Recompile the shipped grammars without JIT through a second registry reading the same files.
        // (CompileGrammarRules always JITs, so the interpreter path is measured on the grammar regexes
        // individually: every rule regex of every grammar, matched across the corpus lines.)
        std::vector<std::shared_ptr<const Regex>> interp;
        for (const std::string& name : reg.Names())
        {
            const GrammarRules& r = reg.Find(name)->Rules();
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < r.RuleCount(); ++i)
                for (const auto& re : { r.Rule(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i)).match, r.Rule(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i)).end,
                                        r.Rule(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i)).escape })
                    if (re)
                        if (auto x = Regex::Compile(re->Pattern(), RegexOptions::Ucp | RegexOptions::NoJit)) interp.push_back(*x);
        }
        std::vector<std::string_view> lines;
        for (std::size_t p = 0; p < corpus.size();)
        {
            const std::size_t q = std::min(corpus.find('\n', p), corpus.size());
            lines.push_back(std::string_view(corpus).substr(p, q - p));
            p = q + 1;
        }
        for (const std::uint32_t v : depthLadder)
        {
            MatchScratch s{ RegexLimits{ 100000000, v } };
            std::uint64_t hits = 0;
            for (const auto& re : interp)
                for (const std::string_view l : lines)
                    if (s.Match(*re, l, 0) == MatchStatus::LimitHit) ++hits;
            if (hits == 0) { d0 = v; break; }
        }
    }
    REQUIRE(d0 != 0u);
    std::uint64_t depthDefault = 10000000;
    for (const std::uint32_t v : depthLadder)
        if (v >= 10ull * d0) { depthDefault = v; break; }
    if (depthDefault == 10000000) depthDefault = std::min<std::uint64_t>(10ull * d0, 10000000);
    Print("regexDepthLimit", static_cast<double>(d0), "D0", depthDefault);

    // bracketScanMaxLines
    const std::string jsonLines = big.substr(0, [&] { std::size_t p = 0; for (int i = 0; i < 10000; ++i) p = big.find('\n', p) + 1; return p; }());
    const Rope rope = Rope::FromUtf8("x\n" + jsonLines);   // the cursor on row 0 sees no enclosing pair: a full scan
    const TokenLookup none = [](std::uint32_t) -> const LineTokens* { return nullptr; };
    const std::uint64_t lastRow = rope.LineCount() - 1;
    const double scanUs = MedianUs(7, [&] { (void)FindEnclosingBrackets(rope, rope.LineStart(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(lastRow)), json->Rules(), none, 0, 0); });
    const double linesPerMs = static_cast<double>(lastRow) / (scanUs / 1000.0);
    const auto scanDefault = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::clamp(std::floor(linesPerMs / 1000.0) * 1000.0, 1000.0, 100000.0));
    Print("bracketScanMaxLines", linesPerMs, "lines/ms", scanDefault);
}
```

(The bracket scan starts at the last row and walks up to the document's outer `[` in the first JSON row -- every other bracket is balanced -- then `FindMatchingBracket` walks forward from it to the end without finding the truncated document's `]`: the whole range twice, the worst case the bound exists for. `S` counts each line once for two passes, so the derived bound is conservative.)

**Spec gaps, conflicts and things I could not place:**
1. **Detection order (s4.1) -- resolved, a spec amendment (CANON D8; controller ruling).** The spec lists ext -> firstLine -> the remembered per-extension choice. Taken literally, the picker's memory could never correct an extension that a grammar's `files` claims (e.g. `.cfg` -> INI), which is the reason it exists. TE3-12 consults the remembered choice **first** (order: remembered choice -> `files` -> `firstLine` -> Plain Text), as the controller ruled; s4.1 is amended accordingly.
2. **Plugin-registered grammars (s4.1).** Arcane has no editor-plugin API for in-process registration today; TE3-12 implements both a data seam (each active plugin root's `Syntaxes/` directory) and an in-process `RegisterPluginGrammar`, but nothing outside the tests calls the latter yet.
3. **Italic/bold syntax styles (s4.5).** Carried through `ScopeStyle`, but only JetBrains Mono Regular ships (`premake5.lua:1129`), so TE3-30 draws them in the regular face; shipping italic/bold faces is a font task for TE2/TE6.
4. **`symbols` (s4.1/s9).** Validated and compiled (`GrammarRules::Symbols()`); the `ISymbolProvider` that consumes them is s9 and not in TE3's brief -- TE4 owns it (CANON A7).
5. **Find-query limit message (s4.2/s11.2).** TE3-31 proves the engine half; the find bar / vim message line wording belongs to TE4's `TextSearch` and TE5c.
6. **Per-entry `bufferVersion`/`grammarVersion` (s4.4).** Realized at cache level (every ready row is valid at the cache's synced version and grammar) and per worker result (checked on arrival) rather than stored in every row -- equivalent, because no row is ever valid at a version other than the cache's; stated in TE3-14 for the reviewer.
7. **Grammar expressiveness limits found while writing the v1 grammars:** no back-references from `end` into `begin` captures (Lua long brackets are listed per level 0-2; shell heredoc bodies and YAML block-scalar bodies are not recognised), no `include`/repository (rules are repeated where needed). None blocks a v1 language; a later format version could add `end` back-references.

- **Test** (always from the exe dir, TEMP/TMP set, seed recorded in the task report):
  ```powershell
  Set-Location D:\dev\starworks\Arcane-text\bin\Debug-windows-x86_64-md\ArcaneTests
  $env:TEMP = 'D:\dev\starworks\Arcane-text\.tmp-tests'; $env:TMP = $env:TEMP; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $env:TEMP | Out-Null
  ```

  Before each commit that touches shared code (`Input/`, `Panels/`, `TextDocument`, `TextEditorView`, settings): `.\ArcaneTests.exe "~[gpu]" --rng-seed 1 -r compact` from the same directory.
- **The constant guard** (`ArcaneTests/src/ConstantGuardTest.cpp`, `[sweep][guard]`) fails on any `constexpr` / `static const` / `inline const` declaration with a numeric literal in `ArcaneEditor/src` that has no `ARC_CONSTANT("why")` (from `<Arcane/Core/Constant.hpp>`) on the line above. TE4 code declares no numeric constants: tunables are `TextSettings` fields, UI metrics are derived from `ImGui::GetFontSize()` / `LineHeight()` inline, and tables use `std::to_array` (no count literal).
- **Settings rule:** every new tunable is a reflected `TextSettings` field with `DisplayName`, `Tooltip` and `Keywords`; limits carry `CVarFlags::Dev`; the settings inventory is frozen, so each new name gets a row in its `### Text editor` section, a "Post-freeze amendments" row, and the frozen list is regenerated with `powershell -NoProfile -File scripts\settings-inventory-lint.ps1 -RequireFrozen -EmitFrozen scripts\settings-frozen-names.txt` (TE1-9's command); the sweep (`[sweep]`) covers each one.
- **Placement:** Core and Syntax files (`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Core/**`, `Syntax/**`) belong to TE1's `ArcaneText` static lib, which globs them: they need only a premake regenerate. View/Document files compile into `ArcaneEditor` by its `src/**` glob; each one a test drives is ALSO appended to the `ArcaneTests` `files` list in `premake5.lua` (the per-file pattern at `premake5.lua:1189-1420`), after the TE2 text-editor entries (grep `TextEditor/View/TextEditorView.cpp` in that list).
- Includes use the `ArcaneEditor/src` root: `#include "TextEditor/Core/TextSearch.hpp"`.
- **TE2 integration edits** are described by insertion point (the function and the statement they follow), not line numbers: TE2's files are written by TE2's plan, not yet in the tree.
