### Task TE7-16: The C grammar, ported from lite-xl `language_c.lua` (spec s4.7, s10)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/C.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_c.c`, `ArcaneTests/src/Text/CGrammarFilesTest.cpp`
- Modify: `NOTICE.md` (the "Ported grammar content" lite-xl entry TE3-25 adds and TE3-29 extends to Markdown now also names C); `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (TE3's per-grammar file: a C case, and TE3-29's shipped-set case gains "C")
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/CGrammarFilesTest.cpp` and `GrammarScopeTests.cpp`, tags `[text-grammar-c][text-syntax-data]`
- **Depends on TE3-29** (plan rev 2 X5): this task edits TE3-29's shipped-set case and the `NOTICE.md` entry as TE3-29 leaves it, so it starts after TE3-29, not after TE3-20.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: TE3's `.arcsyntax` format and earliest-match tokenizer; TE3-20's `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars()` (`Helpers/TextShippedGrammars.hpp`); TE3-29's shipped-set case; `Arcane::Test::FindReferenceProjectDir()`; nlohmann/json.
- Produces: the grammar named `C` (`source.c`, files `.c`) with the scopes:
  - `comment.line.double-slash.c`, `comment.block.c`
  - `string.quoted.double.c`, `string.quoted.single.c`, `string.quoted.other.include.c`
  - `constant.numeric{,.hex,.octal}.c`, `constant.other.c`, `constant.language.c`
  - `keyword.control.c`, `keyword.other.c`, `keyword.other.octal-prefix.c`, `keyword.control.directive.c`, `keyword.operator.c`
  - `storage.type.c`, `entity.name.type.c`, `entity.name.function.c`

**How the port maps lite-xl onto `.arcsyntax`** (MIT; notice in the file's `notice` and in `NOTICE.md`):
- **Rule order is lite-xl's, one for one.** lite-xl tries its patterns in order, anchored at the current token. TE3's tokenizer takes the earliest match and breaks ties by the first rule. The two agree here because every word start is matched by the final identifier rule, so the earliest position is always the current token. Then, as in lite-xl, the first listed rule that matches there wins.
- **Lua patterns -> PCRE2.**

  | Lua | PCRE2 |
  |---|---|
  | `%a %w %u %d %s` | `[A-Za-z] [A-Za-z0-9] [A-Z] \d \s` |
  | `%f[(]` (frontier) | `(?=\()` |
  | `%f[#]#` | `(?<!#)#` |
  | `.-` (lazy) | `.*?` |
  | `^` | `^` |
  | `{ "/%*", "%*/" }` | a `begin`/`end` region |
  | `{ '"', '"', '\\' }` | a region with `escape: "\\\\."` |
  | `regex = ...` (isuf / fsuf / digitsep) | verbatim |

- **Capture types: one lite-xl behaviour needs care.** lite-xl splits a multi-capture match with `()` position captures and then looks **every piece's text** up in `symbols`, so a keyword inside a "type name" capture still gets the keyword colour. `.arcsyntax` keyword lookup applies to a whole match only. So each declaration rule starts with a negative lookahead over the whole symbols list, `(?!(?:if|...|NULL)\b)`. When the first word is a keyword, the rule does not match; the identifier rule colours the keyword, and the next word starts a fresh match. The samples below pin that the colours equal lite-xl's (`static int x`, `int main(`, `const char* kName`, `return foo(`).
- **lite-xl's type names map to TextMate scopes** so `.arctheme` prefix resolution finds them:
  - `keyword` becomes `keyword.control.c` for flow words and `keyword.other.c` for the rest; both resolve through `keyword`.
  - `keyword2` becomes `storage.type.c`.
  - `literal` becomes `constant.language.c` for `true false NULL`, and `entity.name.type.c` for a declaration's type name. lite-xl overloads `literal` for both.
  - `function` becomes `entity.name.function.c`.
  - `number` becomes `constant.numeric.*`. lite-xl also colours UPPER_CASE constants and `__MAGIC__` as `number`; here they are `constant.other.c`.
  - `operator` becomes `keyword.operator.c`.
  - `symbol` (a `#define`'s name) is left unscoped.
- **Strings end at the end of the line (plan rev 2, finding 7.14) -- a deliberate difference from lite-xl.** lite-xl's `"` and `'` regions have no end-of-line, and the grammar is not line-local (block comments span lines), so a stray quote -- the apostrophe in `#error don't build this file directly`, or an unterminated string -- coloured the rest of the file as a string. C has no multi-line string literal (a backslash-newline continuation is the one exception, rare, and it now shows as code on the next line), so both regions end on their quote **or** at the end of the line: `"end": "\"|$"` and `"end": "'|$"`, the zero-width `$` that TE3's Arcane Log grammar already uses. Block comments still span lines. The sample's last section pins it with real shapes: the `#error` apostrophe, `'"'` and `'\\'` character literals, escaped quotes inside a string, and an unterminated string -- each followed by a line that must still be code.
- **Kept as lite-xl has it.**
  - An octal literal's leading `0` is coloured as a keyword (`keyword.other.octal-prefix.c`), and the rest as `constant.numeric.octal.c`.
  - An UPPER_CASE constant at the very end of a line is not recognised, because lite-xl's frontier needs a following character.
- **Not from lite-xl, written fresh:** `indent`, `brackets`, `autoClose`, `symbols` (functions and struct/union/enum names for spec 2's `@`), and `#pragma region` fold markers. lite-xl has none of these.

Every rule and every sample assertion below was run through TE3's tokenizer model and its runner model (`scratchpad/texteditor/te3/proto.py`): 377 assertions, 0 failures (rev 2: the 7.14 string rules and their sample lines added and the whole sample re-run; the same sample against the rev-1 grammar fails 82 of them, so the new lines pin the fix).

```cpp
// TE7-16 / TE7-17: the C and C++ grammar files' metadata (text editor spec
// s4.7). Their highlighting is pinned by data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_c.c
// and syntax_test_cpp.cpp, which the [text-grammar-c] / [text-grammar-cpp]
// cases in GrammarScopeTests.cpp run through TE3-20's RequireScopeTest.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Helpers/ReferenceProjectDir.hpp"

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <set>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace fs = std::filesystem;

namespace
{
    nlohmann::json LoadGrammar(const char* file)
    {
        const fs::path p = Arcane::Test::FindReferenceProjectDir().parent_path() / "data" / "Syntaxes" / file;
        std::ifstream in(p);
        REQUIRE(in.good());
        return nlohmann::json::parse(in);
    }

    // The `end` of every region that begins with a plain " or ' (finding 7.14:
    // each must also end at the end of the line).
    std::vector<std::string> QuoteRegionEnds(const nlohmann::json& g)
    {
        std::vector<std::string> out;
        for (const nlohmann::json& rule : g["patterns"])
            if (rule.contains("begin") && (rule["begin"] == "\"" || rule["begin"] == "'"))
                out.push_back(rule["end"].get<std::string>());
        return out;
    }

    // No word may carry two keyword scopes in one rule (a typo would make the
    // colour depend on map order).
    void CheckKeywordTablesDisjoint(const nlohmann::json& g)
    {
        for (const nlohmann::json& rule : g["patterns"])
        {
            if (!rule.contains("keywords"))
                continue;
            std::set<std::string> seen;
            for (const auto& [scope, words] : rule["keywords"].items())
                for (const nlohmann::json& w : words)
                {
                    INFO(scope << " " << w.get<std::string>());
                    CHECK(seen.insert(w.get<std::string>()).second);
                }
        }
    }
}

TEST_CASE("C grammar: name, scope, .c only, lite-xl notice, both comment forms", "[text-grammar-c][text-syntax-data]")
{
    const nlohmann::json g = LoadGrammar("C.arcsyntax");
    CHECK(g["format"] == "arcsyntax");
    CHECK(g["name"] == "C");
    CHECK(g["scope"] == "source.c");
    CHECK(g["files"] == nlohmann::json::array({ ".c" }));
    CHECK(g["notice"].get<std::string>().find("lite-xl data/plugins/language_c.lua (MIT License") != std::string::npos);
    CHECK(g["comment"]["line"] == "//");
    CHECK(g["comment"]["block"] == nlohmann::json::array({ "/*", "*/" }));
    CHECK(g["lineLocal"] == false);
    CHECK(g["patterns"].size() == 31u);
    CHECK(QuoteRegionEnds(g) == std::vector<std::string>{ "\"|$", "'|$" });   // 7.14: a string never runs past its line
    CheckKeywordTablesDisjoint(g);
}
```

```json
  "files": [".c"],
  "comment": {"line": "//", "block": ["/*", "*/"]},

  "autoClose": [["\"", "\""], ["'", "'"], ["(", ")"], ["[", "]"], ["{", "}"]],

    {"match": "^\\s*(?:typedef\\s+)?(?:struct|union|enum)\\s+([A-Za-z_]\\w*)", "name": 1, "kind": "type"}

    {"begin": "\"", "end": "\"|$", "escape": "\\\\.", "scope": "string.quoted.double.c"},
    {"begin": "'", "end": "'|$", "escape": "\\\\.", "scope": "string.quoted.single.c"},
    {"match": "0x[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F']*(?:[lL][uU]|ll[uU]|LL[uU]|[uU][lL]\\b|[uU]ll|[uU]LL|[uU]|[lL]\\b|ll|LL)?", "scope": "constant.numeric.hex.c"},
    {"match": "(0)([0-7][0-7']*(?:[lL][uU]|ll[uU]|LL[uU]|[uU][lL]\\b|[uU]ll|[uU]LL|[uU]|[lL]\\b|ll|LL)?)", "scope": "constant.numeric.octal.c", "captures": {"1": "keyword.other.octal-prefix.c"}},
    {"match": "(?:\\d[\\d']*)\\.?(?:\\d[\\d']*)?(?:[Ee][-+]?(?:\\d[\\d']*))?[fFlL]?", "scope": "constant.numeric.c"},
    {"match": "\\.(?:\\d[\\d']*)(?:[Ee][-+]?(?:\\d[\\d']*))?[fFlL]?", "scope": "constant.numeric.c"},
    {"match": "[-+=/*^%<>!~|&]", "scope": "keyword.operator.c"},
    {"match": "##", "scope": "keyword.operator.c"},
    {"match": "(struct)\\s([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", "captures": {"1": "keyword.other.c", "2": "storage.type.c"}},
    {"match": "(union)\\s([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", "captures": {"1": "keyword.other.c", "2": "storage.type.c"}},
    {"match": "(static)(\\s+)(inline)", "captures": {"1": "keyword.other.c", "3": "keyword.other.c"}},
    {"match": "(static)(\\s+)(const)", "captures": {"1": "keyword.other.c", "3": "keyword.other.c"}},
    {"match": "(static)(\\s+)(?!(?:if|then|else|elseif|do|while|for|break|continue|return|goto|switch|case|default|typedef|enum|extern|static|volatile|const|inline|auto|struct|union|void|int|short|long|float|double|char|unsigned|bool|true|false|NULL)\\b)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", "captures": {"1": "keyword.other.c", "3": "entity.name.type.c"}},
```

### Task TE7-17: The C++ grammar, ported from lite-xl `language_cpp.lua` (spec s4.7, s10)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/CPP.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_cpp.cpp`
- Modify: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/CGrammarFilesTest.cpp` (the C++ cases); `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (a C++ case; the shipped-set list gains "C++" -- fifteen names, the count derived from the list); `NOTICE.md` (the lite-xl entry gains C++)
- Test: the same, tags `[text-grammar-cpp][text-syntax-data]`
- **Depends on TE3-29** (X5) and TE7-16.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: as TE7-16.
- Produces: the grammar named `C++` (`source.cpp`) with the C scopes (suffix `.cpp`) plus `constant.numeric.binary.cpp` and `string.quoted.raw.cpp`. Its files are `.cpp .cc .cxx .c++ .h .hh .hpp .hxx .h++ .inl .ino .cu .cuh`.
  - `.h` is C++, as in lite-xl: a header is far more often C++ in an Arcane project.
  - lite-xl's case-sensitive `%.C$` and `%.H$` are dropped. Extension matching is case-insensitive here, so they would collide with `.c` and `.h`.

On top of the C rules, the C++ port adds (in lite-xl's order):
- `0b` binary literals;
- `:` in the operator class;
- `class` and `namespace` with their names;
- `static constexpr` / `constinit` / `consteval`;
- the `Type ::` method-declaration rule;
- the `name ::` scope-access rule;
- `#include` with `\s+`;
- the C++ keyword list.

The method rule backtracks exactly as lite-xl's Lua pattern does (`Foo::` is split into two pieces, both `entity.name.type.cpp`). With the keyword lookahead, lite-xl's mis-colouring of `return ::f()` (as two type-name pieces) does not happen. That is the one intentional difference, and it is noted in the self-review.

**Strings end at the end of the line; raw strings span lines (plan rev 2, finding 7.14).** As in TE7-16, the `"` and `'` regions end on their quote or at the end of the line (`"\"|$"`, `"'|$"`), so the apostrophe in `#error don't ...` or an unterminated string colours one line, never the rest of the file. Arcane's own code is full of raw strings (526 `R"(` and 46 delimited ones -- `R"JSON(`, `R"rx(`, `R"ini(` -- in the settings tree), and lite-xl has no rule for them, so two regions are added, listed before the `"` region (the earliest-match tie goes to the first rule listed, so `R"` is never an identifier followed by a string):
- `R"( ... )"` -- begin `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(?:u8|[uUL])?R"\(`, end `\)"`. Exact: the empty delimiter's terminator is `)"`.
- `R"d( ... )d"` -- begin `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(?:u8|[uUL])?R"[^()\\\s"]{1,16}\(`, end `\)[^()\\\s"]{1,16}"`. `.arcsyntax` has no back-references from `end` into `begin` (TE3 self-review item 7), so the end matches the first `)d"` with *any* valid delimiter `d`. It is exact for every raw string in the settings tree, and it can only end **early** -- at a body sequence like `)x"` -- never past the real terminator, which always matches; a raw string therefore never colours past its own end.
- Both span lines (the grammar is not line-local) and have no escapes, as the language says. Scope `string.quoted.raw.cpp` (resolves through `string`).

The sample's last section pins them with Arcane's real shapes: `PathsGuardTest.cpp:67`'s `R"rx(...)rx"` (quotes and parentheses inside), a multi-line `R"JSON({ ... })JSON"` from `ClientRuntimeTest.cpp:69-76`, `WitnessScenariosTest.cpp:428`'s `R"ini(...)ini"`, TE3's own `R"({"match":"//.*$",...})"` (a `//` inside must not start a comment), an `LR"(...)"` prefix, a normal string holding `)"`, the `#error` apostrophe and an unterminated string -- each followed by a line that must still be code.

Validated with the same model: 529 assertions, 0 failures (rev 2: re-run with the new rules and lines; against the rev-1 grammar the same sample fails, so the lines pin the fix).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test** -- append to `ArcaneTests/src/Text/CGrammarFilesTest.cpp`:

```cpp
TEST_CASE("C++ grammar: name, scope, the header and source extensions, lite-xl notice", "[text-grammar-cpp][text-syntax-data]")
{
    const nlohmann::json g = LoadGrammar("CPP.arcsyntax");
    CHECK(g["name"] == "C++");
    CHECK(g["scope"] == "source.cpp");
    CHECK(g["files"] == nlohmann::json::array({ ".cpp", ".cc", ".cxx", ".c++", ".h", ".hh", ".hpp", ".hxx", ".h++",
                                                ".inl", ".ino", ".cu", ".cuh" }));
    CHECK(g["notice"].get<std::string>().find("lite-xl data/plugins/language_cpp.lua (MIT License") != std::string::npos);
    CHECK(g["patterns"].size() == 41u);   // lite-xl's 39 + the two raw-string regions (7.14)
    CHECK(QuoteRegionEnds(g) == std::vector<std::string>{ "\"|$", "'|$" });
    std::size_t raw = 0;
    for (const nlohmann::json& rule : g["patterns"])
        raw += rule.value("scope", std::string()) == "string.quoted.raw.cpp" ? 1u : 0u;
    CHECK(raw == 2u);
    CheckKeywordTablesDisjoint(g);
}

TEST_CASE("No other shipped grammar claims a C or C++ extension", "[text-grammar-cpp][text-syntax-data]")
{
    const std::set<std::string> ours{ ".c", ".cpp", ".cc", ".cxx", ".c++", ".h", ".hh", ".hpp", ".hxx", ".h++",
                                      ".inl", ".ino", ".cu", ".cuh" };
    const fs::path dir = Arcane::Test::FindReferenceProjectDir().parent_path() / "data" / "Syntaxes";
    for (const auto& entry : fs::directory_iterator(dir))
    {
        if (entry.path().extension() != ".arcsyntax")
            continue;
        std::ifstream in(entry.path());
        const nlohmann::json g = nlohmann::json::parse(in);
        if (g["name"] == "C" || g["name"] == "C++")
            continue;
        for (const nlohmann::json& f : g.value("files", nlohmann::json::array()))
        {
            INFO(entry.path().filename().string() << " claims " << f.get<std::string>());
            CHECK_FALSE(ours.contains(f.get<std::string>()));
        }
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test** -- `ArcaneTests/src/Text/OpenersWitnessTest.cpp`:

```cpp
// TE7-18: the D15 witnesses (text editor spec s5.6). A real DocumentHost,
// the real FileOpener wiring, real TextDocuments through OpenAsTextFlow,
// real editor.files.* settings, a real CreateProcessW of the process fixture
// and a real failing launch. Visual Studio is a recorder here; the
// [ide-desk] case drives the real one.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Documents/DocumentHost.hpp"
#include "Helpers/SettingsSweep.hpp"
#include "Helpers/TestEnvironment.hpp"
#include "Panels/DiagnosticStore.hpp"
#include "Project/IdeLaunch.hpp"
#include "Project/ModuleBuild.hpp"
#include "Project/Openers/CommandTemplate.hpp"
#include "Project/Openers/FileOpener.hpp"
#include "Project/Openers/FileOpenerWiring.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Document/OpenAsText.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Document/TextDocument.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Document/TextDocumentRoutes.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Config/CVarRegistry.hpp>

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

#include <chrono>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

namespace fs = std::filesystem;
using namespace Arcane::Editor;
using namespace Arcane::Editor::Openers;
using Arcane::CVarValue;

namespace
{
    fs::path FixtureExe()
    {
        return (ModuleBuild::ExeDir() / ".." / "arcbuild-process-fixture" / "arcbuild-process-fixture.exe").lexically_normal();
    }

    std::vector<std::string> WaitForRecord(const fs::path& record)
    {
        const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(10);
        while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline)
        {
            std::vector<std::string> lines;
            std::ifstream in(record, std::ios::binary);
            for (std::string line; std::getline(in, line);)
                lines.push_back(line);
            if (!lines.empty() && lines.back().starts_with("CWD:"))
                return lines;
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(20));
        }
        return {};
    }

    // The app's wiring over a real DocumentHost with the real text routes
    // (TE2-20, as the app registers them); Visual Studio recorded.
    struct Rig
    {
        DocumentHost host;
        OpenAsTextFlow flow{ host, {}, {} };
        std::vector<std::string> ideCalls;
        IdeLaunch::Outcome ideAnswer = IdeLaunch::Outcome::OpenedInInstance;
        fs::path project, solution;
        std::unique_ptr<FileOpener> files;

        Rig()
        {
            RegisterTextDocumentRoutes(host, TextRouteServices{});   // HasFactory is now true for every text file
            OpenerHost h;
            h.documents = &host;
            h.openAsText = [this](const fs::path& p) -> EditorDocument* { return flow.Open(p); };
            h.openInIde = [this](const fs::path& p, int line, int column) {
                ideCalls.push_back(PathUtf8(p.filename()) + ":" + std::to_string(line) + ":" + std::to_string(column));
                return ideAnswer;
            };
            h.projectRoot = [this] { return project; };
            h.solution = [this] { return solution; };
            files = std::make_unique<FileOpener>(MakeFileOpenerBackends(std::move(h)));
        }
    };
}

TEST_CASE("Witness: a .cpp opens with Visual Studio by default; switching editor.files.openWith opens it in an Arcane tab", "[witness][text-openers]")
{
    Arcane::Test::TempDir dir("openers_witness_cpp");
    const fs::path cpp = dir.path / "Game Mode.cpp";
    { std::ofstream(cpp, std::ios::binary) << "#include <cstdio>\nint main()\n{\n    return 0;\n}\n"; }
    Rig rig;

    OpenResult r = rig.files->Open(cpp, FilePosition{ 4, 5 });
    CHECK(r.ok);
    CHECK(r.opener == OpenerId::VisualStudio());
    CHECK(rig.ideCalls == std::vector<std::string>{ "Game Mode.cpp:4:5" });
    CHECK(rig.host.Count() == 0u);   // nothing opened inside Arcane

    {
        Arcane::Test::ScopedCodeRung map("editor.files.openWith", CVarValue::String("source=arcaneText;text=arcaneText;asset=dedicated"));
        r = rig.files->Open(cpp, FilePosition{ 4, 5 });
        CHECK(r.ok);
        CHECK(r.opener == OpenerId::ArcaneText());
        auto* doc = dynamic_cast<TextDocument*>(r.document);
        REQUIRE(doc != nullptr);
        CHECK(fs::equivalent(doc->CanonicalPath(), cpp));
        CHECK_FALSE(doc->ReadOnly());   // a .cpp has no dedicated editor: an editable tab, not TE6-12's locked one
        CHECK(rig.host.Count() == 1u);
    }

    // Back on the default map: the open tab wins -- no second copy in
    // Visual Studio behind the user's back (spec s5.6 "Rules").
    r = rig.files->Open(cpp);
    CHECK(r.reason == ResolveReason::AlreadyOpen);
    CHECK(rig.host.Count() == 1u);
    CHECK(rig.ideCalls.size() == 1u);
}

TEST_CASE("Witness: the default opener puts a .cpp in the running Visual Studio on this desk", "[ide-desk]")
{
    const char* sln = std::getenv("ARCANE_IDE_DESK");
    const char* file = std::getenv("ARCANE_IDE_DESK_FILE");   // a .cpp of 3+ lines
    if (!sln || !*sln || !file || !*file)
        SKIP("ARCANE_IDE_DESK / ARCANE_IDE_DESK_FILE not set -- desk-only probe");
    DocumentHost host;
    OpenerHost h;
    h.documents = &host;
    // The real route minus any devenv launch: a closed solution answers NoDevenv.
    h.openInIde = [sln](const fs::path& p, int line, int column) { return IdeLaunch::OpenFileAt({}, fs::path(sln), p, line, column); };
    FileOpener files(MakeFileOpenerBackends(std::move(h)));
    const OpenResult r = files.Open(fs::path(file), FilePosition{ 2, 3 });
    INFO(r.error << " -- Visual Studio should show the file, caret on line 2, column 3");
    CHECK(r.opener == OpenerId::VisualStudio());
    CHECK(r.ok);
}

#ifdef _WIN32
TEST_CASE("Witness: a custom program opener launches the fixture with the right argv", "[witness][text-openers]")
{
    Arcane::Test::TempDir dir("openers_witness_custom");
    const fs::path record = dir.path / "argv record.txt";
    const fs::path lua = dir.path / "init script.lua";
    const fs::path sln = dir.path / "My Game.slnx";
    { std::ofstream(lua) << "print(1)\n"; }
    { std::ofstream(sln) << "<Solution />\n"; }
    nlohmann::json list = nlohmann::json::array();
    list.push_back({ { "id", "fixture" }, { "name", "Fixture" }, { "exe", PathUtf8(FixtureExe()) },
                     { "args", "--record \"" + PathUtf8(record) + "\" -g \"{file}:{line}:{col}\" --sln {solution} --root \"{project}\"" } });
    Arcane::Test::ScopedCodeRung customs("editor.files.customEditors", CVarValue::String(list.dump()));
    Arcane::Test::ScopedCodeRung map("editor.files.openWith",
        CVarValue::String(".lua=custom:fixture;source=visualStudio;text=arcaneText;asset=dedicated"));
    Rig rig;
    rig.project = dir.path;
    rig.solution = sln;

    const OpenResult r = rig.files->Open(lua, FilePosition{ 12, 3 });
    INFO(r.error);
    REQUIRE(r.ok);
    CHECK(r.opener == OpenerId::Custom("fixture"));
    const std::vector<std::string> lines = WaitForRecord(record);
    REQUIRE(lines.size() == 7);
    CHECK(lines[0] == "ARG:0:-g");
    CHECK(lines[1] == "ARG:1:" + PathUtf8(lua) + ":12:3");
    CHECK(lines[2] == "ARG:2:--sln");
    CHECK(lines[3] == "ARG:3:" + PathUtf8(sln));
    CHECK(lines[4] == "ARG:4:--root");
    CHECK(lines[5] == "ARG:5:" + PathUtf8(dir.path));
    CHECK(lines[6] == "CWD:" + PathUtf8(dir.path));
    CHECK(rig.host.Count() == 0u);
}
#endif

TEST_CASE("Witness: a failing opener gives a Problems row and the fallback offer, which opens an Arcane tab", "[witness][text-openers]")
{
    Arcane::Test::TempDir dir("openers_witness_fail");
    const fs::path md = dir.path / "notes.md";
    { std::ofstream(md) << "# Notes\n\nSome text.\n"; }
    const fs::path missing = dir.path / "no such editor.exe";
    nlohmann::json list = nlohmann::json::array();
    list.push_back({ { "id", "missing" }, { "name", "Missing Editor" }, { "exe", PathUtf8(missing) }, { "args", "" } });
    Arcane::Test::ScopedCodeRung customs("editor.files.customEditors", CVarValue::String(list.dump()));
    Arcane::Test::ScopedCodeRung map("editor.files.openWith",
        CVarValue::String(".md=custom:missing;source=visualStudio;text=arcaneText;asset=dedicated"));
    DiagnosticStore store;
    store.InstallAsEngineSink();
    Rig rig;

    const OpenResult r = rig.files->Open(md, FilePosition{ 3, 2 });
    CHECK_FALSE(r.ok);
    const std::vector<Arcane::Diagnostic> rows = store.Snapshot();
    REQUIRE(rows.size() == 1);
    CHECK(rows[0].code == "files.open.failed");
    CHECK(rows[0].message == "Could not open notes.md with Missing Editor: '" + PathUtf8(missing) +
                             "' was not found (not an existing file, and not on PATH)");
    CHECK(rows[0].locator.line == 3);
    REQUIRE(rig.files->PendingOffer().has_value());
    CHECK(rig.files->PendingOffer()->offerArcaneText);

    const OpenResult accepted = rig.files->AcceptOffer();
    REQUIRE(accepted.ok);
    auto* doc = dynamic_cast<TextDocument*>(accepted.document);
    REQUIRE(doc != nullptr);
    CHECK(fs::equivalent(doc->CanonicalPath(), md));
    CHECK(rig.host.Count() == 1u);
    CHECK(store.Snapshot().empty());   // the successful open cleared the row
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.files->PendingOffer().has_value());
}
```

### Chunk TE7 self-review

**Spec sections covered -> tasks**

| Spec | Requirement | Task |

| D1 (amended), s1.2 (amended) | C++ editing in Arcane supported; no language services | TE7-9 (a `.cpp` opens as text when chosen), TE7-16/17 (highlighting only) |
| s4.7 | C and C++ grammars from lite-xl, MIT notice | TE7-16, TE7-17 |

| s5.6 Presets | VS Code, Sublime, Notepad++, Rider, CLion, Neovim in WT; App Paths + uninstall + PATH; not offered when absent; associations untouched | TE7-7, TE7-10 (the registry-write guard) |
| s5.6 Choosing | `editor.files.openWith` (map, group keys, PreferencesProject; a Project-rung value names built-in openers only), `editor.files.customEditors` (list, PreferencesMachine: never from a project) -- plan rev 2 D-R6 | TE7-1, TE7-2, TE7-3, TE7-8 (the refusal rows) |

| s5.6 Rules | a failing external opener -> Problems row + "Open in Arcane Text Editor instead"; never silent | TE7-8, TE7-9 (prompt), TE7-18 |
| s5.6 Rules | the C++ module rebuild flow is unchanged | nothing to do: a save in Arcane is a file write the existing watcher sees |
| s5.6 Rules | settings are reflected, swept, frozen | TE7-3 |
| s5.6 first paragraph | **every** route uses `FileOpener` | TE7-10, TE7-11 (enumerated table + `[openers-guard]`), TE7-9 (crash links) |
| s9 / spec 2 | Goto Anything / Find in Files call `FileOpener` | produced (`Open` / `OpenWith`, `FilePosition`, `PositionFrom`); spec 2 consumes |

**Decisions and spec gaps to reconcile**
1. **Explicit before already-open.** Open With / Open as Text are honoured even when a text tab shows the file. The spec's "regardless of the opener **setting**" is read as covering resolution from settings, not the user's own one-off pick. The assignment listed already-open first; flag it to the user if they meant the tab to win over an explicit Open With too.
2. **`dedicated` is overridable** through a `.ext` entry or the `asset` key ("never forced tooling"). The assignment ordered "dedicated-editor assets" before the map. The built-in default is still the dedicated editor, and "nothing" is not an opener.
3. **The page lives at Preferences > Editor > Files > Open With**, not "Files > Open With". The settings tree has fixed roots (`SettingsModel.cpp:17-18`), and an unknown root files under Engine. A spec wording fix.
4. **Map and list are strings.** There is no map or list cvar type, so these are the `key=opener;...` string and JSON, like `languageByExtension` and `vim.remaps`. A user edit copies the effective **trusted** map (`ReadFilesSettings`), so a project's built-in suggestions present then are kept in the user's copy, and its refused custom / preset entries never are (D-R6).
5. **`FileOpener` takes `FilePosition`** (1-based line, character column), not `Text::Point`. It is what `DiagLocator`, crash frames and every external tool speak. The Arcane backend converts (`ToBufferPoint`). Spec 2 callers holding a `Text::Point` convert with `row + 1` and a code-point count.
6. **Console has no file rows** to attach Open With or `file:line` routing to (no locator on Console rows today). Problems rows carry both.
7. **The Inspector's Open With is a right-click on the existing Open icon**, so the `editor-asset-page` golden is unchanged.
8. **devenv's command line takes no column.** A *new* Visual Studio instance gets the line only; a running one gets line and column.
9. **Windows Terminal splits on `;`**, so a `{file}` containing `;` breaks the `nvim-wt` preset (noted in the header and tooltip).
10. **The system-default opener fails on "no association"** (Problems row + offer) instead of falling back to the Open With picker. `OsShell::OpenAsText` keeps no caller after TE7-11 (CANON B6: TE6-12 left its callers for TE7-11); it stays in `OsShell`, and the guard allows only `OsShell` itself.
11. **Clicking a `files:open` failure row** routes through `FileOpener` again, with the same opener. The way out is the row's Open With or the offer; that is by design, since the row stays until a successful open.
12. **C/C++ grammar fidelity.**
    - The keyword-exclusion lookahead reproduces lite-xl's per-capture symbol lookup. The samples pin it, and it also fixes lite-xl's `return ::f()` mis-colour.
    - lite-xl's `literal`/`number` overloads are split into TextMate scopes (table in TE7-16).
    - `.C`/`.H` (case-sensitive in lite-xl) are dropped.
    - Strings end at the end of the line, and C++ raw strings (`R"(...)"`, `R"d(...)d"`) are recognised, spanning lines (rev 2, finding 7.14; not in lite-xl). A delimited raw string ends at the first `)d"` with any valid delimiter -- `.arcsyntax` has no `end` back-references -- so it can end early, never late. The spec's s4.7 note "C++ raw string literals are not recognised" changes accordingly (header/spec fixer).
13. **Other chunks must call `FileOpener`**, or `[openers-guard]` fails them: TE5's global marks and `:e` (the adapter's `openText`), TE6-14/15's restore (`openText`), TE6-23's automation open. TE2's own direct opens (`--open-path`, RouteLocator's `OpenAt`, the scripted focus) are re-routed by TE7-11. GATE-1's sweep is `[openers-guard]`. TE3-29's shipped-set case lists the fifteen grammars (TE7-16 adds "C", TE7-17 "C++").
14. **Names now canonical** (CANON A): `TextDocument::GoTo` (TE2-19), `SniffsAsText` (TE2-15), `IsCppSourcePath` (TE2-15), `Text::NormaliseExtension` (TE3-3), `Utf8::DecodeAt` (TE1-1), `TextDocument::Open(path, services, error)`, `CanonicalPath()` by value, `WindowLabel()`. `Files()` is public because TE5's runtime, TE6-15's restore lambda and TE6-23's automation call it.
15. **`HasFactory` is not "has a dedicated editor".** After TE2-20 it is true for every text file. TE2-19 produces `DocumentHost::HasDedicatedFactory` (and `RegisterTextFactory`, which TE2-20's `RegisterTextDocumentRoutes` calls for each explicit text extension; cross-fix X1 moved both out of TE7-9) and every TE7 "dedicated editor" fact (FileOpener's wiring, the tab menu, the asset panels, the Open With page) reads it. Without it, every text file falls in the `asset` group and a `.cpp` opens as text by default. TE7-9's routes case and witness 1 (over the real routes) pin it.
16. **Plan revision 2 (external review, findings 7.1-7.15, X5, D-R6).**
    - D-R6 (7.2): `customEditors` is PreferencesMachine and read only from rungs outside the project tree; a Project/Plugin `openWith` keeps built-in openers only; refusals are `files.openWith.refused` Problems rows; `IsBatchFile` strips trailing dots and spaces; `DocumentHost::OpenPath` / `OpenAt` and `EditorApp::OpenAsText` are private (TE7-11, `HostOpenAccess` is the wiring's friend), and the widened guard is the secondary check.
    - 7.1: program existence is `GetFileAttributesW` (`ProgramFileExists`), never `is_regular_file`, so a Store execution alias (`wt.exe`) is found; the PATH walk is TE7-5's own.
    - 7.3: a write a stronger rung outranks is saved and reported (`note`), never treated as a failure.
    - 7.4 / 7.15: `files:openWith` rows come from the settings (recomputed on publish), never the last file; `ClearFailures` lets them come back after a project switch.
    - 7.5: Visual Studio's column is UTF-16 code units; `VisualStudioColumn` converts.
    - 7.6: custom programs break away from the editor's job (retried without on access denied).
    - 7.7 / 7.8: TE2-20's `OpenAtPathAndPoint` wrapper is deleted; the guard scans whole files (multi-line calls, literal-aware), matches tokens (aliases, wrappers) and gives allowed files budgets instead of whole-file exemptions.
    - 7.9 / 7.10: `NoteAssetMoved` keeps `RefreshCanonicalKey`; `CloseAll` / `Add` drop stale paths and the tab-menu target.
    - 7.11 / 7.13: every Open With menu builds from `FileOpener::FactsFor` (the real facts), so "(default)" is what Open does and "Arcane editor" appears only for a dedicated editor.
    - 7.12: the scripted focus re-request focuses; it never re-opens.
    - 7.14: C/C++ strings end at the end of the line; C++ raw strings are regions (exact for every raw string in the settings tree: 526 `R"(` and 46 delimited, checked).
    - X5: TE7-16/17 run after TE3-29.

## Chunk TE6 (continued): Polish + gates

### TE6 part 2 of 3: the essentials and the release gate (TE6-3, 4, 5, 21, 22, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 23, 24, GATE-1)

### Task TE6-3: Follow over TE2-17's poll -- the follow cadence, a per-poll chunk cap, `FollowAvailable` (spec s3.5, s5.3)

TE2 owns change detection, the clean-only append, truncation, rotation and deletion (CANON B1: TE2-4's classifier, TE2-17's `PollDisk` / `AppendTail` / `ReloadFromDisk`; appends are applied on the first poll that sees them, CANON C TE2 #12). Follow adds three things on top and nothing else: a faster poll while `Follow()` is on, a cap on how many appended bytes one poll reads (the rest arrives on later polls), and the question "should the status strip offer Follow at all". The Follow state itself is TE2-16's `TextDocument::SetFollow(bool)` / `Follow()`, unchanged here; TE6-4 makes `SetFollow(true)` scroll the primary view to the end (it produces `TextEditorView::ScrollToEnd`).

**Files:**
- Modify: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/TextSettings.hpp`: add `followPollSeconds` and `followChunkKB` to `struct TextSettings`.
- Modify: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/TextSettings.cpp`: two `ARC_REFLECT_FIELD` rows inside the `ARC_REFLECT_TYPE(TextSettings)` block, before `ARC_END_REFLECT_TYPE()`.
- Modify: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Document/TextDocument.hpp` and `.cpp`:
  - `bool FollowAvailable() const` (new, public);
  - TE2-17's `Tick(double)` rewritten (the Follow cadence);
  - the `DiskChange::Appended` branch of TE2-17's private `ObserveDisk(const FileStamp&) const` rewritten (the per-poll cap and the CR hold-back); `ActOnDisk` and `AppendTail` stay TE2-17's.
- Modify: `docs/superpowers/audits/2026-10-03-settings-inventory.md`: two rows in the Part 3 `### Text editor` table, one row in the "Post-freeze amendments" table (the inventory is FROZEN).
- Modify: `scripts/settings-frozen-names.txt`: regenerated by the lint, never by hand.
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/TextDocumentFollowTest.cpp` (tag `[text-follow]`)
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/TextPolishSettingsTest.cpp` (new; later TE6 tasks append their settings cases here)

No new source file and no `premake5.lua` change: everything lives in TE2's `TextDocument` and TE1's `TextSettings`, which ArcaneTests already source-compiles. The two test files are picked up by the ArcaneTests `ArcaneTests/src/**.cpp` glob once premake is re-run.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - TE2-16 `TextDocument::SetFollow(bool)`, `Follow() const` (the state, CANON B22);
  - TE2-17 `TextDocument::Tick(double) override`, `PollDisk()` (appends act on the poll that sees them; a replacement settles per D-R10: a pending stamp that differs from the last only by growth settles at once, a rotation or truncation when two consecutive polls agree or `editor.text.follow.maxDebounceMs` passes, via `m_pendingStamp`), the private `struct DiskObservation { DiskChange change; std::string window; std::string tail; bool splitsCrLf; }`, `DiskObservation ObserveDisk(const FileStamp&) const`, `ActOnDisk(const DiskObservation&, const FileStamp&)`, `AppendTail(window, tail, now)` (decodes the consumed tail with `Text::DecodeFragment(bytes, Encoding(), Buffer().Eols().Dominant())`, CANON B2), `m_pollElapsed`, `m_synced`, `m_canonical`, `Encoding()`, and `std::uint64_t AppendCount() const` (CANON A11);
  - TE2-4 `CompleteTailLength`, `TailSplitsCrLf`, `LastUnitOf` (all over `Text::TextEncoding`; `Utf8Bom` behaves as `Utf8`), `DiskChange`;
  - TE2-5 `std::optional<std::string> ReadRangeShared(const std::filesystem::path&, std::uint64_t offset, std::uint64_t length)` (opens with read, write and delete sharing);
  - TE2-15 `TextDocument::Open(path, TextDocumentServices, std::string& error)`, `CanonicalPath()` (by value), `Buffer()`, `Model()`, `Synced()`, `Dirty()`, `Save()`;
  - TE2-2 `TextSettings::watchPollSeconds`; TE3-3 `Text::NormaliseExtension(std::string_view)`;
  - TE1-11 `Text::TextEncoding`; TE1 `TextBuffer::{ChangeId, CanUndo, Eols}`, `Text::TextCommands`; TE2-11 `DefaultEditContext(TextModel&)`;
  - `Test::RequireDefault`, `Test::ScopedCodeRung` (`ArcaneTests/src/Helpers/SettingsSweep.hpp`); `scripts/settings-inventory-lint.ps1 -RequireFrozen -EmitFrozen` (the frozen-inventory route TE2-2 and TE4-3 use).
- Produces:
  - `bool TextDocument::FollowAvailable() const` = `AppendCount() > 0 || Text::NormaliseExtension(CanonicalPath().extension().string()) == ".log"` (CANON A11);
  - settings `editor.text.followPollSeconds` (`double`, default 0.25, Dev, range 0.05..5) and `editor.text.followChunkKB` (`std::uint32_t`, default 4096, Dev, range 1..65536) (CANON A12; both are s8 amendments, CANON D29);
  - the behaviour: while `Follow()` is on, `Tick` polls every `followPollSeconds` instead of every `watchPollSeconds`; every append (Follow or not) reads at most `followChunkKB * 1024` bytes per poll.
- Does NOT produce: a follow class, file or poll of its own (CANON A11/B1: TE2-17's poll is the only one), and no `ScrollToEnd` call (TE6-4 adds it to `SetFollow`).

**Why the cap applies to every append, not only under Follow.** A program that dumps 200 MB into a log the editor has open (Follow or not) would otherwise make one poll read, decode and append 200 MB inside a frame. With the cap, one poll costs at most one `followChunkKB` read + decode + `AppendExternal`; the rest arrives on the following polls while the document stays clean (the synced size advances only by what was appended, so the next poll classifies the remainder as `Appended` again).

**Why the CR hold-back.** TE2-4's `TailSplitsCrLf` turns an append whose first unit is `\n` after a file that ended in `\r` into a full reload (the old text's lone CR would otherwise become a blank line). That rule is right for a writer that really stopped after `\r`, but our own chunk cut must never manufacture the case: when the cap cut the tail (`take < available`) and the trimmed tail's last unit is `\r`, that unit is held back with the rest (one byte for `Utf8` / `Utf8Bom` / `Windows1252`, two for `Utf16LE` / `Utf16BE`).

**TE4-3's hidden contract case.** TE4-3's `[.te6-recovery-contract]` case checks `followPollSeconds` / `followChunkKB` and TE6-13's `recoveryMaxMB` / `recoveryIntervalSeconds` together (CANON C TE4 #3). This task makes its two follow lines true (the defaults, the Dev flag) but does NOT remove the `.` from the tag: the recovery names do not exist until TE6-13, which registers them and un-hides the case. `TextPolishSettingsTest.cpp` below asserts the same follow lines now, so they are green from this task on.

```cpp
// Text editor TE6-3 (spec s3.5, s5.3): Follow over TE2-17's poll -- the follow
// cadence, the per-poll chunk cap (a burst arrives over several polls, the
// document stays clean), our own chunk cut never splits a CRLF, and when the
// status strip offers Follow at all.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
#include "Helpers/SettingsSweep.hpp"

#include "TextEditor/Core/TextCommands.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Document/TextDocument.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextModel.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>

using namespace Arcane;
using namespace Arcane::Editor;

namespace
{
    struct ScratchDir
    {
        std::filesystem::path dir;
        explicit ScratchDir(const char* name) : dir(std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / name)
        {
            std::error_code ec;
            std::filesystem::remove_all(dir, ec);
            std::filesystem::create_directories(dir);
        }
        ~ScratchDir()
        {
            std::error_code ec;
            std::filesystem::remove_all(dir, ec);
        }
    };

    void WriteAll(const std::filesystem::path& p, std::string_view bytes)
    {
        std::ofstream(p, std::ios::binary).write(bytes.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));
    }

    void AppendAll(const std::filesystem::path& p, std::string_view bytes)
    {
        std::ofstream(p, std::ios::binary | std::ios::app).write(bytes.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));
    }

    std::unique_ptr<TextDocument> OpenOrFail(const std::filesystem::path& p)
    {
        std::string error;
        std::unique_ptr<TextDocument> doc = TextDocument::Open(p, {}, error);
        INFO(error);
        REQUIRE(doc != nullptr);
        return doc;
    }

    std::string TextOf(TextDocument& d) { return d.Buffer().Text().ToString(); }

    // A user edit at the primary cursor, through TE1's commands (one undo step).
    void Type(TextDocument& doc, std::string_view text)
    {
        Text::TextCommands(doc.Buffer(), doc.Model().selections, DefaultEditContext(doc.Model())).InsertText(text);
    }

    // ASCII -> UTF-16LE code units (no BOM).
    std::string Utf16Le(std::string_view ascii)
    {
        std::string out;
        for (const char c : ascii) { out += c; out += '\0'; }
        return out;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("follow: under Follow, Tick polls every editor.text.followPollSeconds; without it, every watchPollSeconds", "[text-follow]")
{
    const ScratchDir s("arcane-te6-follow-cadence");
    const std::filesystem::path plainPath = s.dir / "plain.log";
    const std::filesystem::path followPath = s.dir / "follow.log";
    WriteAll(plainPath, "1\n");
    WriteAll(followPath, "1\n");
    auto plain = OpenOrFail(plainPath);
    auto followed = OpenOrFail(followPath);
    followed->SetFollow(true);
    REQUIRE(followed->Follow());

    AppendAll(plainPath, "2\n");
    AppendAll(followPath, "2\n");

    followed->Tick(0.2);                                   // 0.2 s < followPollSeconds (0.25): no poll yet
    CHECK(TextOf(*followed) == "1\n");
    followed->Tick(0.1);                                   // 0.3 s: one poll, and an append acts on the first poll
    CHECK(TextOf(*followed) == "1\n2\n");

    plain->Tick(0.3);                                      // not following: watchPollSeconds (1.0) governs
    CHECK(TextOf(*plain) == "1\n");
    plain->Tick(0.8);                                      // 1.1 s: one poll
    CHECK(TextOf(*plain) == "1\n2\n");

    followed->SetFollow(false);                            // back to the watch cadence
    AppendAll(followPath, "3\n");
    followed->Tick(0.3);
    CHECK(TextOf(*followed) == "1\n2\n");
    followed->Tick(0.8);
    CHECK(TextOf(*followed) == "1\n2\n3\n");
}

TEST_CASE("follow: a burst larger than editor.text.followChunkKB arrives over several polls and stays clean", "[text-follow]")
{
    const Test::ScopedCodeRung chunk("editor.text.followChunkKB", CVarValue::UInt32(4));   // 4096 bytes per poll
    const ScratchDir s("arcane-te6-follow-burst");
    const std::filesystem::path p = s.dir / "burst.log";
    WriteAll(p, "head\n");
    auto doc = OpenOrFail(p);
    Type(*doc, "> ");
    REQUIRE(doc->Save());                                  // clean, with one undo entry
    REQUIRE(doc->Buffer().CanUndo());
    const std::uint64_t changeId = doc->Buffer().ChangeId();
    const std::uint64_t base = std::filesystem::file_size(p);   // "> head\n" = 7 bytes
    REQUIRE(base == 7u);

    std::string burst;
    for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) burst += std::string(99, 'x') + "\n";   // 10000 bytes, no CR anywhere
    REQUIRE(burst.size() == 10000u);
    AppendAll(p, burst);

    doc->PollDisk();                                       // Follow is OFF: the cap applies to every append
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "> head\n" + burst.substr(0, 4096));
    CHECK(doc->Synced().stamp.size == base + 4096u);       // synced size advanced by exactly what was appended
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Dirty());
    doc->PollDisk();
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "> head\n" + burst.substr(0, 8192));
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Dirty());
    doc->PollDisk();
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "> head\n" + burst);
    CHECK(doc->Synced().stamp.size == base + 10000u);
    CHECK(doc->AppendCount() == 3u);

    doc->PollDisk();                                       // nothing left: nothing changes
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "> head\n" + burst);
    CHECK(doc->AppendCount() == 3u);

    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Dirty());
    CHECK(doc->Buffer().ChangeId() == changeId);           // appends are not edits (spec s3.5)
    CHECK(doc->Buffer().CanUndo());                        // history intact...
    REQUIRE(doc->Buffer().Undo(doc->Model().selections));  // ...and the pre-append edit still undoes
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "head\n" + burst);
}

TEST_CASE("follow: a chunk cut between CR and LF holds the CR back -- the CRLF is appended whole, never a reload", "[text-follow]")
{
    const Test::ScopedCodeRung chunk("editor.text.followChunkKB", CVarValue::UInt32(4));
    const ScratchDir s("arcane-te6-follow-crlf");

    SECTION("UTF-8: one byte held back")
    {
        const std::filesystem::path p = s.dir / "crlf.log";
        WriteAll(p, "a\r\n");
        auto doc = OpenOrFail(p);
        const std::uint64_t changeId = doc->Buffer().ChangeId();
        REQUIRE_FALSE(doc->Buffer().CanUndo());
        const std::string ys(4095, 'y');
        AppendAll(p, ys + "\r\n" + "tail\r\n");           // byte 4096 of the tail is the CR

        doc->PollDisk();
        CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "a\n" + ys);                 // the CR waits with the rest
        CHECK(doc->Synced().stamp.size == 3u + 4095u);
        doc->PollDisk();
        CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "a\n" + ys + "\ntail\n");
        CHECK(doc->Buffer().Eols().Dominant() == Text::Eol::CRLF);
        CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Eols().IsMixed());
        CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().CanUndo());              // a reload would have been one undoable step
        CHECK(doc->Buffer().ChangeId() == changeId);
        CHECK_FALSE(doc->Dirty());
        CHECK(doc->AppendCount() == 2u);
    }

    SECTION("UTF-16LE: one two-byte unit held back")
    {
        const std::filesystem::path p = s.dir / "crlf16.log";
        WriteAll(p, std::string("\xFF\xFE", 2) + Utf16Le("a\r\n"));
        auto doc = OpenOrFail(p);
        REQUIRE(doc->Encoding() == Text::TextEncoding::Utf16LE);
        const std::uint64_t changeId = doc->Buffer().ChangeId();
        const std::string ys(2047, 'y');                   // 4094 bytes; bytes 4094..4095 are the CR unit
        AppendAll(p, Utf16Le(ys + "\r\n" + "z\r\n"));

        doc->PollDisk();
        CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "a\n" + ys);
        CHECK(doc->Synced().stamp.size == 8u + 4094u);     // BOM + "a\r\n" = 8 bytes
        doc->PollDisk();
        CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "a\n" + ys + "\nz\n");
        CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().CanUndo());
        CHECK(doc->Buffer().ChangeId() == changeId);
        CHECK_FALSE(doc->Dirty());
        CHECK(doc->AppendCount() == 2u);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("follow: the status strip offers Follow for a .log, or once the file has grown under the document", "[text-follow]")
{
    const ScratchDir s("arcane-te6-follow-available");
    const std::filesystem::path notes = s.dir / "notes.txt";
    const std::filesystem::path log = s.dir / "Game.LOG";

    WriteAll(log, "boot\n");

}
```

Replace TE2-17's `TextDocument::Tick` whole:

```cpp
    void TextDocument::Tick(double dt)
    {
        // Follow polls faster (spec s3.5: a followed log should feel live); every other
        // open document is checked at the watch cadence. Both read the same poll.
        const TextSettings& s = Arcane::Settings<TextSettings>();
        const double interval = Follow() ? s.followPollSeconds : s.watchPollSeconds;
        m_pollElapsed += dt;
        if (m_pollElapsed < interval)
            return;
        m_pollElapsed = 0.0;
        PollDisk();
    }
```

In TE2-17's `TextDocument::ObserveDisk(const FileStamp& now) const`, replace the `if (seen.change == DiskChange::Appended) { ... }` block (the tail read) whole -- everything before it (the window read and hash, `ClassifyDiskChange`) stays TE2-17's, and so do `PollDisk`'s D-R10 settling rule for replacements, `ActOnDisk` (`NoteExternalWrite`, the `DecideDiskAction` switch) and `AppendTail` (the `Text::DecodeFragment` decode in the document's encoding, the synced state advanced by the consumed bytes only):

```cpp
        if (seen.change == DiskChange::Appended)
        {
            // TE6-3: one poll reads at most editor.text.followChunkKB of the tail, Follow or
            // not -- a burst never stalls a frame; the rest arrives on the next polls, and the
            // document stays clean (AppendTail advances the synced size only by what it appended).
            const std::uint64_t available = now.size - oldSize;
            const std::uint64_t cap = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::max<std::uint32_t>(1u, Arcane::Settings<TextSettings>().followChunkKB)) * 1024u;
            const std::uint64_t take = std::min(available, cap);
            if (std::optional<std::string> t = ReadRangeShared(m_canonical, oldSize, take))
            {
                seen.tail = std::move(*t);
                seen.tail.resize(CompleteTailLength(seen.tail, Encoding()));   // a partial character waits for the next poll
                if (take < available && !seen.tail.empty() && LastUnitOf(seen.tail, Encoding()) == u'\r')
                {
                    // Our own cut must never split a CRLF: a CR held back here arrives with its LF
                    // on the next poll. Left in, the next tail would start with LF after a CR and
                    // TailSplitsCrLf would turn a plain append into a full reload.
                    const Text::TextEncoding enc = Encoding();
                    const bool utf16 = enc == Text::TextEncoding::Utf16LE || enc == Text::TextEncoding::Utf16BE;
                    seen.tail.resize(seen.tail.size() - (utf16 ? 2u : 1u));
                }
                seen.splitsCrLf = TailSplitsCrLf(m_synced.lastUnit, seen.tail, Encoding());
            }
            else
                seen.change = DiskChange::Rewritten;   // the tail could not be read: treat it as a replacement
        }
```

(`oldSize` is TE2-17's `m_synced.stamp.size`, captured at the top of `ObserveDisk`. `seen.tail` now holds complete characters only, so `AppendTail`'s own `CompleteTailLength` trim is a no-op on it. An empty `seen.tail` after the trims is TE2-17's "only a partial character so far" case: `AppendTail` returns without touching the synced state, and the next poll reads it whole. With `followChunkKB >= 1` the cap is at least 1024 bytes, so a trim can only empty a tail the writer itself left incomplete. `TextDocument.cpp` already includes `<algorithm>` for TE2-17's `std::min`.)

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/View/TextModel.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextStatusStrip.hpp"

#include <imgui_internal.h>

    struct ImGuiHarness   // TE2-13's bare-context harness
    {
        ImGuiContext* prev = ImGui::GetCurrentContext();
        ImGuiContext* ctx = ImGui::CreateContext();
        ImGuiHarness()
        {
            ImGui::SetCurrentContext(ctx);
            ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO();
            io.DisplaySize = ImVec2(1024, 768);
            io.IniFilename = nullptr;
            unsigned char* px = nullptr;
            int w = 0, h = 0;
            io.Fonts->GetTexDataAsRGBA32(&px, &w, &h);
        }
        ~ImGuiHarness()
        {
            ImGui::DestroyContext(ctx);
            ImGui::SetCurrentContext(prev);
        }
        void Frame(const std::function<void()>& body)
        {
            ImGui::GetIO().DeltaTime = 1.0f / 60.0f;
            ImGui::NewFrame();
            ImGui::SetNextWindowPos(ImVec2(0, 0));
            ImGui::SetNextWindowSize(ImVec2(600, 400));
            ImGui::Begin("doc", nullptr, ImGuiWindowFlags_NoTitleBar | ImGuiWindowFlags_NoSavedSettings);
            body();
            ImGui::End();
            ImGui::Render();
        }
    };

    std::string Rows(int n)
    {
        std::string s;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) s += "row " + std::to_string(i) + "\n";
        return s;   // n + 1 display rows (the empty last one)
    }

    std::filesystem::path WriteTemp(const char* name, const std::string& text)
    {
        const std::filesystem::path p = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / name;
        std::ofstream(p, std::ios::binary) << text;
        return p;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("follow toggle: text.toggleFollow is a TextDocument row, unbound by default, registered and conflict-free", "[text-follow]")
{
    const auto it = std::find_if(kTextActionTable.begin(), kTextActionTable.end(),
                                 [](const TextActionRow& r) { return r.desc.id == "text.toggleFollow"; });
    REQUIRE(it != kTextActionTable.end());
    CHECK(it->action == TextAction::ToggleFollow);
    CHECK(FindTextAction(TextAction::ToggleFollow) == &*it);
    CHECK(it->desc.context == ActionContext::TextDocument);
    CHECK_FALSE(it->repeats);
    const auto chord = ParseKeyChord(it->desc.defaultChord);
    REQUIRE(chord.has_value());
    CHECK_FALSE(chord->Bound());                           // Ctrl+Shift+F stays free for spec 2's Find in Files
    for (const EditorActionDesc& d : kEditorActionTable) { INFO(d.id); CHECK(d.id != "text.toggleFollow"); }

    CVarRegistry reg;
    EditorActions actions(reg);
    RegisterEditorActions(actions);
    CHECK_FALSE(reg.Find("editor.keys.text.toggleFollow").IsStale());   // rebindable from the Shortcuts page
    CHECK(actions.ConflictsOf("text.toggleFollow").empty());
}

TEST_CASE("follow toggle: after a view frame, Follow survives unless the user scrolled away from the end", "[text-follow]")
{
    CHECK(FollowAfterViewFrame(true, /*userScrolled*/false, /*atEnd*/true));
    CHECK(FollowAfterViewFrame(true, false, false));            // an append moved the end; the next append chases it
    CHECK_FALSE(FollowAfterViewFrame(true, true, false));       // the user scrolled up: off
    CHECK(FollowAfterViewFrame(true, true, true));              // scrolling while at the end keeps it
    CHECK_FALSE(FollowAfterViewFrame(false, false, true));      // never turns itself on
    CHECK_FALSE(FollowAfterViewFrame(false, true, false));
}

TEST_CASE("follow view: ScrollToEnd puts the last row in view at the next Draw; AtEnd reads it", "[text-follow][text-view]")
{
    ImGuiHarness h;
    TextModel model(Rope::FromUtf8(Rows(200)));
    TextEditorView view(model);
    const auto draw = [&] { h.Frame([&] { view.Draw("##tv", ImVec2(0, 0), false); }); };
    draw();
    REQUIRE(view.VisibleRowCount() > 0u);
    REQUIRE(view.VisibleRowCount() < view.Display().DisplayRowCount());
    CHECK(view.FirstVisibleDisplayRow() == 0u);
    CHECK_FALSE(view.AtEnd());

    view.ScrollToEnd();
    CHECK(view.AtEnd());                                    // a pending ScrollToEnd counts
    draw();
    CHECK(view.AtEnd());
    CHECK(view.FirstVisibleDisplayRow() > 0u);
    CHECK(view.FirstVisibleDisplayRow() + view.VisibleRowCount() >= view.Display().DisplayRowCount());
    CHECK_FALSE(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());              // a programmatic scroll is never the user's
    draw();
    CHECK(view.AtEnd());                                    // ImGui's own clamp next frame keeps the end in view

    model.buffer.AppendExternal("more 1\nmore 2\nmore 3\n");   // the file grew: the end moved away
    draw();
    CHECK_FALSE(view.AtEnd());
    CHECK_FALSE(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());
    view.ScrollToEnd();
    draw();
    CHECK(view.AtEnd());

    TextModel shortModel(Rope::FromUtf8("a\nb\n"));
    TextEditorView shortView(shortModel);
    h.Frame([&] { shortView.Draw("##short", ImVec2(0, 0), false); });
    CHECK(shortView.AtEnd());                               // everything fits: the end is in view
}

TEST_CASE("follow view: a wheel scroll is the user's for one frame; a reveal asked from input counts when it lands", "[text-follow][text-view]")
{
    ImGuiHarness h;
    TextModel model(Rope::FromUtf8(Rows(200)));
    TextEditorView view(model);
    const auto draw = [&] { h.Frame([&] { view.Draw("##tv", ImVec2(0, 0), false); }); };
    draw();
    view.ScrollToEnd();
    draw();
    REQUIRE(view.AtEnd());

    ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO();
    const TextViewFacts f = view.Facts();
    io.AddMousePosEvent(f.clipMin.x + f.gutterWidth + 40.0f, f.clipMin.y + 40.0f);
    draw();                                                 // the hover lands
    CHECK_FALSE(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());
    io.AddMouseWheelEvent(0.0f, 3.0f);                      // wheel up
    draw();
    CHECK(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());
    CHECK_FALSE(view.AtEnd());
    draw();
    CHECK_FALSE(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());              // cleared at the start of the next Draw

    view.ScrollToEnd();
    draw();
    REQUIRE(view.AtEnd());
    {
        const TextEditorView::UserInputScope input(view);   // what DrawOneView opens around the user's chords
        view.RevealOffset(0, false);                        // Ctrl+Home / PageUp through EnsureCursorVisible
    }
    draw();                                                 // the view asks ImGui for the scroll...
    draw();                                                 // ...which lands in this frame's Begin
    CHECK(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());
    CHECK(view.FirstVisibleDisplayRow() == 0u);
    CHECK_FALSE(view.AtEnd());
}

TEST_CASE("follow view: a programmatic reveal or top-row jump is never the user's scroll (finding 6.17)", "[text-follow][text-view]")
{
    ImGuiHarness h;
    TextModel model(Rope::FromUtf8(Rows(200)));
    TextEditorView view(model);
    const auto draw = [&] { h.Frame([&] { view.Draw("##tv", ImVec2(0, 0), false); }); };
    draw();
    view.ScrollToEnd();
    draw();
    REQUIRE(view.AtEnd());

    view.RevealOffset(model.buffer.Text().LineStart(20), true);   // a find result / GoTo / OpenAt: no input scope open
    draw();
    draw();
    CHECK(view.FirstVisibleDisplayRow() < 20u);             // it did scroll...
    CHECK_FALSE(view.AtEnd());
    CHECK_FALSE(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());              // ...but not as the user

    view.ScrollToEnd();
    draw();
    REQUIRE(view.AtEnd());
    view.SetFirstVisibleDisplayRow(0);                      // session restore's top row
    draw();
    CHECK(view.FirstVisibleDisplayRow() == 0u);
    CHECK_FALSE(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());

    view.ScrollToEnd();
    draw();
    REQUIRE(view.AtEnd());
    {
        const TextEditorView::UserInputScope input(view);   // vim's Ctrl-E / zt arrive through the key interceptor, inside HandleKeyboard's scope
        view.SetFirstVisibleDisplayRow(10);
    }
    draw();
    CHECK(view.FirstVisibleDisplayRow() == 10u);
    CHECK(view.UserScrolledThisFrame());                    // a top row the user's key asked for counts
}

TEST_CASE("follow toggle: RunTextAction(ToggleFollow) flips Follow; turning it on asks the primary view for the end", "[text-follow]")

TEST_CASE("follow toggle: scrolling the primary view away from the end turns Follow off; frames without a user scroll keep it", "[text-follow]")
{
    const std::filesystem::path p = WriteTemp("te6-auto-unfollow.log", Rows(200));
    std::string error;
    auto doc = TextDocument::Open(p, {}, error);
    REQUIRE(doc);
    ImGuiContext* prev = ImGui::GetCurrentContext();
    ImGuiContext* ctx = ImGui::CreateContext();
    ImGui::SetCurrentContext(ctx);
    ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO();
    io.DisplaySize = ImVec2(1280, 800);
    io.IniFilename = nullptr;
    unsigned char* px = nullptr; int w = 0, h = 0;
    io.Fonts->GetTexDataAsRGBA32(&px, &w, &h);

        io.DeltaTime = 1.0f / 60.0f;
        ImGui::NewFrame();
        ImGui::SetNextWindowSize(ImVec2(900, 600), ImGuiCond_Always);
        bool close = false;
        doc->Draw(close);
        ImGui::Render();
    };

    frame();                                                // the document settles (open-time focus, layout)
    doc->SetFollow(true);
    frame();
    frame();
    CHECK(doc->Follow());                                   // no user scroll: it stays on
    CHECK(doc->View().AtEnd());

    doc->GoTo(Text::Point{ 0, 0 });                         // programmatic: a Console link / Go to Line confirm / find result
    frame();
    frame();
    CHECK(doc->Follow());                                   // finding 6.17: a reveal no input asked for never stops the chase

    doc->SetFollow(true);                                   // (still on) back to the end
    frame();
    frame();
    REQUIRE(doc->View().AtEnd());
    {
        const TextEditorView::UserInputScope input(doc->View());   // a navigation key's reveal to the top
        doc->View().RevealOffset(0, false);
    }
    frame();
    frame();
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Follow());                             // tail -f: reading back stops the chase

    doc->SetFollow(true);                                   // back on: scrolls to the end again
    frame();
    frame();
    CHECK(doc->Follow());
    CHECK(doc->View().AtEnd());

    doc.reset();
    ImGui::DestroyContext(ctx);
    ImGui::SetCurrentContext(prev);
    std::filesystem::remove(p);
}
```

### Task TE6-5: Witness -- another process writes the log without delete sharing; follow while it is still writing, rotation, truncation, dirty growth (spec s11.4)

**Files:**
- Create: `ArcaneTests/text-writer-fixture/TextWriterFixtureMain.cpp`. This is a dependency-free Win32 console app, the same shape as `arcbuild-process-fixture`.
- Modify: `premake5.lua`:
  - a new `project "text-writer-fixture"`, inside an `if os.target() == "windows" then ... end` block after `death-fixture` (same filters as `arcbuild-process-fixture`, `premake5.lua:457-488`);
  - `dependson { "text-writer-fixture" }` in `project "ArcaneTests"`;
  - an ArcaneTests postbuild `COPYFILE` of `bin/<cfg>/text-writer-fixture/text-writer-fixture.exe` beside `ArcaneTests.exe`, using the same `{COPYFILE}` form the ArcaneTests block already uses for `automation-exclusions.json` (`premake5.lua:1884-1888`).
- Create: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/Helpers/ChildProcess.hpp`: a running child process, CreateProcessW with no window, `Wait(ms)`, `ExitCode()`.
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/TextFollowWitnessTest.cpp`, tags `[witness][text]`. These cases run in the `~[gpu]` pass and in the gate's `[witness]~[shell]` pass. They need no GPU.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - TE2-15 `TextDocument::Open(path, TextDocumentServices, std::string& error)`, `Buffer()`, `Model()`, `View()`, `Banner()` (`TextBanner::kind`, `TextBannerKind::ChangedOnDisk`);
  - TE2-16 `Save()`, `SetFollow(bool)` / `Follow()`; TE2-17 `Tick(double dt)`, `PollDisk()` (CANON A7), with D-R10's settling rule (a pending stamp that differs from the last only by growth settles at once; a rotation or truncation settles when two consecutive polls agree, or at `editor.text.follow.maxDebounceMs`) -- TE6-5 is D-R10's witness;
  - TE6-3's Follow cadence (`followPollSeconds`, 0.25 s) and TE6-4's `SetFollow(true)` -> `View().ScrollToEnd()` (headless here: a pending request, harmless);
  - TE1 `TextBuffer::{Dirty, ChangeId, CanUndo, Undo(SelectionSet&), Text}`, `Rope::ToString`; TE1 `Text::TextCommands`; TE2-11 `DefaultEditContext(TextModel&)`.
- Produces:
  - `text-writer-fixture.exe`. It takes `--file <p> --share rw|rwd` followed by ops, executed in order:
    - `--append <text>` (`\n` in the text is a newline);
    - `--signal <name>`: creates `<p>.<name>`;
    - `--wait <name>`: waits up to 30 s for `<p>.<name>`, exit 4 on timeout;
    - `--rotate`: close, `MoveFileExW(p, p.1, MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)`, reopen with `CREATE_ALWAYS`;
    - `--truncate`: a second, short-lived `GENERIC_WRITE` handle opened `TRUNCATE_EXISTING` (the append handle cannot `SetEndOfFile`: it has no `FILE_WRITE_DATA`), closed at once; the append handle keeps writing at the new end;
    - `--hold <ms>`.
  - The writer's handle is `FILE_APPEND_DATA | SYNCHRONIZE` and nothing else (finding 6.8). `GENERIC_WRITE` includes `FILE_WRITE_DATA`, and a handle with `FILE_WRITE_DATA` writes at its own file pointer (offset 0 here), overwriting the log instead of appending. With `FILE_APPEND_DATA` alone every `WriteFile` lands at the current end of file, as a logger's `O_APPEND` / `fopen("a")` does.
  - Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 bad args, 3 Win32 failure (message on stderr with `GetLastError`), 4 wait timeout.
  - `Arcane::Test::ChildProcess` (`Started`, `Wait(ms)`, `ExitCode`).

Why this is a witness in the test process rather than a host run: the editor host has no way to type or watch a document from automation. The behaviour under test is entirely `TextDocument`'s disk poll (TE2-17) with Follow's cadence and chunk cap (TE6-3) against a real second process, real sharing modes, a real rename and a real truncation. The host adds only drawing, which TE6-23's log golden covers. The process boundary is the part that matters, so it is real.

TF-W4 is the witness reinforcement of CANON Review Focus F1 ("Follow never shows a log that is still being written"): TE2-17's own test (CANON C TE2 #12) grows a file between polls in-process; TF-W4 has a second process append a line every 100 ms for 3 s and requires the lines in the buffer while that process is still running.

The pump polls MORE SLOWLY than the writer writes (every 250 ms against a write every 100 ms, D-R10, finding 6.9), so two consecutive polls never see the same stamp while the writer runs. A poll every ~20 ms would see equal stamps between writes, and an append path that wrongly waited for two equal stamps would still pass. TF-W5 is D-R10's rotation-path witness (finding 2.8): a game truncates its log at start and then writes every 100 ms; the truncation must reload while the writer is still writing, not after it stops.

```cpp
// sharing), follow it while it grows, survive a rotation and a truncation";

// TF-W4 (CANON F1): lines appear while the writer is still writing.

#include "Text/Helpers/ChildProcess.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Core/TextCommands.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Document/TextDocument.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextModel.hpp"

{
    std::filesystem::path FixtureExe() { return std::filesystem::current_path() / "text-writer-fixture.exe"; }
    std::filesystem::path Dir()
    {
        const auto d = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "arcane-text-follow-witness";
        std::error_code ec;
        std::filesystem::remove_all(d, ec);
        std::filesystem::create_directories(d);
        return d;
    }
    void Touch(const std::filesystem::path& p) { std::ofstream(p).put('x'); }
    bool Exists(const std::filesystem::path& p) { return std::filesystem::exists(p); }

    std::unique_ptr<TextDocument> OpenOrFail(const std::filesystem::path& p)
    {
        std::string error;
        std::unique_ptr<TextDocument> doc = TextDocument::Open(p, {}, error);
        INFO(error);
        REQUIRE(doc != nullptr);
        return doc;
    }

    // One poll every 250 ms: SLOWER than the fixture's 100 ms writes, so while a
    // writer runs no two consecutive polls see the same stamp (D-R10, finding 6.9).
    constexpr auto kPumpEvery = std::chrono::milliseconds(250);

    // Ticks the document (TE2-17's poll; Follow's 0.25 s cadence when on) until `pred` holds or 10 s pass.
    template <class Pred> bool PumpUntil(TextDocument& doc, Pred pred)
    {
        const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(10);
        while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline)
        {
            doc.Tick(0.3);                                   // > followPollSeconds: every tick polls under Follow
            if (pred()) return true;
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(kPumpEvery);
        }
        return false;
    }
    std::string TextOf(TextDocument& d) { return d.Buffer().Text().ToString(); }

    // One user edit at the primary cursor through TE1's commands (one undo step).
    void Type(TextDocument& doc, std::string_view text)
    {
        Text::TextCommands(doc.Buffer(), doc.Model().selections, DefaultEditContext(doc.Model())).InsertText(text);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("TF-W1: follow a log another process writes (no delete sharing) through growth, rotation and truncation", "[witness][text]")
{
    const auto dir = Dir();
    const auto log = dir / "game.log";
    { std::ofstream(log, std::ios::binary) << "[info] boot\n"; }

    auto doc = OpenOrFail(log);
    doc->SetFollow(true);

    Test::ChildProcess writer(FixtureExe(), {
        "--file", log.string(), "--share", "rw",
        "--wait", "opened",
        "--append", "[warn] one\\n", "--signal", "s1", "--wait", "g1",
        "--rotate", "--append", "[info] fresh\\n", "--signal", "s2", "--wait", "g2",
        "--append", "[info] more\\n", "--truncate", "--append", "[error] after truncate\\n", "--signal", "s3",
        "--hold", "500" });
    REQUIRE(writer.Started());
    Touch(log.string() + ".opened");

    // growth: appended, still clean, nothing on the undo stack
    REQUIRE(PumpUntil(*doc, [&] { return TextOf(*doc) == "[info] boot\n[warn] one\n"; }));
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().CanUndo());                    // an append is not an undo entry (s3.5)
    Touch(log.string() + ".g1");

    // rotation: game.log was renamed to game.log.1 and re-created -> a reload, not an append
    REQUIRE(PumpUntil(*doc, [&] { return TextOf(*doc) == "[info] fresh\n"; }));
    CHECK(Exists(dir / "game.log.1"));
    CHECK(doc->Follow());                                    // a rotation does not stop following
    Touch(log.string() + ".g2");

    // truncation (then new text): a reload to the truncated-then-appended content
    REQUIRE(PumpUntil(*doc, [&] { return TextOf(*doc) == "[error] after truncate\n"; }));
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());

    REQUIRE(writer.Wait(30000));
    CHECK(writer.ExitCode() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("TF-W2: a dirty document whose file grows shows the banner and appends nothing", "[witness][text]")
{
    const auto dir = Dir();
    const auto log = dir / "notes.txt";
    { std::ofstream(log, std::ios::binary) << "a\n"; }
    auto doc = OpenOrFail(log);

    REQUIRE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());

    Test::ChildProcess writer(FixtureExe(), { "--file", log.string(), "--share", "rw", "--append", "b\\n" });
    REQUIRE(writer.Wait(10000));
    CHECK(writer.ExitCode() == 0);
    doc->PollDisk();
    doc->PollDisk();                                         // a second equal look: whatever TE2-17 debounces has settled
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "Xa\n");                           // nothing appended into a dirty buffer
    CHECK(doc->Banner().kind == TextBannerKind::ChangedOnDisk);   // TE2-17's s5.3 dirty banner
    CHECK(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
}

TEST_CASE("TF-W3: an append to a clean document keeps it clean with its undo history intact", "[witness][text]")
{
    const auto dir = Dir();

    REQUIRE_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
    const std::uint64_t changeId = doc->Buffer().ChangeId();

    Test::ChildProcess writer(FixtureExe(), { "--file", log.string(), "--share", "rw", "--append", "b\\n" });
    REQUIRE(writer.Wait(10000));
    CHECK(writer.ExitCode() == 0);
    doc->PollDisk();
    doc->PollDisk();
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "Xa\nb\n");
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());                      // s3.5: changeId == savedChangeId still
    CHECK(doc->Buffer().ChangeId() == changeId);
    REQUIRE(doc->Buffer().Undo(doc->Model().selections));   // the pre-append edit is still undoable
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc) == "a\nb\n");
}

TEST_CASE("TF-W4: a followed log shows its lines while the writer is still writing them (CANON F1)", "[witness][text]")
{
    const auto dir = Dir();
    const auto log = dir / "live.log";
    { std::ofstream(log, std::ios::binary) << "[info] start\n"; }
    auto doc = OpenOrFail(log);
    doc->SetFollow(true);
    const bool canUndo = doc->Buffer().CanUndo();
    const std::uint64_t changeId = doc->Buffer().ChangeId();

    // One line every 100 ms for 3 s, polled every 250 ms: the stamp changes on EVERY
    // poll, so an append that waited for two equal stamps would show nothing until the end.
    std::vector<std::string> args = { "--file", log.string(), "--share", "rw" };
    std::string expected = "[info] start\n";
    for (int i = 0; i < 30; ++i)
    {
        args.push_back("--append");
        args.push_back("tick " + std::to_string(i) + "\\n");
        args.push_back("--hold");
        args.push_back("100");
        expected += "tick " + std::to_string(i) + "\n";
    }
    Test::ChildProcess writer(FixtureExe(), args);
    REQUIRE(writer.Started());

    REQUIRE(PumpUntil(*doc, [&] { return TextOf(*doc).find("tick 5\n") != std::string::npos; }));
    CHECK_FALSE(writer.Wait(0));                             // the writer is still running (tick 5 lands ~0.6 s into 3 s)
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc).starts_with("[info] start\ntick 0\ntick 1\n"));   // in order, nothing lost or doubled
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
    CHECK(doc->Buffer().CanUndo() == canUndo);               // appends never touch the history
    CHECK(doc->Buffer().ChangeId() == changeId);

    REQUIRE(PumpUntil(*doc, [&] { return TextOf(*doc) == expected; }));
    REQUIRE(writer.Wait(30000));
    CHECK(writer.ExitCode() == 0);
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
    CHECK(doc->Buffer().CanUndo() == canUndo);
    CHECK(doc->Follow());
}

TEST_CASE("TF-W5: a log truncated at start and then written every 100 ms reloads while the writer still writes (D-R10, finding 2.8)", "[witness][text]")
{
    const auto dir = Dir();
    const auto log = dir / "game.log";
    std::string old;
    for (int i = 0; i < 50; ++i) old += "[old] line " + std::to_string(100 + i) + "\n";   // 50 x 15 = 750 bytes: far more than the writer reaches
    REQUIRE(old.size() == 750u);
    { std::ofstream(log, std::ios::binary) << old; }
    auto doc = OpenOrFail(log);
    doc->SetFollow(true);
    REQUIRE(TextOf(*doc) == old);

    // The game's start: truncate, then a line every 100 ms for 3 s. Every poll (250 ms)
    // sees a size below the old one AND a different stamp from the poll before, so a
    // rotation rule that waited for two EQUAL stamps would never reload until the end.
    std::vector<std::string> args = { "--file", log.string(), "--share", "rw", "--truncate" };
    std::string expected;
    for (int i = 0; i < 30; ++i)
    {
        args.push_back("--append");
        args.push_back("new " + std::to_string(10 + i) + "\\n");   // 7 bytes a line: 210 bytes in all, always below 750
        args.push_back("--hold");
        args.push_back("100");
        expected += "new " + std::to_string(10 + i) + "\n";
    }
    Test::ChildProcess writer(FixtureExe(), args);
    REQUIRE(writer.Started());

    REQUIRE(PumpUntil(*doc, [&] { const std::string t = TextOf(*doc); return t.starts_with("new 10\n") && t.find("new 14\n") != std::string::npos; }));
    CHECK_FALSE(writer.Wait(0));                             // still writing: the reload did not wait for the writer to stop
    CHECK(TextOf(*doc).find("[old]") == std::string::npos);  // the truncated text is gone, not merged
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
    CHECK(doc->Follow());                                    // a truncation does not stop following

    REQUIRE(PumpUntil(*doc, [&] { return TextOf(*doc) == expected; }));   // after the reload, growth appends
    REQUIRE(writer.Wait(30000));
    CHECK(writer.ExitCode() == 0);
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
}
```
