```cpp
    {
        VimChordRow Row(VimKey k, std::string_view n, std::string_view v, std::string_view i, std::string_view off,
                        bool cn, bool cv, bool ci)
        {
            return VimChordRow{ k, n, v, i, off, cn, cv, ci };
        }

        const std::array<VimChordRow, 20>& Table()
        {
            static const std::array<VimChordRow, 20> s_rows = {
                Row(VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Esc), "cancel pending", "-> Normal", "-> Normal", "ui.cancel", true, true, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'['), "cancel pending", "-> Normal", "-> Normal", "outdent", true, true, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'z'), "undo", "undo", "undo", "undo", true, true, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'y'), "scroll up 1", "scroll up 1", "redo", "redo", true, true, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'r'), "redo", "redo", "insert register {reg}", "(unbound)", true, true, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'c'), "cancel pending", "copy, -> Normal", "copy", "copy", true, true, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'x'), "decrement number", "decrement", "cut", "cut", true, true, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'a'), "increment number", "increment", "select all (-> Visual)", "select all", true, true, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'v'), "Visual Block", "toggle Visual Block", "paste", "paste", true, true, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'w'), "window prefix", "window prefix", "delete word back", "close document", true, true, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'd'), "half page down", "half page down", "outdent line", "add next match", true, true, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'u'), "half page up", "half page up", "delete to line start", "(unbound)", true, true, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'f'), "page down", "page down", "find", "find", true, true, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'b'), "page up", "page up", "(unbound)", "(unbound)", true, true, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'e'), "scroll down 1", "scroll down 1", "(unbound)", "(unbound)", true, true, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'o'), "jump back", "--", "one Normal command", "open scene", true, false, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'i'), "jump forward", "--", "--", "(unbound)", true, false, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U't'), "--", "--", "indent line", "(unbound)", false, false, true),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U's'), "save", "save", "save", "save", false, false, false),
                Row(VimKey::Ctrl(U'h'), "h", "h", "backspace", "replace", true, true, true),
            };
            return s_rows;
        }
    }

    std::span<const VimChordRow> VimChordTable() { return Table(); }

    bool VimClaimsChord(const VimKey& chord, VimMode mode, const VimOptions& options)
    {
        if (chord.IsEsc()) return true;                       // Esc and Ctrl+[ are vim's whenever vim is on
        if (!chord.ctrl) return true;                         // plain keys are always vim's
        if (!options.handleCtrlKeys) return false;
        if (mode == VimMode::CommandLine) return chord.ch != U's';
        for (const VimChordRow& row : Table())
        {
            if (!(row.chord == chord)) continue;
            switch (mode)
            {
            case VimMode::Visual:
            case VimMode::VisualLine:
            case VimMode::VisualBlock: return row.visualClaimed;
            case VimMode::Insert:
            case VimMode::Replace:     return row.insertClaimed;
            default:                   return row.normalClaimed;
            }
        }
        return false;                                         // a Ctrl chord the table does not list
    }
}
```

```cpp
    VimKeyResult VimState::HandleNormalOrVisual(const VimKey& key)
    {
        if (key.ctrl && !key.alt && key.ch == U'c')          // s6.6: Normal cancels, Visual copies and leaves
        {
            if (IsVisual(m_mode)) CopyVisualToClipboard();
            else m_parser.Reset();
            MaybeRestartInsert();
            return {};
        }
        if (key.IsEsc() && m_parser.Idle())
        {
            if (IsVisual(m_mode)) EndVisualAtHeads();
            MaybeRestartInsert();
            return {};
        }
        switch (m_parser.Feed(key, IsVisual(m_mode) ? m_mode : VimMode::Normal))
        {
        case VimParseStatus::NeedMore:
            return {};
        case VimParseStatus::Invalid:
            m_parser.Reset();
            if (!key.IsEsc()) Beep();
            MaybeRestartInsert();
            return {};
        case VimParseStatus::Complete:
        {
            const VimParsed p = m_parser.Result();
            m_parser.Reset();
            Execute(p);
            MaybeRestartInsert();
            return {};
        }
        }
        return {};
    }
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Vim/VimInsertChords.cpp
// The Insert column of the s6.6 chord table, Normal/Visual Ctrl+C, and the
// Ctrl+W window prefix. Neovim defaults: backspace=indent,eol,start (Ctrl-W /
// Ctrl-U stop once at the insert start), autoindent (Ctrl-U keeps the indent).
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimState.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    VimKeyResult VimState::HandleInsertCtrl(const VimKey& key)
    {
        switch (key.ch)
        {
        case U'w': InsertDeleteWord(); return {};
        case U'u': InsertDeleteLine(); return {};
        case U't': InsertShiftIndent(true); return {};
        case U'd': InsertShiftIndent(false); return {};
        case U'h': InsertBackspace(); return {};
        case U'o': InsertOneNormal(); return {};
        case U'z': InsertUndoRedo(true); return {};
        case U'y': InsertUndoRedo(false); return {};
        default:   return VimKeyResult{ false };   // Ctrl-R{reg}: TE5b-2
        }
    }

    void VimState::InsertDeleteWord()
    {
        const Rope& r = m_doc.buffer.Text();
        const std::vector<Selection> sels = VimText::Selections(m_doc);
        const std::size_t primary = VimText::PrimaryIndex(m_doc);
        const ByteOffset start = m_insert.hasStart ? m_anchors.Get(m_insert.start).offset : 0;
        const auto cls = [&](ByteOffset o) { return m_chars.Class(VimText::CodePointAt(r, o), false); };
        std::vector<EditOp> ops;
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> ids;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < sels.size(); ++i)
        {
            const ByteOffset caret = sels[i].head;
            const std::uint32_t row = VimText::RowOf(r, caret);
            const ByteOffset ls = r.LineStart(row);
            ByteRange del{ caret, caret };
            if (caret == ls)
            {
                if (row > 0) del.begin = caret - 1;               // backspace=eol: join with the line above
            }
            else
            {
                ByteOffset p = caret;
                while (p > ls && cls(VimText::PrevChar(r, p)) == 0) p = VimText::PrevChar(r, p);
                if (p > ls)
                {
                    const int c = cls(VimText::PrevChar(r, p));
                    while (p > ls && cls(VimText::PrevChar(r, p)) == c) p = VimText::PrevChar(r, p);
                }
                if (i == primary && start > p && start < caret && VimText::RowOf(r, start) == row) p = start;   // stop once
                del.begin = p;
            }
            if (!ops.empty() && del.begin < ops.back().range.end) continue;
            ops.push_back(EditOp{ del, "" });
            ids.push_back(sels[i].id);
        }
        std::vector<Selection> after;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < ops.size(); ++i)
        {
            const ByteOffset c = VimText::MapThrough(ops[i].range.begin, ops, Bias::Left);
            after.push_back(Selection{ ids[i], c, c, std::nullopt });
        }
        VimText::Apply(m_doc, std::move(ops), std::move(after), std::min(primary, ids.size() - 1));
        m_insert.autoIndentPending = false;
    }

    void VimState::InsertDeleteLine()
    {
        const Rope& r = m_doc.buffer.Text();
        const std::vector<Selection> sels = VimText::Selections(m_doc);
        const std::size_t primary = VimText::PrimaryIndex(m_doc);
        const ByteOffset start = m_insert.hasStart ? m_anchors.Get(m_insert.start).offset : 0;
        std::vector<EditOp> ops;
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> ids;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < sels.size(); ++i)
        {
            const ByteOffset caret = sels[i].head;
            const std::uint32_t row = VimText::RowOf(r, caret);
            const ByteOffset ls = r.LineStart(row);
            ByteRange del{ caret, caret };
            if (caret == ls)
            {
                if (row > 0) del.begin = caret - 1;
            }
            else
            {
                const ByteOffset fnb = VimText::FirstNonBlank(r, row);
                ByteOffset target = caret > fnb ? fnb : ls;       // autoindent: the indent stays
                if (i == primary && start > target && start < caret && VimText::RowOf(r, start) == row) target = start;   // entered text first
                del.begin = target;
            }
            if (!ops.empty() && del.begin < ops.back().range.end) continue;
            ops.push_back(EditOp{ del, "" });
            ids.push_back(sels[i].id);
        }
        std::vector<Selection> after;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < ops.size(); ++i)
        {
            const ByteOffset c = VimText::MapThrough(ops[i].range.begin, ops, Bias::Left);
            after.push_back(Selection{ ids[i], c, c, std::nullopt });
        }
        VimText::Apply(m_doc, std::move(ops), std::move(after), std::min(primary, ids.size() - 1));
    }

    void VimState::InsertShiftIndent(bool right)
    {
        const Rope& r = m_doc.buffer.Text();
        const std::vector<Selection> sels = VimText::Selections(m_doc);
        const std::uint32_t sw = std::max(1u, m_options.shiftWidth), ts = std::max(1u, m_options.tabSize);
        std::vector<EditOp> ops;
        std::uint32_t lastRow = ~0u;
        for (const Selection& s : sels)
        {
            const std::uint32_t row = VimText::RowOf(r, s.head);
            if (row == lastRow) continue;
            lastRow = row;
            const std::string ws = VimText::LeadingWhitespace(r, row);
            const ByteOffset ls = r.LineStart(row);
            const std::uint32_t vcol = VimText::VirtualColumn(r, ls + ws.size(), ts);
            const std::uint32_t next = right ? (vcol / sw + 1) * sw : (vcol == 0 ? 0 : ((vcol - 1) / sw) * sw);
            std::string indent = m_options.expandTab ? std::string(next, ' ')
                                                     : std::string(next / ts, '\t') + std::string(next % ts, ' ');
            ops.push_back(EditOp{ ByteRange{ ls, ls + ws.size() }, std::move(indent) });
        }
        std::vector<Selection> after;
        for (const Selection& s : sels)
        {
            const ByteOffset c = VimText::MapThrough(s.head, ops, Bias::Right);
            after.push_back(Selection{ s.id, c, c, std::nullopt });
        }
        VimText::Apply(m_doc, std::move(ops), std::move(after), VimText::PrimaryIndex(m_doc));
    }

    void VimState::InsertOneNormal()
    {
        if (m_insert.autoIndentPending) RemovePendingAutoIndent();
        EndInsertSession();
        const Rope& r = m_doc.buffer.Text();
        std::vector<Selection> sels = VimText::Selections(m_doc);
        const std::size_t primary = VimText::PrimaryIndex(m_doc);
        const ByteOffset head = sels[primary].head;
        m_insertRestartEol = VimText::AtLineEnd(r, head) && r.LineStart(VimText::RowOf(r, head)) != head;
        for (Selection& s : sels)
        {
            s.anchor = s.head = VimCursorModel::Clamp(r, s.head);   // the cursor is not moved back (i_CTRL-O)
            s.goalColumn.reset();
        }
        m_insertRestartAt = sels[primary].head;
        m_insertRestart = true;
        m_mode = VimMode::Normal;
        VimText::Select(m_doc, std::move(sels), primary);
    }

    void VimState::MaybeRestartInsert()
    {
        if (!m_insertRestart) return;
        if (m_mode == VimMode::Insert || m_mode == VimMode::Replace) { m_insertRestart = false; return; }   // the command entered Insert itself
        if (m_mode != VimMode::Normal || !m_parser.Idle()) return;   // Visual, command line or a pending command: later
        m_insertRestart = false;
        const Rope& r = m_doc.buffer.Text();
        std::vector<Selection> sels = VimText::Selections(m_doc);
        const std::size_t primary = VimText::PrimaryIndex(m_doc);
        if (m_insertRestartEol && sels.size() == 1 && sels[0].head == m_insertRestartAt)
        {
            const ByteOffset le = r.LineEnd(VimText::RowOf(r, sels[0].head));   // back after the last char
            sels[0].anchor = sels[0].head = le;
        }
        BeginInsertSession(VimActionId::InsertBefore, 1);
        VimText::Select(m_doc, std::move(sels), primary);
        MarkInsertStart();
        m_mode = VimMode::Insert;
    }

    void VimState::InsertUndoRedo(bool undo)
    {
        EndInsertSession();                                      // never undo inside an open transaction
        TextCommands commands(m_doc.buffer, m_doc.selections, m_doc.context ? *m_doc.context : EditContext{});
        const bool ok = undo ? commands.Undo() : commands.Redo();   // through the TextCommands class (CANON C TE5 items 5, 13)
        BeginInsertSession(VimActionId::InsertBefore, 1);
        MarkInsertStart();
        if (!ok) Beep();
    }

    void VimState::CopyVisualToClipboard()
    {
        const Rope& r = m_doc.buffer.Text();
        std::string text;
        if (m_mode == VimMode::VisualLine)
        {
            for (const VimCursor& c : Cursors())
                text += VimCursorModel::LinewiseText(r, VimText::RowOf(r, std::min(c.anchor, c.head)), VimText::RowOf(r, std::max(c.anchor, c.head)));
        }
        else
        {
            bool first = true;
            for (const Selection& s : m_doc.selections.All())
            {
                if (!first) text.push_back('\n');
                first = false;
                std::string piece;
                r.CopyTo(ByteRange{ std::min(s.anchor, s.head), std::max(s.anchor, s.head) }, piece);
                text += piece;
            }
        }
        m_host.WriteClipboard(text);
        EndVisualAtHeads();
    }

    void VimState::RunWindowKey(char32_t key)
    {
        std::optional<VimWindowCommand> cmd;
        switch (key)
        {
        case U'v': cmd = VimWindowCommand::SplitVertical; break;
        case U's': cmd = VimWindowCommand::SplitHorizontal; break;
        case U'h': cmd = VimWindowCommand::FocusLeft; break;
        case U'j': cmd = VimWindowCommand::FocusDown; break;
        case U'k': cmd = VimWindowCommand::FocusUp; break;
        case U'l': cmd = VimWindowCommand::FocusRight; break;
        case U'w': cmd = VimWindowCommand::FocusNext; break;
        case U'c':
        case U'q': cmd = VimWindowCommand::Close; break;
        default: break;
        }
        if (!cmd) { Beep(); return; }
        const VimHostResult result = m_host.RunWindowCommand(*cmd);
        if (!result.message.empty()) m_host.ShowMessage(result.message, !result.ok);
    }
}
```

### Task TE5a-21: `gb` -- add the next match in Normal and Visual (spec s6.2 last bullet, s6.6 "multi-cursor stays reachable", s3.2 maxCursors)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `ResolveTextObject` (TE5a-16), TE1-17 `static std::optional<ByteOffset> TextCommands::FindForward(const Rope&, std::string_view, ByteOffset from)` (the literal scan, chunk-straddling; CANON B25), TE1-17 `bool TextCommands::ConfirmCursorCount(std::size_t requested) const` over `EditContext::maxCursors` (`editor.text.maxCursors`, TE1-17; reached through `VimDoc::context`, TE5a-2 -- `VimOptions` carries no cursor cap of its own), `VimCharClass::IsWord/Class`, TE5a-18 Visual representation, Part A's Visual operators (for the composed `c` check).
- Produces: `VimState::AddNextMatch(const VimParsed&)`, `m_gbWholeWord`; `std::optional<ByteOffset> FindNextLiteral(const Rope&, std::string_view needle, ByteOffset from, bool wholeWord, const VimCharClass&, std::span<const Selection> taken)` (free function in `VimMultiCursor.cpp`, declared in `VimState.hpp`'s namespace scope).

Sublime's Ctrl+D in vim's Normal mode (Ctrl+D is half-page there): `gb` with an empty cursor selects the word under each cursor and enters Visual (whole-word matching from then on, as Sublime does after a word pick); `gb` in Visual adds the next occurrence of the primary selection's text after it, wrapping, skipping text already selected, and makes it the primary. Every vim command then runs once per selection (spec s6.2). The search is TE1-17's `TextCommands::FindForward` (one literal scan for the editor, CANON B25); `FindNextLiteral` adds only gb's filters (whole word, already-selected text) and the single wrap. The limit is TE1-17's gate: `TextCommands(buffer, selections, <view's EditContext>).ConfirmCursorCount(n + 1)` with `editor.text.maxCursors` from the EditContext (`ApplyEditSettings`), so vim and the editor read one value. `gb` adds one at a time; above the limit `ConfirmCursorCount` asks the view's `confirmCursors` hook exactly as the editor's commands do -- vim never clears or replaces it. The adapter's context is `doc.MakeEditContext(model)` with **no rerun action** (TE5a-22), and TE4-24's hook then refuses with the document's note ("Not added: N cursors is more than editor.text.maxCursors (M).") instead of queuing a question, because a vim key has no `text.*` action to re-run; gb also says why in vim's message line and stops. (The s3.2 "asks first" stays with the editor's own Ctrl+D / Alt+F3, which pass their `TextAction` as the rerun.)

```cpp
TEST_CASE("vim gb: FindNextLiteral wraps and skips taken text", "[text-vim-visual]")
{
    const Rope t = Rope::FromUtf8("ab\nxab\nab");
    const VimCharClass chars;
    const std::vector<Selection> none;
    CHECK(FindNextLiteral(t, "ab", 2, false, chars, none) == std::optional<ByteOffset>(4));
    CHECK(FindNextLiteral(t, "ab", 2, true, chars, none) == std::optional<ByteOffset>(7));    // xab is not a whole word
    const std::vector<Selection> taken{ Selection{ 1, 7, 9, std::nullopt } };
    CHECK(FindNextLiteral(t, "ab", 8, true, chars, taken) == std::optional<ByteOffset>(0));    // wraps to the start
    CHECK(FindNextLiteral(t, "b\nx", 0, false, chars, none) == std::optional<ByteOffset>(1));  // multi-line needle
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Vim/VimMultiCursor.cpp
// gb: Sublime's add-next-match, reachable in vim's Normal mode (spec s6.2, s6.6).
// The scan and the cursor limit are TE1-17's (TextCommands::FindForward,
// ConfirmCursorCount); this file adds vim's word pick, whole-word filter and wrap.
#include "TextEditor/Core/TextCommands.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimState.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimTextObjects.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <string>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    namespace
    {
        bool WholeWordAt(const Rope& r, const VimCharClass& chars, ByteOffset b, ByteOffset e)
        {
            if (b > 0)
            {
                const std::uint32_t row = VimText::RowOf(r, b);
                const char32_t before = b > r.LineStart(row) ? VimText::CodePointAt(r, VimText::PrevChar(r, b)) : U'\n';
                if (chars.IsWord(before)) return false;
            }
            return !chars.IsWord(VimText::CodePointAt(r, e));
        }
    }

    std::optional<ByteOffset> FindNextLiteral(const Rope& r, std::string_view needle, ByteOffset from, bool wholeWord,
                                              const VimCharClass& chars, std::span<const Selection> taken)
    {
        if (needle.empty()) return std::nullopt;
        const auto acceptable = [&](ByteOffset a) {
            const ByteOffset e = a + needle.size();
            for (const Selection& s : taken)
                if (a < std::max(s.anchor, s.head) && e > std::min(s.anchor, s.head)) return false;
            return !wholeWord || WholeWordAt(r, chars, a, e);
        };
        // TE1-17's literal scan (chunk-straddling, multi-line needles included); gb only filters its hits
        const auto scan = [&](ByteOffset start, ByteOffset limit) -> std::optional<ByteOffset> {
            for (std::optional<ByteOffset> hit = TextCommands::FindForward(r, needle, start); hit && *hit < limit;
                 hit = TextCommands::FindForward(r, needle, *hit + 1))
                if (acceptable(*hit)) return hit;
            return std::nullopt;
        };
        if (const std::optional<ByteOffset> hit = scan(from, r.Size() + 1)) return hit;
        return scan(0, from);                                    // wrapped once: only matches starting before `from`
    }

    void VimState::AddNextMatch(const VimParsed& p)
    {
        const Rope& r = m_doc.buffer.Text();
        if (m_mode == VimMode::Normal)
        {
            VimContext ctx = Context();
            std::vector<Selection> sels = VimText::Selections(m_doc);
            bool any = false;
            for (Selection& s : sels)
            {
                if (m_chars.Class(VimText::CodePointAt(r, s.head), false) == 0) continue;   // on blanks: no word
                const auto obj = ResolveTextObject(ctx, ByteRange{ s.head, s.head }, s.head, VimObjectArgs{ VimObjectId::Word, true, 1, false });
                if (!obj || obj->range.begin == obj->range.end) continue;
                s.anchor = obj->range.begin;
                s.head = obj->range.end;                          // the Visual (inclusive) editor range of the word
                s.goalColumn.reset();
                any = true;
            }
            if (!any) { Beep(); return; }
            m_mode = VimMode::Visual;
            m_gbWholeWord = true;
            VimText::Select(m_doc, std::move(sels), VimText::PrimaryIndex(m_doc));
            return;
        }
        if (m_mode != VimMode::Visual) { Beep(); return; }
        // TE1-17's gate over the view's EditContext (editor.text.maxCursors) and its confirmCursors hook,
        // used as is: the adapter builds it with MakeEditContext(model) and no rerun action, so TE4-24's
        // hook refuses with a note (never a question) -- vim never clears or replaces it.
        const EditContext gate = m_doc.context ? *m_doc.context : EditContext{};
        for (std::uint32_t n = 0; n < p.Count1(); ++n)
        {
            std::vector<Selection> sels = VimText::Selections(m_doc);
            if (!TextCommands(m_doc.buffer, m_doc.selections, gate).ConfirmCursorCount(sels.size() + 1))
            {
                m_host.ShowMessage("gb: " + std::to_string(gate.maxCursors) + " cursors is the limit (editor.text.maxCursors)", true);
                return;
            }
            const Selection& primary = sels[VimText::PrimaryIndex(m_doc)];
            const ByteOffset lo = std::min(primary.anchor, primary.head), hi = std::max(primary.anchor, primary.head);
            if (lo == hi) { Beep(); return; }
            std::string needle;
            r.CopyTo(ByteRange{ lo, hi }, needle);
            const std::optional<ByteOffset> at = FindNextLiteral(r, needle, hi, m_gbWholeWord, m_chars, sels);
            if (!at) { m_host.ShowMessage("gb: no more matches", false); return; }
            sels.push_back(Selection{ m_doc.selections.AllocateId(), *at, *at + needle.size(), std::nullopt });
            const std::size_t newest = sels.size() - 1;           // the newest selection is the primary (spec s3.4)
            VimText::Select(m_doc, std::move(sels), newest);
        }
    }
}
```

The keyboard rules (spec s5.5, D-R1): in Normal, Visual and operator-pending modes vim asks TE2-10's `TextInputHook` for command keys -- dead keys arrive bare with the layout's dead state cleared (`SetCommandMode(true)`), the IME is off (`SetImeAllowed(false)`, which TE2-10 makes a real IME-context disassociation that `PollFrame` re-applies every frame, CANON B24), and letters come from the key's Latin letter when `editor.text.vim.latinLettersInNormal` resolves to on (TE5a-23). **While a pending command waits for a LITERAL character** -- `f t F T r` (`VimCommandParser::AwaitingLiteral`) -- command mode is OFF (`VimState::Keyboard()` reports `commandKeys = false`, D-R15, finding 5a.20), so a dead key composes: French `f` `^` `e` is `fê`, and `rê` replaces with `ê`; the Latin-letter path is off with it (it only exists in command mode, where the hook owns the stream). Replace mode's characters are Replace-mode text (the text keyboard, below); Insert-mode `Ctrl-K` digraphs are not implemented (spec s6.3 lists no digraph input), and if added their two characters are literals too. **A NAME argument keeps command mode ON (D-R15):** marks (`m ' `` ` ``), registers (`" q @`, Insert `Ctrl-R` -- TE5b-2 -- and the command line's `Ctrl-R`) and Ctrl-W's command (`VimCommandParser::AwaitingName`): spec s5.5 makes those Latin on any layout, as vim users expect. Insert, Replace and the command line get the text keyboard: composition and IME on. The keyboard state is pushed into the hook from `VimState::ApplyModeHooks` -> `IVimHost::SetKeyboard` at the end of every `HandleKey`, so `SetImeAllowed(false)` on entering Normal/Visual/operator-pending lands BEFORE vim handles the next key (D-R1). The Latin-letter path is Arcane's own addition to TE2-10's hook: in command mode, on a letter `WM_KEYDOWN` without Ctrl/Alt (read with `GetKeyState`, which is the thread's key state as of that message -- ImGui's `io.KeyCtrl/KeyAlt/KeyShift` lag a frame inside the message pump and carry no Caps Lock toggle) it records the VK's Latin letter as a `Char` event through TE2-10's `Record` (so it carries `seq = NextTextInputSeq()` and `fromCommandHook = true` and sits in the ONE ordered stream `TakeCommandModeEvents` drains) and swallows the layout's `WM_CHAR` / `WM_DEADCHAR` for that keystroke; the key-down itself passes on, so SDL's key state stays right.

**One ordered stream into vim (D-R1, finding 5a.17).** The view no longer feeds vim chords, then named keys, then characters: `DispatchTextEvents` walks the frame's `TextInputFrame::events` front to back and offers EACH event to the key interceptor at its place in the stream, after inserting the text typed so far, so `ix<Esc>` arriving in one slow frame types `x` in Insert and then leaves Insert. **Ctrl chords ride the same stream (A12):** TE2-10 records a Ctrl+letter / Ctrl+[ press as a `Key` event whose `TextKeyPress::chordChar` names the character key, at its place in arrival order (ImGui's queue outside command mode, the hook's `WM_KEYDOWN` in command mode), so `ix<C-[>l` in one frame leaves Insert between `x` and `l` exactly as typed -- there is no chord-first residual. `DispatchTextEvents` offers a chord event to `interceptor.chord` (as `ChordOfCharKey`'s `KeyChord`) and records a consumed one in `consumedChords`; an unconsumed chord is never a baseline key -- it stays the action table's (`EditorActions` reads chords on its own route, gated by the chord claim below).

**A chord vim claims fires nowhere else (finding 5a.18).** `ChordConsumed` gated only the `text.*` rows and the shared verbs; a Global row bound to the same chord (Ctrl+O -> open scene, Esc -> `ui.cancel`) still fired, and Global shortcuts are read in `EditorApp::FrameInput`, BEFORE the documents draw. So `EditorActions` gains an owner-tagged chord claim: the adapter whose view holds the keyboard installs `VimClaimsKeyChord(chord, mode, options)` (every bare or Shift key that types or names a vim key, and the Ctrl chords `VimClaimsChord` gives vim in the current mode), `Fired` / `Down` / `PressedInWindow` answer false for a claimed chord in EVERY context, and `VimEditorRuntime::FrameBoundary` (TE5a-23) clears the claim when no vim view holds the keyboard. Alt/Super chords, F-keys, Ctrl+named keys and every chord vim does not claim (Ctrl+S, Insert Ctrl+V) stay the editor's.

The hook is process-wide: the adapter whose view holds the keyboard pushes vim's keyboard state into it (`Tick`, every frame, after the mode may have changed), and `VimEditorRuntime::FrameBoundary` (TE5a-23) resets it to the text keyboard (`ResetTextKeyboard`: `SetCommandMode(false)` + `SetImeAllowed(true)`) whenever no vim view holds the keyboard, so a plain text view or another widget never inherits command mode. That reset is the focus-loss rule: TE2-10's `PollFrame` re-applies `!ImeAllowed()` every frame, so without it the IME would stay disassociated from whatever widget took the keyboard. `FrameBoundary` runs after `DocumentHost::DrawAll` and before the next frame's `EditorApp::PumpFrameEvents` -> `PollFrame`, so the IME is back before the next keystroke reaches IMM; a vim adapter's own destructor does the same when its view held the keyboard.

The adapter is the one place TE2/TE4/TE7 names are consumed by the vim layer. Every document and window operation a vim command asks for (`:q`, `:e`, `:sp`, `Ctrl-W c`, `:bn`, a global mark in another file) is **deferred** (`TakeDeferred`) and run by `VimEditorRuntime` at the frame boundary (TE5a-23), never inside the key dispatch: closing a document there would destroy the adapter and the `VimState` that is still on the call stack, and opening one would grow `DocumentHost`'s list while `DrawAll` iterates it. Files open only through `Services::openText` (TE7's `FileOpener`, CANON A10), never `DocumentHost::OpenAt`.

Each view's `VimDoc` is built over `doc.ModelOf(view)` (TE4-17: that view's `TextModel` -- buffer, selections, folds, display) with `VimDoc::context = &m_context`, an `EditContext` member the adapter refreshes from `doc.MakeEditContext(model)` (TE4-24) when it attaches, when settings publish (`VimEditorRuntime::OnSettingsPublished` calls `RefreshContext`) and once per frame before vim handles that frame's first key -- so vim's commands get the document's indentation, word characters, comment tokens, cursor limit and cursor-confirm hook exactly as the default bindings do. The adapter passes **no rerun action** (`MakeEditContext(model)`, never `MakeEditContext(model, action)`): TE4-24's hook then turns a refused cursor count into the document's note, never a Yes/No question, and vim (`gb`, TE5a-21, and every multi-cursor path) uses that hook as is -- it never clears or replaces `confirmCursors`.

hlsearch (CANON B19): the adapter owns a second `SearchHighlightOverlay` (the find bar owns the first), attached with `view.AddOverlay` and removed on detach, fed by its own `VisibleMatchCache` over a `CompiledQuery` built from `SearchQuery{ text = <the translated pcre2>, regex = true, caseSensitive = true, forceMultiline = translated.multiline }`. `IVimHost::SetSearchHighlight` (TE5a-5) carries only the translated pcre2 string; TE5c-1's `VimPattern::Translate` puts `(?m)` first exactly when `TranslatedPattern::multiline` is set, so the adapter reads the flag back as `pcre2.starts_with("(?m)")`. Like the find bar, a multi-line query is not painted (`VisibleMatchCache` is the single-line path), and neither are vim's `\%V` / `\%23l` predicates (TE5c-16's `VimDivergences()` rows).

```cpp
// ArcaneTests/src/Helpers/TextInputScript.hpp
#pragma once

// Test seam for TE2-10's TextInputHook (CANON A8, TE5a-22): a real keyboard
// layout loaded the way TE2-10's ScopedLayout test helper does it, and each
// keystroke played as the synthetic MSG sequence Windows produces -- the
// WM_KEYDOWN, then the WM_DEADCHAR / WM_CHAR TranslateMessage would post
// (computed with ToUnicodeEx on that layout, dead-key state kept) -- every one
// fed to TextInputHook::OnMessage. What the view would read is returned through
// TE2-10's own BuildTextInputFrame over ONE ordered stream (D-R1): the events
// the hook recorded when it owned the stream (command mode), else the
// characters SDL would have queued, each stamped with NextTextInputSeq().

#include "TextEditor/Core/Utf8.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextInput.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextInputHook.hpp"

#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#ifndef NOMINMAX
#define NOMINMAX
#endif
#include <windows.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Test
{
    // The frame's characters as UTF-8, in stream order (Key events skipped): what the tests compare.
    inline std::string FrameText(const Editor::TextInputFrame& frame)
    {
        std::string out;
        for (const Editor::TextInputEvent& e : frame.events)
            if (e.kind == Editor::TextInputEventKind::Char) Text::Utf8::Append(out, e.ch);
        return out;
    }

    // TE2-10's ScopedLayout pattern: loads the layout, unloads it only when this scope loaded it.
    class ScopedTestLayout
    {
    public:
        ScopedTestLayout(const wchar_t* klid, WORD expectedLanguage)
        {
            const int count = ::GetKeyboardLayoutList(0, nullptr);
            std::vector<HKL> before(static_cast<std::size_t>(count));
            ::GetKeyboardLayoutList(count, before.data());
            m_hkl = ::LoadKeyboardLayoutW(klid, KLF_NOTELLSHELL);
            m_loadedHere = m_hkl && std::find(before.begin(), before.end(), m_hkl) == before.end();
            m_ok = m_hkl && LOWORD(reinterpret_cast<UINT_PTR>(m_hkl)) == expectedLanguage;
        }
        ~ScopedTestLayout() { if (m_loadedHere) ::UnloadKeyboardLayout(m_hkl); }
        ScopedTestLayout(const ScopedTestLayout&) = delete;
        ScopedTestLayout& operator=(const ScopedTestLayout&) = delete;
        [[nodiscard]] bool Ok() const { return m_ok; }
        [[nodiscard]] std::uintptr_t Id() const { return reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(m_hkl); }
    private:
        HKL  m_hkl = nullptr;
        bool m_loadedHere = false;
        bool m_ok = false;
    };

    struct TextInputStroke
    {
        std::uint32_t vk = 0;
        bool shift = false;
        bool altGr = false;      // Ctrl + Right Alt held
        bool capsLock = false;
    };

    namespace Detail
    {
        // ToUnicodeEx without the keep-state flag on Space consumes a pending dead key.
        inline void ClearDeadKeyState(HKL hkl)
        {
            const BYTE none[256] = {};
            wchar_t buf[8] = {};
            const UINT scan = ::MapVirtualKeyExW(VK_SPACE, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC, hkl);
            (void)::ToUnicodeEx(VK_SPACE, scan, none, buf, 8, 0, hkl);
            (void)::ToUnicodeEx(VK_SPACE, scan, none, buf, 8, 0, hkl);
        }
    }

    // Plays `strokes` on `layout` through `hook` and returns the frame the view would build.
    // The thread's key state is set per stroke (SetKeyboardState) so GetKeyState inside the
    // hook sees the stroke's Shift / AltGr / Caps Lock, and restored afterwards.
    inline Editor::TextInputFrame PlayStrokes(Editor::TextInputHook& hook, const ScopedTestLayout& layout,
                                              const std::vector<TextInputStroke>& strokes)
    {
        const HKL hkl = reinterpret_cast<HKL>(layout.Id());
        hook.RefreshLayout(layout.Id());
        BYTE saved[256] = {};
        (void)::GetKeyboardState(saved);
        Detail::ClearDeadKeyState(hkl);
        Editor::RawTextInput raw;
        raw.layoutHasAltGr = hook.Layout().hasAltGr;
        std::vector<Editor::TextInputEvent> queued;          // what SDL would queue as text (ImGui's input queue), in order
        for (const TextInputStroke& s : strokes)
        {
            BYTE state[256] = {};
            if (s.shift) state[VK_SHIFT] = state[VK_LSHIFT] = 0x80;
            if (s.altGr) state[VK_CONTROL] = state[VK_LCONTROL] = state[VK_MENU] = state[VK_RMENU] = 0x80;
            if (s.capsLock) state[VK_CAPITAL] = 0x01;
            (void)::SetKeyboardState(state);
            raw.rightAltDown = raw.rightAltDown || s.altGr;

            const UINT scan = ::MapVirtualKeyExW(s.vk, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC, hkl);
            MSG down{};
            down.message = WM_KEYDOWN;
            down.wParam = s.vk;
            down.lParam = static_cast<LPARAM>(1u | (scan << 16));
            if (!hook.OnMessage(&down))
                continue;                                    // swallowed: TranslateMessage never sees it
            wchar_t buf[8] = {};
            const int n = ::ToUnicodeEx(s.vk, scan, state, buf, 8, 0, hkl);   // TranslateMessage's translation
            MSG ch{};
            ch.lParam = down.lParam;
            if (n < 0)
            {
                ch.message = WM_DEADCHAR;                    // passed on = it composes with the next key
                ch.wParam = buf[0];
                (void)hook.OnMessage(&ch);
                continue;
            }
            for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
            {
                ch.message = WM_CHAR;
                ch.wParam = buf[i];
                if (hook.OnMessage(&ch))
                {
                    Editor::TextInputEvent e;                // what SDL would queue as text
                    e.seq = Editor::NextTextInputSeq();
                    e.kind = Editor::TextInputEventKind::Char;
                    e.ch = static_cast<char32_t>(buf[i]);
                    queued.push_back(e);
                }
            }
        }
        (void)::SetKeyboardState(saved);
        Detail::ClearDeadKeyState(hkl);
        // TE2-10's ReadImGuiTextInput rule (D-R1): when the hook recorded events (command mode), they ARE
        // the stream and ImGui's copies are dropped; otherwise ImGui's queue is the stream.
        std::vector<Editor::TextInputEvent> recorded = hook.TakeCommandModeEvents();
        raw.events = recorded.empty() ? std::move(queued) : std::move(recorded);
        return Editor::BuildTextInputFrame(raw);
    }
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneTests/src/Text/VimKeyboardTest.cpp
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <iterator>

#include "Helpers/TextInputScript.hpp"

using namespace Arcane;
using Arcane::Test::FrameText;
using Arcane::Test::PlayStrokes;
using Arcane::Test::ScopedTestLayout;
using Arcane::Test::TextInputStroke;
using Arcane::Test::VimRig;

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: Ctrl chords become vim keys only for Labelled Ctrl+letter and Ctrl+[; TE2-10's named keys", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    CHECK(Editor::VimKeyFromChord(*Editor::ParseKeyChord("Ctrl+R")) == Text::VimKey::Ctrl(U'r'));
    CHECK(Editor::VimKeyFromChord(*Editor::ParseKeyChord("Ctrl+[")) == Text::VimKey::Ctrl(U'['));
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::VimKeyFromChord(*Editor::ParseKeyChord("Ctrl+Shift+R")).has_value());
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::VimKeyFromChord(*Editor::ParseKeyChord("Alt+R")).has_value());
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::VimKeyFromChord(*Editor::ParseKeyChord("Ctrl+F4")).has_value());
    CHECK(Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Escape }) == Text::VimKey::Named(Text::VimNamedKey::Esc));
    CHECK(Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Tab, false, true, false })
          == Text::VimKey::Named(Text::VimNamedKey::Tab, true));
    CHECK(Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Enter }) == Text::VimKey::Named(Text::VimNamedKey::Enter));
    CHECK(Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::PageDown, false, true, false })
          == Text::VimKey::Named(Text::VimNamedKey::PageDown, true));
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Home, true, false, false }).has_value());   // Ctrl+Home stays text.documentStart
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Left, false, false, true }).has_value());
    CHECK(Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Insert }) == Text::VimKey::Named(Text::VimNamedKey::Insert));   // X24
    CHECK(Text::FormatKey(*Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Insert })) == "<Insert>");   // TE5a-1 notation
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Insert, false, true, false }).has_value());   // Shift+Insert
}

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: every TE2-10 named key has a chord name -- <Insert> included (5a.16)", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    // kNames is indexed by TextNamedKey: a static_assert in TextViewHooks.hpp pins its size to Insert + 1.
    for (std::uint8_t k = 0; k <= static_cast<std::uint8_t>(Editor::TextNamedKey::Insert); ++k)
    {
        INFO("TextNamedKey " << int(k));
        CHECK(Editor::ChordOfNamedKey(Editor::TextKeyPress{ static_cast<Editor::TextNamedKey>(k) }).has_value());
    }
    CHECK(Editor::FormatKeyChord(*Editor::ChordOfNamedKey(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Insert })) == "Insert");
    CHECK(Editor::FormatKeyChord(*Editor::ChordOfNamedKey(Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Home, true })) == "Ctrl+Home");
}

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: one ordered stream -- ix<Esc> in one frame types x in Insert, then leaves Insert (D-R1, 5a.17)", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    VimRig rig("\xCB\x87" "ab");
    const auto ch = [](char32_t c) { Editor::TextInputEvent e; e.seq = Editor::NextTextInputSeq(); e.kind = Editor::TextInputEventKind::Char; e.ch = c; return e; };
    const auto key = [](Editor::TextNamedKey k) { Editor::TextInputEvent e; e.seq = Editor::NextTextInputSeq(); e.kind = Editor::TextInputEventKind::Key; e.key = Editor::TextKeyPress{ k }; return e; };
    const std::vector<Editor::TextInputEvent> frame{ ch(U'i'), ch(U'x'), key(Editor::TextNamedKey::Escape), ch(U'l') };
    const auto toVim = [&](const Text::VimKey& k) { rig.now += 0.001; return rig.vim->HandleKey(k, rig.now).handled; };
    const Editor::TextKeyInterceptor interceptor{
        [&](char32_t c) { return toVim(Text::VimKey::Char(c)); },
        {},
        [&](const Editor::TextKeyPress& k) { const auto v = Editor::VimKeyFromNamed(k); return v ? toVim(*v) : false; } };
    std::vector<Editor::KeyChord> consumed;
    std::vector<Editor::TextNamedKey> viewKeys;
    Editor::DispatchTextEvents(frame, interceptor, [&] { return rig.host.inputEnabled; },
                               Editor::TextEventSink{ [&](std::string_view t) { rig.TypeLikeTheView(t); },
                                                      [&](const Editor::TextKeyPress& k) { viewKeys.push_back(k.key); } },
                               consumed);
    CHECK(rig.Mode() == Text::VimMode::Normal);           // Esc ran AFTER x was typed
    CHECK(rig.Marked() == "x\xCB\x87" "ab");              // ... and l after Esc: the cursor moved right in Normal
    CHECK(viewKeys.empty());                              // every key went to vim
    REQUIRE(consumed.size() == 1u);                       // Esc's chord: its text.* / ui row does not fire too
    CHECK(Editor::FormatKeyChord(consumed[0]) == "Escape");
}

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: a Ctrl chord rides the stream at its place -- ix<C-[>l in one frame (A12)", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    VimRig rig("\xCB\x87" "ab");
    const auto ch = [](char32_t c) { Editor::TextInputEvent e; e.seq = Editor::NextTextInputSeq(); e.kind = Editor::TextInputEventKind::Char; e.ch = c; return e; };
    const auto chord = [](char32_t c) {
        Editor::TextInputEvent e;
        e.seq = Editor::NextTextInputSeq();
        e.kind = Editor::TextInputEventKind::Key;
        e.key = Editor::TextKeyPress{ Editor::TextNamedKey::Chord, true, false, false, c };   // TE2-10 (A12)
        return e;
    };
    const std::vector<Editor::TextInputEvent> frame{ ch(U'i'), ch(U'x'), chord(U'['), chord(U's'), ch(U'l') };
    const auto toVim = [&](const Text::VimKey& k) { rig.now += 0.001; return rig.vim->HandleKey(k, rig.now).handled; };
    const Editor::TextKeyInterceptor interceptor{
        [&](char32_t c) { return toVim(Text::VimKey::Char(c)); },
        [&](const Editor::KeyChord& c) {                  // what VimViewAdapter's interceptor does: only chords vim claims
            const auto v = Editor::VimKeyFromChord(c);
            return v && Text::VimClaimsChord(*v, rig.vim->Mode(), rig.vim->Options()) && toVim(*v);
        },
        {} };
    std::vector<Editor::KeyChord> consumed;
    std::vector<Editor::TextNamedKey> viewKeys;
    Editor::DispatchTextEvents(frame, interceptor, [&] { return rig.host.inputEnabled; },
                               Editor::TextEventSink{ [&](std::string_view t) { rig.TypeLikeTheView(t); },
                                                      [&](const Editor::TextKeyPress& k) { viewKeys.push_back(k.key); } },
                               consumed);
    CHECK(rig.Mode() == Text::VimMode::Normal);           // Ctrl-[ left Insert AFTER x was typed ...
    CHECK(rig.Marked() == "x\xCB\x87" "ab");              // ... and l moved right in Normal: stream order, no chord-first
    CHECK(viewKeys.empty());                              // a chord event is never a baseline key
    REQUIRE(consumed.size() == 1u);                       // Ctrl+S is the editor's (document.save): not consumed
    CHECK(Editor::FormatKeyChord(consumed[0]) == "Ctrl+[");
    CHECK(chord(U'[').key.key == Editor::TextNamedKey::Chord);   // TE2-10: a chord event's key is Chord
    CHECK(chord(U'[').key.chordChar == U'[');
    CHECK(Editor::ChordOfCharKey(Editor::TextKeyPress{}) == std::nullopt);   // a named-key event is not a chord
}

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: command mode records Ctrl+R through OnMessage as a Chord (A12)", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    // The case above builds TextKeyPress::Chord by hand, so it stays green if TE5a-22's
    // OnMessage drops TE2-10's chord branch. This one posts the same messages TE2-10's
    // hook test posts, through the same ScopedCtrlHeld helper, at the real OnMessage.
    class ScopedCtrlHeld
    {
    public:
        ScopedCtrlHeld()
        {
            ::GetKeyboardState(m_saved);
            BYTE held[256];
            std::copy(std::begin(m_saved), std::end(m_saved), std::begin(held));
            held[VK_CONTROL] = 0x80;
            held[VK_LCONTROL] = 0x80;
            ::SetKeyboardState(held);
        }
        ~ScopedCtrlHeld() { ::SetKeyboardState(m_saved); }
        ScopedCtrlHeld(const ScopedCtrlHeld&) = delete;
        ScopedCtrlHeld& operator=(const ScopedCtrlHeld&) = delete;
    private:
        BYTE m_saved[256] = {};
    };

    Editor::TextInputHook hook;
    hook.SetCommandMode(true);
    hook.SetLatinLetters(true);                              // a Ctrl chord is never a Latin letter
    {
        const ScopedCtrlHeld ctrl;
        MSG down{};
        down.message = WM_KEYDOWN;
        down.wParam = 'R';
        CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&down));
        MSG ctrlChar{};
        ctrlChar.message = WM_CHAR;
        ctrlChar.wParam = 0x12;                               // TranslateMessage's control character for Ctrl+R
        CHECK(hook.OnMessage(&ctrlChar));
    }
    const std::vector<Editor::TextInputEvent> ev = hook.TakeCommandModeEvents();
    REQUIRE(ev.size() == 2u);
    CHECK(ev[0].kind == Editor::TextInputEventKind::Key);
    CHECK(ev[0].key.key == Editor::TextNamedKey::Chord);
    CHECK(ev[0].key.ctrl);
    CHECK(ev[0].key.chordChar == U'r');
    CHECK(ev[1].kind == Editor::TextInputEventKind::Char);    // 0x12 is recorded, then dropped by BuildTextInputFrame
    CHECK(ev[1].ch == U'\x12');
}

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: a dead key composes while f / r wait for a literal; a mark name keeps command mode (D-R15, 5a.20)", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    const ScopedTestLayout fr(L"0000040C", 0x040C);
    if (!fr.Ok()) SKIP("the French layout could not be loaded");
    VimRig rig("\xCB\x87" "ab\xC3\xAA");                   // "abê"
    Editor::TextInputHook hook;
    Editor::ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, rig.vim->Keyboard(), false);
    CHECK(hook.CommandMode());                            // Normal: command keys
    rig.Keys("f");
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.vim->Keyboard().commandKeys);         // waiting for f's character: command mode off
    Editor::ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, rig.vim->Keyboard(), false);
    CHECK_FALSE(hook.CommandMode());
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, fr, { { VK_OEM_6 }, { 'E' } })) == "\xC3\xAA");   // ^ e composes: f^e is fê
    rig.Keys("\xC3\xAA");
    CHECK(rig.Marked() == "ab\xCB\x87" "\xC3\xAA");
    Editor::ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, rig.vim->Keyboard(), false);
    CHECK(hook.CommandMode());                            // back to command keys once the character arrived
    rig.Keys("m");
    CHECK(rig.vim->Keyboard().commandKeys);               // a NAME argument keeps command mode on (D-R15) ...
    Editor::ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, rig.vim->Keyboard(), false);
    CHECK(hook.CommandMode());                            // ... so the mark's name is the key's, not a composed character
}

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: Ctrl-W h/j/k/l/w map onto the two-view split's FocusOtherView", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    using Text::VimWindowCommand;
    // Not split: no direction has another view.
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusNext, false, false, true));
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusRight, false, true, true));
    // Side by side (vertical split): the primary is on the left.
    CHECK(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusRight, true, true, true));
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusLeft, true, true, true));
    CHECK(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusLeft, true, true, false));
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusDown, true, true, true));
    // Stacked (horizontal split): the primary is on top.
    CHECK(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusDown, true, false, true));
    CHECK(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusUp, true, false, false));
    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusRight, true, false, true));
    // Ctrl-W w always reaches the other view.
    CHECK(Editor::OtherViewLiesIn(VimWindowCommand::FocusNext, true, false, false));
}

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: Latin letters on a Cyrillic layout in Normal, the layout's letters for f's argument and in Insert", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    const ScopedTestLayout ru(L"00000419", 0x0419);
    if (!ru.Ok()) SKIP("the Russian layout could not be loaded");
    VimRig rig("\xCB\x87" "ab");
    Editor::TextInputHook hook;
    hook.RefreshLayout(ru.Id());
    CHECK_FALSE(hook.Layout().lettersLatin);          // what latinLettersInNormal=Auto reads (TE5a-23)
    const std::vector<TextInputStroke> keyF{ { 'F' } };
    Editor::ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, rig.vim->Keyboard(), true);
    CHECK(hook.LatinLetters());
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, keyF)) == "f");
    rig.Keys("f");                                    // waiting for f's literal argument: command mode and Latin letters off
    Editor::ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, rig.vim->Keyboard(), true);
    CHECK_FALSE(hook.LatinLetters());
    CHECK_FALSE(hook.CommandMode());
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, keyF)) == "\xD0\xB0");   // U+0430, the layout's letter
    rig.Keys("<Esc>m");                               // a mark NAME: command mode and Latin letters stay on (D-R15)
    Editor::ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, rig.vim->Keyboard(), true);
    CHECK(hook.LatinLetters());
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, keyF)) == "f");          // mf, as on a Latin layout
    rig.Keys("<Esc>i");
    Editor::ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, rig.vim->Keyboard(), true);
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, keyF)) == "\xD0\xB0");
}

TEST_CASE("vim keyboard: the Latin-letter path follows Shift, leaves non-letter keys to the layout and stands down under AltGr", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    const ScopedTestLayout ru(L"00000419", 0x0419);
    if (!ru.Ok()) SKIP("the Russian layout could not be loaded");
    Editor::TextInputHook hook;
    hook.SetCommandMode(true);
    hook.SetLatinLetters(true);
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, { { 'F', true } })) == "F");                      // Shift+F: the capital
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, { { 'F', false, false, true } })) == "F");        // Caps Lock
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, { { VK_OEM_1 } })) == "\xD0\xB6");               // U+0436: not a letter VK, the layout's character
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, { { 'F' }, { 'J' } })) == "fj");                  // one swallowed character per keystroke
    const Editor::TextInputFrame ordered = PlayStrokes(hook, ru, { { 'F' }, { 'J' } });
    REQUIRE(ordered.events.size() == 2u);
    CHECK(ordered.events[0].seq < ordered.events[1].seq);                                    // one stream, in keystroke order
    CHECK(ordered.events[0].fromCommandHook);
    hook.SetLatinLetters(false);
    CHECK(FrameText(PlayStrokes(hook, ru, { { 'F' } })) == "\xD0\xB0");
}
```

```cpp
    char32_t LatinLetterForVirtualKey(std::uint32_t vk, bool shift, bool capsLock)
    {
        if (vk < 'A' || vk > 'Z')
            return 0;
        const bool upper = shift != capsLock;
        return static_cast<char32_t>(upper ? vk : vk - 'A' + 'a');
```

and `OnMessage` becomes (TE2-10's D-R1 body plus the Latin-letter path):

```cpp
    bool TextInputHook::OnMessage(void* msgPtr)
    {
        const MSG& msg = *static_cast<const MSG*>(msgPtr);
        switch (msg.message)
        {
        case WM_KEYDOWN:
        case WM_SYSKEYDOWN:
        {
            if (msg.hwnd)
                m_lastKeyWindow = msg.hwnd;
            m_dropNextChar = false;   // a new keystroke: nothing is pending from the previous one
            if (!m_commandMode)
                return true;          // text-entry modes: ImGui's queue is the stream (D-R1)
            // GetKeyState answers as of the message just retrieved (ImGui's io lags a frame inside
            // the pump and has no Caps Lock toggle). Ctrl or Alt held (AltGr included): the key is
            // a chord or AltGr text, never a Latin letter.
            const bool ctrl = ::GetKeyState(VK_CONTROL) < 0;
            const bool alt = ::GetKeyState(VK_MENU) < 0;
            const bool shift = ::GetKeyState(VK_SHIFT) < 0;
            if (m_latinLetters && msg.message == WM_KEYDOWN && !ctrl && !alt)
                if (const char32_t latin = LatinLetterForVirtualKey(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(msg.wParam), shift,
                                                                    (::GetKeyState(VK_CAPITAL) & 0x0001) != 0))
                {
                    TextInputEvent e;
                    e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Char;
                    e.ch = latin;                 // the vim key is the key's Latin letter (spec s5.5)
                    Record(e);                    // seq = NextTextInputSeq(), fromCommandHook (D-R1)
                    m_dropNextChar = true;        // the layout's own character for this keystroke goes
                    return true;                  // the key-down itself continues: SDL's key state stays right
                }
            if (const std::optional<TextNamedKey> named = NamedKeyForVirtualKey(msg.wParam))
            {
                TextInputEvent e;
                e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Key;
                e.key = TextKeyPress{ *named, ctrl, shift, alt };
                Record(e);
            }
            else if ((ctrl || alt) && !(m_layout.hasAltGr && ::GetKeyState(VK_RMENU) < 0))   // AltGr is text, never a chord
                if (const std::optional<char32_t> key = ChordKeyCharForVirtualKey(static_cast<std::uintptr_t>(msg.wParam)))
                {
                    TextInputEvent e;   // rev-2 A12: the chord at its place in the stream
                    e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Key;
                    e.key = TextKeyPress{ TextNamedKey::Chord, ctrl, shift, alt, *key };
                    Record(e);
                }
            return true;   // SDL still updates its key state and the chords
        }
        case WM_CHAR:
            if (m_dropNextChar)
            {
                m_dropNextChar = false;
                return false;   // the Latin path took this keystroke: swallowed before SDL's text queue
            }
            if (m_commandMode)
                RecordUtf16(static_cast<char16_t>(msg.wParam));
            return true;
        case WM_DEADCHAR:
            if (m_dropNextChar)
            {
                m_dropNextChar = false;
                ConsumeDeadKeyState(m_layout.layout != 0 ? m_layout.layout : ActiveKeyboardLayout());
                return false;
            }
            if (!m_commandMode)
                return true;    // text-entry modes -- and vim waiting for f's / r's character (D-R1): it composes
            {
                TextInputEvent e;
                e.kind = TextInputEventKind::Char;
                e.ch = static_cast<char32_t>(msg.wParam);
                Record(e);
            }
            ConsumeDeadKeyState(m_layout.layout != 0 ? m_layout.layout : ActiveKeyboardLayout());
            return false;   // swallowed: nothing composes with the next key
        default:
            return true;
        }
    }
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/TextViewHooks.hpp
#pragma once

// The small hook surface the view exposes to the vim layer (spec s6.1):
// cursor shape, line mode, input enabled, clip at line ends, the four events,
// and a key interceptor consulted before the view's own handling and before
// any text.* / shared-verb row fires. With vim off nothing is installed and
// the view behaves as TE2/TE4 built it.

#include "Input/EditorActions.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Core/Utf8.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextInput.hpp"

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <iterator>
#include <optional>
#include <span>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    enum class TextCursorShape : std::uint8_t { Bar, Block, Underline };

    struct TextCaretBox { float x0 = 0.f, y0 = 0.f, x1 = 0.f, y1 = 0.f; };

    // The caret rectangle for the cell at (x, y): Bar is barWidth wide, Block the
    // whole cell, Underline barWidth tall at the cell's bottom.
    [[nodiscard]] inline TextCaretBox CaretBoxFor(TextCursorShape shape, float x, float y, float cellWidth, float lineHeight, float barWidth)
    {
        switch (shape)
        {
        case TextCursorShape::Block:     return TextCaretBox{ x, y, x + cellWidth, y + lineHeight };
        case TextCursorShape::Underline: return TextCaretBox{ x, y + lineHeight - barWidth, x + cellWidth, y + lineHeight };
        case TextCursorShape::Bar:       break;
        }
        return TextCaretBox{ x, y, x + barWidth, y + lineHeight };
    }

    struct TextViewEvents
    {
        std::function<void(std::string_view)> inputHandled;        // typed text the view inserted (IME commits included)
        std::function<void()>                 transactionBegun;    // an editing command ran outside vim (row, paste, cut, find bar)
        std::function<void()>                 transactionUndone;   // the document's undo/redo ran
        std::function<void(bool byMouse)>     selectionsChanged;   // a click or drag moved selections
        // The DOCUMENT is about to change the buffer outside any view's input (save transforms,
        // reload, Follow's append, undo/redo verbs, line-ending conversion): vim ends its open
        // insert transaction first (finding 5a.7; TE1 refuses those changes inside a transaction).
        std::function<void()>                 outsideChange;
    };

    struct TextKeyInterceptor
    {
        std::function<bool(char32_t)>            character;   // true = consumed, the view does not type it
        std::function<bool(const KeyChord&)>     chord;       // Ctrl+letter / Ctrl+[ chord events (A12); true = consumed, no row fires
        std::function<bool(const TextKeyPress&)> named;       // TE2-10's named keys; true = consumed, no row fires
    };

    // A named key as the KeyChord its row is bound to (Home -> text.lineStart, Esc -> ui.cancel ...),
    // in ParseKeyChord's own key names, indexed by TextNamedKey (finding 5a.16: Insert included).
    [[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<KeyChord> ChordOfNamedKey(const TextKeyPress& k)
    {
        static constexpr const char* kNames[] = { "Left", "Right", "Up", "Down", "Home", "End", "PageUp", "PageDown",
                                                  "Backspace", "Delete", "Enter", "Tab", "Escape", "Insert" };
        static_assert(std::size(kNames) == static_cast<std::size_t>(TextNamedKey::Insert) + 1,
                      "kNames must name every TextNamedKey (TE2-10's enum order)");
        const auto index = static_cast<std::size_t>(k.key);
        if (index >= std::size(kNames)) return std::nullopt;
        std::string text;
        if (k.ctrl) text += "Ctrl+";
        if (k.shift) text += "Shift+";
        if (k.alt) text += "Alt+";
        text += kNames[index];
        return ParseKeyChord(text);
    }

    // A12: a Ctrl chord riding TE2-10's stream (TextKeyPress::chordChar = 'a'..'z' or '[') as the KeyChord
    // EditorActions binds ("Ctrl+R", "Ctrl+Shift+R", "Ctrl+["); nullopt for a named-key event.
    [[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<KeyChord> ChordOfCharKey(const TextKeyPress& k)
    {
        if (k.chordChar == 0) return std::nullopt;
        std::string text;
        if (k.ctrl) text += "Ctrl+";
        if (k.shift) text += "Shift+";
        if (k.alt) text += "Alt+";
        text.push_back(k.chordChar >= U'a' && k.chordChar <= U'z' ? static_cast<char>(k.chordChar - U'a' + 'A')
                                                                  : static_cast<char>(k.chordChar));
        return ParseKeyChord(text);
    }

    // Where the view sends what the interceptor leaves: typed text (one run) and named keys.
    struct TextEventSink
    {
        std::function<void(std::string_view)>    type;
        std::function<void(const TextKeyPress&)> key;
    };

    // D-R1 / finding 5a.17: the frame's ONE ordered stream, front to back. Every event goes to the
    // interceptor at its place in the stream, AFTER the text typed so far was inserted (so vim's Esc
    // in `ix<Esc>` sees the x already typed); what it leaves is typed (when input is enabled -- vim
    // flips that per mode, so it is asked per event) or applied as a key. A consumed named key's or
    // chord's KeyChord is recorded so the row bound to it does not fire as well. A Ctrl chord event
    // (A12, chordChar != 0) is never a baseline key: unconsumed, it stays the action table's.
    inline void DispatchTextEvents(std::span<const TextInputEvent> events, const TextKeyInterceptor& interceptor,
                                   const std::function<bool()>& inputEnabled, const TextEventSink& sink,
                                   std::vector<KeyChord>& consumedChords)
    {
        std::string run;
        const auto flush = [&] {
            if (run.empty()) return;
            sink.type(run);
            run.clear();
        };
        for (const TextInputEvent& e : events)
        {
            if (e.kind == TextInputEventKind::Char)
            {
                if (interceptor.character)
                {
                    flush();
                    if (interceptor.character(e.ch)) continue;
                }
                if (inputEnabled()) Text::Utf8::Append(run, e.ch);
                continue;
            }
            flush();
            if (const std::optional<KeyChord> chord = ChordOfCharKey(e.key))      // A12: a chord at its place
            {
                if (interceptor.chord && interceptor.chord(*chord)) consumedChords.push_back(*chord);
                continue;
            }
            if (interceptor.named && interceptor.named(e.key))
            {
                if (const std::optional<KeyChord> c = ChordOfNamedKey(e.key)) consumedChords.push_back(*c);
                continue;
            }
            sink.key(e.key);
        }
        flush();
    }
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimKeyTranslate.hpp
#pragma once

// Pure editor-side helpers of the vim glue (spec s5.5, s6.1): chord / named-key
// translation, pushing the vim keyboard state into TE2-10's TextInputHook, the
// :q decision, the status text and the split direction rule. Compiled into ArcaneTests.

#include "Input/EditorActions.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextInput.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimCommand.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimHost.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimKey.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimOptions.hpp"   // VimClaimsKeyChord

#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    class TextInputHook;

    // Spec D12: vim is Experimental until VIM-GATE flips this (status strip + Vim Preferences
    // page badge). Defined HERE ONLY (CANON B15): TE5d-5 includes this header.
    inline constexpr bool kVimExperimental = true;

    [[nodiscard]] std::optional<Text::VimKey> VimKeyFromChord(const KeyChord& chord);
    // TE2-10's named keys; Ctrl/Alt + a named key stays the action table's (Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+Left ...).
    [[nodiscard]] std::optional<Text::VimKey> VimKeyFromNamed(const TextKeyPress& key);
    // A bound chord as the vim key it would be: Ctrl chords through VimKeyFromChord, bare / Shift
    // named keys through VimKeyFromNamed; nullopt for everything else (letters, F-keys, Alt chords).
    [[nodiscard]] std::optional<Text::VimKey> VimKeyFromKeyChord(const KeyChord& chord);
    // The chord claim of a vim view holding the keyboard (finding 5a.18): a bare or Shift printable key
    // (it types or is a vim command), a bare / Shift named key vim maps, and the Ctrl chords
    // Text::VimClaimsChord gives vim in `mode`. Alt / Super chords, F-keys and Ctrl+named keys: never.
    [[nodiscard]] bool VimClaimsKeyChord(const KeyChord& chord, Text::VimMode mode, const Text::VimOptions& options);
    // Command mode, Latin letters and the IME per vim's mode (spec s5.5, s5.1).
    void ApplyVimKeyboard(TextInputHook& hook, const Text::VimKeyboardState& state, bool latinLettersWanted);
    // The text keyboard: no command mode, no Latin letters, IME allowed (no vim view holds the keyboard).
    void ResetTextKeyboard(TextInputHook& hook);
    [[nodiscard]] Text::VimHostResult QuitDecision(bool dirty, bool bang);
    // :w {file} writes a COPY (finding 5a.25): an existing target needs ! (E13), as in Vim.
    [[nodiscard]] Text::VimHostResult WriteCopyDecision(bool targetExists, bool bang);
    [[nodiscard]] std::string VimModeStatusText(Text::VimMode mode);
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimKeyTranslate.cpp
#include "TextEditor/View/VimKeyTranslate.hpp"

#include "TextEditor/View/TextInputHook.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/TextViewHooks.hpp"   // ChordOfNamedKey
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimChords.hpp"        // VimClaimsChord (TE5a-20)

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    std::optional<Text::VimKey> VimKeyFromChord(const KeyChord& chord)
    {
        if (!chord.ctrl || chord.alt || chord.shift || chord.super || chord.type != KeyType::Labelled) return std::nullopt;
        if (chord.key >= 'a' && chord.key <= 'z') return Text::VimKey::Ctrl(static_cast<char32_t>(chord.key));   // SDL keycodes: lowercase ASCII
        if (chord.key >= 'A' && chord.key <= 'Z') return Text::VimKey::Ctrl(static_cast<char32_t>(chord.key - 'A' + 'a'));
        if (chord.key == '[') return Text::VimKey::Ctrl(U'[');
        return std::nullopt;                                     // Ctrl+F4, Ctrl+arrows ...: the action table's
    }

    std::optional<Text::VimKey> VimKeyFromNamed(const TextKeyPress& k)
    {
        using Text::VimKey;
        using Text::VimNamedKey;
        if (k.ctrl || k.alt) return std::nullopt;
        switch (k.key)
        {
        case TextNamedKey::Escape:    return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Esc);
        case TextNamedKey::Enter:     return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Enter);
        case TextNamedKey::Tab:       return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Tab, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::Backspace: return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Backspace);
        case TextNamedKey::Delete:    return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Delete);
        case TextNamedKey::Up:        return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Up, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::Down:      return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Down, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::Left:      return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Left, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::Right:     return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Right, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::Home:      return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Home, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::End:       return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::End, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::PageUp:    return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::PageUp, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::PageDown:  return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::PageDown, k.shift);
        case TextNamedKey::Insert:                               // vim's <Insert> (cross-fix X24): i in Normal, the Insert/Replace toggle
            if (k.shift) return std::nullopt;                    // Shift+Insert is not a vim key: it stays the editor's
            return VimKey::Named(VimNamedKey::Insert);
        }
        return std::nullopt;
    }

    std::optional<Text::VimKey> VimKeyFromKeyChord(const KeyChord& chord)
    {
        if (chord.ctrl) return VimKeyFromChord(chord);
        if (chord.alt || chord.super || !chord.Bound()) return std::nullopt;
        for (std::uint8_t k = 0; k <= static_cast<std::uint8_t>(TextNamedKey::Insert); ++k)
        {
            const TextKeyPress press{ static_cast<TextNamedKey>(k), false, chord.shift, false };
            if (const std::optional<KeyChord> named = ChordOfNamedKey(press); named && SameKey(*named, chord))
                return VimKeyFromNamed(press);
        }
        return std::nullopt;
    }

    bool VimClaimsKeyChord(const KeyChord& chord, Text::VimMode mode, const Text::VimOptions& options)
    {
        if (!chord.Bound() || chord.alt || chord.super) return false;
        if (!chord.ctrl && chord.type == KeyType::Labelled && chord.key >= 0x20 && chord.key < 0x7F)
            return true;                                         // a printable key: text, or a vim command
        const std::optional<Text::VimKey> key = VimKeyFromKeyChord(chord);
        return key && Text::VimClaimsChord(*key, mode, options);  // named keys are always vim's; Ctrl chords per s6.6
    }

    void ApplyVimKeyboard(TextInputHook& hook, const Text::VimKeyboardState& state, bool latinLettersWanted)
    {
        hook.SetCommandMode(state.commandKeys);
        hook.SetLatinLetters(state.latinLetters && latinLettersWanted);
        hook.SetImeAllowed(state.imeAllowed);    // TE2-10 disassociates / restores the IME context (CANON B24)
    }

    void ResetTextKeyboard(TextInputHook& hook)
    {
        Text::VimKeyboardState text;
        text.commandKeys = false;
        text.latinLetters = false;
        text.imeAllowed = true;
        ApplyVimKeyboard(hook, text, false);
    }

    Text::VimHostResult QuitDecision(bool dirty, bool bang)
    {
        if (dirty && !bang) return Text::VimHostResult{ false, "E37: No write since last change (add ! to override)" };
        return Text::VimHostResult{};
    }

    Text::VimHostResult WriteCopyDecision(bool targetExists, bool bang)
    {
        if (targetExists && !bang) return Text::VimHostResult{ false, "E13: File exists (add ! to override)" };
        return Text::VimHostResult{};
    }

    std::string VimModeStatusText(Text::VimMode mode)
    {
        switch (mode)
        {
        case Text::VimMode::Insert:      return "-- INSERT --";
        case Text::VimMode::Replace:     return "-- REPLACE --";
        case Text::VimMode::Visual:      return "-- VISUAL --";
        case Text::VimMode::VisualLine:  return "-- VISUAL LINE --";
        case Text::VimMode::VisualBlock: return "-- VISUAL BLOCK --";
        default:                         return {};
        }
    }

    bool OtherViewLiesIn(Text::VimWindowCommand direction, bool splitOpen, bool splitVertical, bool focusedIsPrimary)
    {
        using Text::VimWindowCommand;
        if (!splitOpen) return false;
        switch (direction)
        {
        case VimWindowCommand::FocusNext:  return true;
        case VimWindowCommand::FocusLeft:  return splitVertical && !focusedIsPrimary;
        case VimWindowCommand::FocusRight: return splitVertical && focusedIsPrimary;
        case VimWindowCommand::FocusUp:    return !splitVertical && !focusedIsPrimary;
        case VimWindowCommand::FocusDown:  return !splitVertical && focusedIsPrimary;
        default:                           return false;
        }
    }

    std::string PathToUtf8(const std::filesystem::path& path)
    {
        const std::u8string u8 = path.u8string();
        return std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(u8.data()), u8.size());
    }

    std::filesystem::path Utf8ToPath(std::string_view utf8)
    {
        return std::filesystem::path(std::u8string(reinterpret_cast<const char8_t*>(utf8.data()), utf8.size()));
    }
}
```

```cpp
    void EditorActions::SetChordClaim(const void* owner, ChordClaim claim)
    {
        m_claimOwner = owner;
        m_claim = std::move(claim);
    }

    void EditorActions::ClearChordClaim(const void* owner) noexcept
    {
        if (owner != nullptr && owner != m_claimOwner) return;   // another widget's claim stays
        m_claimOwner = nullptr;
        m_claim = {};
```

```cpp
// ArcaneTests/src/Text/VimChordClaimTest.cpp
// Finding 5a.18: a chord the focused vim view claims fires in no context.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Input/EditorActions.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/VimKeyTranslate.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimOptions.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Config/CVarRegistry.hpp>
#include <Arcane/Input/InputSnapshot.hpp>
#include <Arcane/Input/KeyLayout.hpp>

#include <initializer_list>

using namespace Arcane::Editor;
namespace Keys = Arcane::Keys;

namespace
{
    Arcane::InputSnapshot Snap(std::initializer_list<std::uint32_t> scancodes)
    {
        Arcane::InputSnapshot s;
        for (std::uint32_t sc : scancodes)
        {
            s.SetScancode(sc);
            if (const std::int32_t kc = Arcane::QwertyKeyLayout().KeycodeFor(sc)) s.AddKeycode(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kc));
        }
        return s;
    }

TEST_CASE("vim chord claim: a claimed chord fires in no context; another owner's clear leaves it (5a.18)", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    Arcane::CVarRegistry reg;
    EditorActions actions{ reg };
    actions.Register({ "t.openScene", "Open Scene", ActionContext::Global, "Ctrl+O" });
    actions.Register({ "t.cancel", "Cancel", ActionContext::Global, "Escape" });
    actions.Register({ "t.save", "Save", ActionContext::Global, "Ctrl+S" });
    Arcane::InputSnapshot snap;
    const auto frame = [&](std::initializer_list<std::uint32_t> keys) {
        snap = Snap(keys);
        ActionFrameInput in;
        in.snap = &snap;
        in.viewportActive = true;
        actions.BeginFrame(in);
    };
    frame({ Keys::kScanLCtrl, Keys::ScanLetter('O') });
    CHECK(actions.Pressed("t.openScene"));                       // no claim: Global fires
    frame({});

    int vimView = 0, otherWidget = 0;
    const Arcane::Text::VimOptions options;                       // handleCtrlKeys on (Neovim default chord table)
    actions.SetChordClaim(&vimView, [&options](const KeyChord& c) {
        return VimClaimsKeyChord(c, Arcane::Text::VimMode::Normal, options);
    });
    frame({ Keys::kScanLCtrl, Keys::ScanLetter('O') });
    CHECK_FALSE(actions.Pressed("t.openScene"));                 // vim's Ctrl-O (jump older) only
    frame({});
    frame({ Keys::kScanEscape });
    CHECK_FALSE(actions.Pressed("t.cancel"));                    // vim's Esc only
    frame({});
    frame({ Keys::kScanLCtrl, Keys::ScanLetter('S') });
    CHECK(actions.Pressed("t.save"));                            // Ctrl+S: never vim's (spec s6.6)
    frame({});

    actions.ClearChordClaim(&otherWidget);                       // not the owner: the claim stays
    frame({ Keys::kScanLCtrl, Keys::ScanLetter('O') });
    CHECK_FALSE(actions.Pressed("t.openScene"));
    frame({});
    actions.ClearChordClaim(&vimView);
    frame({ Keys::kScanLCtrl, Keys::ScanLetter('O') });
    CHECK(actions.Pressed("t.openScene"));
}

TEST_CASE("vim chord claim: printable and named keys are vim's; F-keys, Alt and Ctrl+named keys are not", "[text-vim-keyboard]")
{
    const Arcane::Text::VimOptions o;
    using Arcane::Text::VimMode;
    CHECK(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("F"), VimMode::Normal, o));          // a bare letter: a vim command
    CHECK(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("Shift+G"), VimMode::Normal, o));
    CHECK(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("Escape"), VimMode::Insert, o));
    CHECK(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("Home"), VimMode::Visual, o));
    CHECK_FALSE(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("F5"), VimMode::Normal, o));
    CHECK_FALSE(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("Alt+F"), VimMode::Normal, o));
    CHECK_FALSE(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("Ctrl+Home"), VimMode::Normal, o));
    CHECK_FALSE(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("Ctrl+S"), VimMode::Normal, o));
    Arcane::Text::VimOptions off = o;
    off.handleCtrlKeys = false;
    CHECK_FALSE(VimClaimsKeyChord(*ParseKeyChord("Ctrl+O"), VimMode::Normal, off));   // handleCtrlKeys off: the editor's
}
```

```cpp
    int DispatchTextActions(EditorActions& actions, TextActionTarget& target, const TextEditorView* keysView)
    {
        actions.MarkContextActive(ActionContext::TextDocument);
        int ran = 0;
        for (const TextActionRow& row : kTextActionTable)
        {
            const bool fired = row.repeats ? actions.PressedRepeat(row.desc.id) : actions.Pressed(row.desc.id);
            if (!fired) continue;
            if (keysView && keysView->ChordConsumed(row.desc.id)) continue;   // vim took this chord (spec s6.1)
            if (keysView) keysView->NotifyTransactionBegun();                  // a row's motion splits an insert session as vim's arrows do
            target.RunTextAction(row.action);
            ++ran;
        }
        return ran;
    }
```

```cpp
    void TextDocument::ApplySharedVerbs(const TextSharedVerbs& verbs, bool& requestClose)
    {
        // TE5a-22 (spec s6.1): a chord the focused view's key interceptor (vim) consumed this
        // frame -- Ctrl+R, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+W ... -- never fires its shared verb as well.
        TextSharedVerbs v = verbs;
        const TextEditorView& keysView = FocusedView();
        if (keysView.ChordConsumed("edit.undo")) v.undo = false;
        if (keysView.ChordConsumed("edit.redo") || keysView.ChordConsumed("edit.redoAlt")) v.redo = false;
        if (keysView.ChordConsumed("edit.cut")) v.cut = false;
        if (keysView.ChordConsumed("edit.copy")) v.copy = false;
        if (keysView.ChordConsumed("edit.paste")) v.paste = false;
        if (keysView.ChordConsumed("document.close")) v.close = false;      // Ctrl+W is vim's window prefix; Ctrl+F4 still closes
        if ((v.undo || v.redo || v.cut || v.paste) && !ReadOnly()) NotifyOutsideChange();   // 5a.7: TE2-15's hook (both views); undo is a no-op inside vim's transaction
        if ((v.cut || v.paste) && !ReadOnly()) keysView.NotifyTransactionBegun();
        // ... the body as TE4-17 left it: FocusedView / ModelOf / ViewEditScope / cmds, then TE2-18's undo, redo,
        //     copy/cut, paste, TE4-17's reveal on the focused view, close ...
        if ((v.undo || v.redo) && !ReadOnly()) keysView.NotifyTransactionUndone();
    }
```
