### Task TE5d-6: Persisting marks, registers and history in the editor user folder (spec s6.4 "persist in user data", `persistState`)

**Files:**
- Create: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Vim/VimPersist.hpp`
- Create: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Vim/VimPersist.cpp`
- Create: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimPersistence.hpp`
- Create: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimPersistence.cpp`
- Modify: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimEditorRuntime.hpp/.cpp` (TE5a-23: load once on the first attach, save when the last vim view detaches)
- Modify: `ArcaneEditor/src/App/EditorApp.cpp:3023` (save after `m_documents.CloseAll()` on the exit path)
- Modify: `premake5.lua` -- ArcaneTests file list gains `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimPersistence.cpp` (after the line TE5a-22 added for `VimViewAdapter.cpp`)
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/VimPersistTest.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `VimRegisters::Store/Get/List`, `VimRegisterValue`, `VimRegisterKind`, `VimRegisterOp` (TE5a-12/TE5b-1); `VimGlobalMarks::Set/Get/List`, `VimGlobalMark`, `VimGlobals::fileMarks` (TE5b-6/7); `VimGlobals::searchHistory/commandHistory` (TE5c-5/6); `VimEditorRuntime::Get/Globals/Attach/Detach/ForEachVim` (TE5a-23); `TextVimSettings::persistState` (TE5d-1); `Paths::Get(Paths::Location::EditorUserDir)` (`Paths.hpp:28,52`), `WriteTextFileAtomic` (`Project/AssetFileOps.hpp:114`); `IVimHost` (all methods incl. TE5d-2's `SetSessionOption`).
- Produces: `struct VimPersistedState { registers, globalMarks, fileMarks, searchHistory, commandHistory }`, `VimPersistedState CaptureVimState(const VimGlobals&, IVimHost&, const VimOptions&)`, `void RestoreVimState(VimGlobals&, const VimPersistedState&, IVimHost&, const VimOptions&)`, `std::string SerializeVimState(const VimPersistedState&)`, `std::expected<VimPersistedState, std::string> ParseVimState(std::string_view)`, `VimPersistedState MergeVimState(const VimPersistedState& base, const VimPersistedState& ours, const VimPersistedState& theirs)` (finding 5d.4), the caps `kVimPersistMaxRegisterLines` (50), `kVimPersistMaxRegisterBytes` (10 KB), `kVimPersistMaxHistory` (10000), `kVimPersistMaxFiles` (1000), `kVimStateFormatVersion` (1); editor side `std::filesystem::path VimStateFilePath()`, `enum class VimPersistLoad : std::uint8_t { Disabled, Missing, Loaded, Refused }`, `struct VimPersistLoadResult { VimPersistLoad status; Text::VimPersistedState base; }`, `VimPersistLoadResult LoadVimPersistence(Text::VimGlobals&, const std::filesystem::path&, bool enabled)`, `std::optional<Text::VimPersistedState> SaveVimPersistence(const Text::VimGlobals&, const std::filesystem::path&, bool enabled, const Text::VimPersistedState& base)`, `class DetachedVimHost`, `VimEditorRuntime::LoadPersistedStateOnce()`, `VimEditorRuntime::SavePersistedState()`.

What persists follows Neovim's default `'shada'` (`!,'100,<50,s10,h`): the named, numbered and small-delete registers (`a-z 0-9 -`), each at most 50 lines and 10 KB (larger ones are skipped, as shada skips them); the global marks `A-Z` (path + row/col); the lowercase marks of files (TE5b's `fileMarks` table, keyed by canonical path); and the search and command histories (Neovim's `'history'` default, 10000 entries each). `+ * _ . : / %` are not persisted (clipboard, black hole, read-only). The file is `<EditorUserDir>/TextEditor/vim-state.json` (empty in Dist, so nothing is written there), written through `WriteTextFileAtomic` (temp + rename). It loads once, when the first vim view attaches, and saves when the last vim view detaches and on editor exit; `persistState` off does neither. Restoring stores `"0` last so the unnamed register points at the last yank, as after a Neovim restart. Invalid UTF-8 in a register (a binary log) is written with U+FFFD replacements: the file stays valid JSON; that register text is lossy across sessions, which shada also does not promise for invalid bytes.

**Never clobber a file this session could not read; merge with another editor's writes (finding 5d.4).** The load reports `Loaded`, `Missing` (no file yet: writing one is fine), `Refused` (unreadable, corrupt, or a newer `version`) or `Disabled`. Only `Loaded` and `Missing` make the session's state writable; after `Refused` nothing is written for the rest of the session, so a newer editor's file survives an older editor (and a broken file stays for the user to inspect). The state the load applied is kept as the merge **base**. Saving re-reads the file first: if it is now missing, this session's state is written; if it parses, the three are merged (`MergeVimState`): a register, global mark, file's mark table or history entry this session changed since the base wins, anything this session left alone takes the file's current value, so a second editor instance that saved in between keeps its changes (histories: the file's entries, then this session's new ones, newest last, capped); if it no longer parses (corrupt, or a newer version written since), the save is refused and logged. The written state becomes the new base, so the next save merges against it.

```cpp
TEST_CASE("vim persist: Serialize then Parse is the identity", "[text-vim-persist]")
{
    const VimPersistedState s = Sample();
    const auto back = ParseVimState(SerializeVimState(s));
    REQUIRE(back.has_value());
    REQUIRE(back->registers.size() == 3u);
    CHECK(back->registers[0].first == U'a');
    CHECK(back->registers[0].second == s.registers[0].second);
    CHECK(back->registers[1].second == s.registers[1].second);
    CHECK(back->registers[2].second.kind == VimRegisterKind::Blockwise);
    REQUIRE(back->globalMarks.size() == 1u);
    CHECK(back->globalMarks[0].second.path == "C:/proj/a.lua");
    CHECK(back->globalMarks[0].second.point.row == 3u);
    CHECK(back->globalMarks[0].second.point.col == 4u);
    CHECK(back->fileMarks.at("C:/proj/b.txt").at(U'q').row == 7u);
    CHECK(back->searchHistory == s.searchHistory);
    CHECK(back->commandHistory == s.commandHistory);
}

TEST_CASE("vim persist: shada-sized caps and refused files", "[text-vim-persist]")
{
    VimPersistedState s;
    std::string big;
    for (int i = 0; i < 51; ++i) big += "line\n";
    s.registers.emplace_back(U'a', VimRegisterValue{ { big }, VimRegisterKind::Linewise });           // > 50 lines
    s.registers.emplace_back(U'b', VimRegisterValue{ { std::string(10 * 1024 + 1, 'x') }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise });   // > 10 KB
    s.registers.emplace_back(U'c', VimRegisterValue{ { "ok" }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise });
    for (int i = 0; i < 10005; ++i) s.searchHistory.push_back("p" + std::to_string(i));
    const auto back = ParseVimState(SerializeVimState(s));
    REQUIRE(back.has_value());
    REQUIRE(back->registers.size() == 1u);
    CHECK(back->registers[0].first == U'c');
    REQUIRE(back->searchHistory.size() == kVimPersistMaxHistory);
    CHECK(back->searchHistory.front() == "p5");                   // the newest entries are kept
    CHECK(back->searchHistory.back() == "p10004");

    CHECK_FALSE(ParseVimState("{").has_value());
    CHECK_FALSE(ParseVimState(R"({"format":"other","version":1})").has_value());
    CHECK_FALSE(ParseVimState(R"({"format":"arcvimstate","version":99})").has_value());   // a newer file: left alone
}

TEST_CASE("vim persist: Capture and Restore through VimGlobals", "[text-vim-persist]")
{
    Arcane::Test::FakeVimHost host;
    const VimOptions options;
    VimGlobals g;
    g.registers.Store(U'a', VimRegisterValue{ { "alpha" }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise }, VimRegisterOp::Yank, host, options);
    g.registers.Store(0, VimRegisterValue{ { "yanked" }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise }, VimRegisterOp::Yank, host, options);
    g.registers.Store(U'_', VimRegisterValue{ { "gone" }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise }, VimRegisterOp::Yank, host, options);
    g.globalMarks.Set(U'B', VimGlobalMark{ "C:/x.txt", Point{ 1, 2 } });
    g.fileMarks["C:/y.txt"][U'a'] = Point{ 5, 1 };
    g.searchHistory = { "needle" };
    g.commandHistory = { "noh" };

    const VimPersistedState s = CaptureVimState(g, host, options);
    for (const auto& [name, value] : s.registers) CHECK(name != U'_');

    VimGlobals fresh;
    RestoreVimState(fresh, s, host, options);
    CHECK(fresh.registers.Get(U'a', host, options) == g.registers.Get(U'a', host, options));
    CHECK(fresh.registers.Get(U'0', host, options) == g.registers.Get(U'0', host, options));
    CHECK(fresh.registers.Get(0, host, options) == g.registers.Get(U'0', host, options));   // " points at the last yank
    REQUIRE(fresh.globalMarks.Get(U'B').has_value());
    CHECK(fresh.globalMarks.Get(U'B')->path == "C:/x.txt");
    CHECK(fresh.fileMarks.at("C:/y.txt").at(U'a').row == 5u);
    CHECK(fresh.searchHistory == g.searchHistory);
    CHECK(fresh.commandHistory == g.commandHistory);
}

    CHECK_FALSE(Editor::SaveVimPersistence(g, file, false, VimPersistedState{}).has_value());
    CHECK_FALSE(std::filesystem::exists(file));
    REQUIRE(Editor::SaveVimPersistence(g, file, true, VimPersistedState{}).has_value());
    REQUIRE(std::filesystem::exists(file));

    VimGlobals loaded;
    CHECK(Editor::LoadVimPersistence(loaded, file, false).status == Editor::VimPersistLoad::Disabled);
    CHECK(loaded.searchHistory.empty());
    const Editor::VimPersistLoadResult ok = Editor::LoadVimPersistence(loaded, file, true);
    REQUIRE(ok.status == Editor::VimPersistLoad::Loaded);
    CHECK(ok.base.searchHistory == g.searchHistory);           // the merge base is what the load applied
    CHECK(loaded.searchHistory == g.searchHistory);
    CHECK(loaded.registers.Get(U'q', host, VimOptions{}) == g.registers.Get(U'q', host, VimOptions{}));

    { std::ofstream(file, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc) << "{ broken"; }
    VimGlobals fromBroken;
    CHECK(Editor::LoadVimPersistence(fromBroken, file, true).status == Editor::VimPersistLoad::Refused);   // never half-applied
    CHECK(fromBroken.searchHistory.empty());
    CHECK(Editor::LoadVimPersistence(fromBroken, dir / "missing.json", true).status == Editor::VimPersistLoad::Missing);
    CHECK(Editor::VimStateFilePath().filename() == "vim-state.json");
    std::filesystem::remove_all(dir);
}

TEST_CASE("vim persist: a newer or broken file is never overwritten", "[text-vim-persist]")
{
    const std::filesystem::path dir = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "te5d-vim-persist-newer";
    std::filesystem::remove_all(dir);
    std::filesystem::create_directories(dir);
    const std::filesystem::path file = dir / "vim-state.json";
    const std::string newer = R"({"format":"arcvimstate","version":99,"registers":[]})";
    { std::ofstream(file, std::ios::binary) << newer; }
    VimGlobals g;
    g.searchHistory = { "mine" };
    CHECK(Editor::SaveVimPersistence(g, file, true, VimPersistedState{}) == std::nullopt);   // re-read first: refused
    std::ifstream in(file, std::ios::binary);
    std::stringstream after;
    after << in.rdbuf();
    CHECK(after.str() == newer);                              // byte for byte untouched
    in.close();
    std::filesystem::remove_all(dir);
}

TEST_CASE("vim persist: two editor instances merge instead of clobbering (three-way)", "[text-vim-persist]")
{
    VimPersistedState base;
    base.registers.emplace_back(U'a', VimRegisterValue{ { "old a" }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise });
    base.registers.emplace_back(U'b', VimRegisterValue{ { "old b" }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise });
    base.searchHistory = { "x" };
    VimPersistedState ours = base;                            // this session changed b and searched for "mine"
    ours.registers[1].second = VimRegisterValue{ { "our b" }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise };
    ours.searchHistory = { "x", "mine" };
    ours.globalMarks.emplace_back(U'A', VimGlobalMark{ "C:/o.txt", Point{ 1, 0 } });
    VimPersistedState theirs = base;                          // the other instance saved a, a mark and a search meanwhile
    theirs.registers[0].second = VimRegisterValue{ { "their a" }, VimRegisterKind::Charwise };
    theirs.searchHistory = { "x", "theirs" };
    theirs.globalMarks.emplace_back(U'B', VimGlobalMark{ "C:/t.txt", Point{ 2, 0 } });
    theirs.fileMarks["C:/t.txt"][U'q'] = Point{ 3, 1 };

    const VimPersistedState m = MergeVimState(base, ours, theirs);
    REQUIRE(m.registers.size() == 2u);
    CHECK(m.registers[0].second.Text() == "their a");         // untouched here: the file's newer value
    CHECK(m.registers[1].second.Text() == "our b");           // changed here: ours
    CHECK(m.globalMarks.size() == 2u);
    CHECK(m.fileMarks.count("C:/t.txt") == 1u);
    CHECK(m.searchHistory == std::vector<std::string>{ "x", "theirs", "mine" });
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Vim/VimPersist.hpp
#pragma once

// What vim keeps between editor sessions (spec s6.4, editor.text.vim.persistState),
// sized like Neovim's default 'shada' (!,'100,<50,s10,h). Pure: the editor side
// (View/VimPersistence) reads and writes the file.

#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimGlobals.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimHost.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimOptions.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Core/Constant.hpp>

#include <cstdint>
#include <expected>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    ARC_CONSTANT("vim behaviour: Neovim's default 'shada' <50 -- a register over 50 lines is not persisted")
    inline constexpr std::size_t kVimPersistMaxRegisterLines = 50;
    ARC_CONSTANT("vim behaviour: Neovim's default 'shada' s10 -- a register over 10 KB is not persisted")
    inline constexpr std::size_t kVimPersistMaxRegisterBytes = 10 * 1024;
    ARC_CONSTANT("vim behaviour: Neovim's default 'history' -- 10000 entries per history")
    inline constexpr std::size_t kVimPersistMaxHistory = 10000;
    ARC_CONSTANT("size cap: the persisted per-file mark table stops at 1000 files (Arcane keeps no recency, so this bounds the file, it is not a policy)")
    inline constexpr std::size_t kVimPersistMaxFiles = 1000;
    ARC_CONSTANT("file format: the vim-state.json version")
    inline constexpr std::int32_t kVimStateFormatVersion = 1;

    struct VimPersistedState
    {
        std::vector<std::pair<char32_t, VimRegisterValue>> registers;   // a-z 0-9 -
        std::vector<std::pair<char32_t, VimGlobalMark>> globalMarks;   // A-Z
        std::map<std::string, std::map<char32_t, Point>> fileMarks;     // lowercase marks by canonical path
        std::vector<std::string> searchHistory, commandHistory;         // oldest first
    };

    [[nodiscard]] VimPersistedState CaptureVimState(const VimGlobals& globals, IVimHost& host, const VimOptions& options);
    void RestoreVimState(VimGlobals& globals, const VimPersistedState& state, IVimHost& host, const VimOptions& options);
    [[nodiscard]] std::string SerializeVimState(const VimPersistedState& state);   // applies the caps
    [[nodiscard]] std::expected<VimPersistedState, std::string> ParseVimState(std::string_view json);
    // Three-way merge for two editor instances (finding 5d.4): what this session changed since `base` (the
    // state its load applied, or its last save) wins; everything else takes `theirs` (the file as it is now).
    [[nodiscard]] VimPersistedState MergeVimState(const VimPersistedState& base, const VimPersistedState& ours,
                                                  const VimPersistedState& theirs);
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Vim/VimPersist.cpp
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimPersist.hpp"

#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimKey.hpp"   // Utf8::Append (via TextEditor/Core/Utf8.hpp)

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

#include <algorithm>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    namespace
    {
        bool Persisted(char32_t name)
        {
            return (name >= U'a' && name <= U'z') || (name >= U'0' && name <= U'9') || name == U'-';
        }

        bool WithinCaps(const VimRegisterValue& v)
        {
            const std::string text = v.Text();
            return text.size() <= kVimPersistMaxRegisterBytes
                && static_cast<std::size_t>(std::count(text.begin(), text.end(), '\n')) <= kVimPersistMaxRegisterLines;
        }

        std::string NameText(char32_t c)
        {
            std::string s;
            Utf8::Append(s, c);
            return s;
        }

        std::optional<char32_t> NameOf(const nlohmann::json& j)
        {
            if (!j.is_string()) return std::nullopt;
            const auto keys = ParseKeys(j.get<std::string>());
            if (!keys || keys->size() != 1 || !(*keys)[0].IsChar()) return std::nullopt;
            return (*keys)[0].ch;
        }

        const char* KindText(VimRegisterKind k)
        {
            switch (k)
            {
            case VimRegisterKind::Linewise:  return "V";
            case VimRegisterKind::Blockwise: return "b";
            case VimRegisterKind::Charwise:  break;
            }
            return "v";
        }

        std::vector<std::string> Newest(const std::vector<std::string>& h)
        {
            const std::size_t from = h.size() > kVimPersistMaxHistory ? h.size() - kVimPersistMaxHistory : 0;
            return std::vector<std::string>(h.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(from), h.end());
        }
    }

    VimPersistedState CaptureVimState(const VimGlobals& g, IVimHost& host, const VimOptions& options)
    {
        VimPersistedState s;
        for (const auto& [name, value] : g.registers.List(host, options))
            if (Persisted(name) && WithinCaps(value)) s.registers.emplace_back(name, value);
        s.globalMarks = g.globalMarks.List();
        s.fileMarks = g.fileMarks;
        s.searchHistory = Newest(g.searchHistory);
        s.commandHistory = Newest(g.commandHistory);
        return s;
    }

    void RestoreVimState(VimGlobals& g, const VimPersistedState& s, IVimHost& host, const VimOptions& options)
    {
        // an explicit register name stores into that register only; "0 goes last so the unnamed register
        // points at the last yank, as after a Neovim restart
        const std::pair<char32_t, VimRegisterValue>* zero = nullptr;
        for (const auto& entry : s.registers)
        {
            if (!Persisted(entry.first)) continue;
            if (entry.first == U'0') { zero = &entry; continue; }
            g.registers.Store(entry.first, entry.second, VimRegisterOp::Yank, host, options);
        }
        if (zero) g.registers.Store(U'0', zero->second, VimRegisterOp::Yank, host, options);
        for (const auto& [name, mark] : s.globalMarks) g.globalMarks.Set(name, mark);
        for (const auto& [path, marks] : s.fileMarks)
            for (const auto& [name, point] : marks) g.fileMarks[path].emplace(name, point);   // a mark set this session wins
        g.searchHistory = s.searchHistory;
        g.commandHistory = s.commandHistory;
    }

    std::string SerializeVimState(const VimPersistedState& s)
    {
        nlohmann::json j;
        j["format"] = "arcvimstate";
        j["version"] = kVimStateFormatVersion;
        nlohmann::json regs = nlohmann::json::array();
        for (const auto& [name, value] : s.registers)
        {
            if (!Persisted(name) || !WithinCaps(value)) continue;
            regs.push_back({ { "name", NameText(name) }, { "kind", KindText(value.kind) }, { "parts", value.parts } });
        }
        j["registers"] = std::move(regs);
        nlohmann::json marks = nlohmann::json::array();
        for (const auto& [name, mark] : s.globalMarks)
            marks.push_back({ { "name", NameText(name) }, { "path", mark.path }, { "row", mark.point.row }, { "col", mark.point.col } });
        j["globalMarks"] = std::move(marks);
        nlohmann::json files = nlohmann::json::object();
        std::size_t fileCount = 0;
        for (const auto& [path, byName] : s.fileMarks)
        {
            if (fileCount++ >= kVimPersistMaxFiles) break;
            nlohmann::json list = nlohmann::json::array();
            for (const auto& [name, point] : byName)
                list.push_back({ { "name", NameText(name) }, { "row", point.row }, { "col", point.col } });
            files[path] = std::move(list);
        }
        j["fileMarks"] = std::move(files);
        j["searchHistory"] = Newest(s.searchHistory);
        j["commandHistory"] = Newest(s.commandHistory);
        return j.dump(2, ' ', false, nlohmann::json::error_handler_t::replace);
    }

    std::expected<VimPersistedState, std::string> ParseVimState(std::string_view json)
    {
        const nlohmann::json j = nlohmann::json::parse(json, nullptr, false);
        if (j.is_discarded() || !j.is_object()) return std::unexpected(std::string("vim-state: not a JSON object"));
        if (j.value("format", std::string()) != "arcvimstate") return std::unexpected(std::string("vim-state: not an arcvimstate file"));
        const auto version = j.find("version");
        if (version == j.end() || !version->is_number_integer() || version->get<std::int32_t>() > kVimStateFormatVersion)
            return std::unexpected(std::string("vim-state: an unknown version"));
        VimPersistedState s;
        try
        {
            for (const nlohmann::json& r : j.value("registers", nlohmann::json::array()))
            {
                const std::optional<char32_t> name = NameOf(r.at("name"));
                if (!name || !Persisted(*name)) continue;
                VimRegisterValue v;
                v.parts = r.at("parts").get<std::vector<std::string>>();
                const std::string kind = r.at("kind").get<std::string>();
                v.kind = kind == "V" ? VimRegisterKind::Linewise : kind == "b" ? VimRegisterKind::Blockwise : VimRegisterKind::Charwise;
                if (WithinCaps(v)) s.registers.emplace_back(*name, std::move(v));
            }
            for (const nlohmann::json& m : j.value("globalMarks", nlohmann::json::array()))
            {
                const std::optional<char32_t> name = NameOf(m.at("name"));
                if (!name || *name < U'A' || *name > U'Z') continue;
                s.globalMarks.emplace_back(*name, VimGlobalMark{ m.at("path").get<std::string>(),
                                                                 Point{ m.at("row").get<std::uint32_t>(), m.at("col").get<std::uint32_t>() } });
            }
            for (const auto& [path, list] : j.value("fileMarks", nlohmann::json::object()).items())
                for (const nlohmann::json& m : list)
                    if (const std::optional<char32_t> name = NameOf(m.at("name")); name && *name >= U'a' && *name <= U'z')
                        s.fileMarks[path][*name] = Point{ m.at("row").get<std::uint32_t>(), m.at("col").get<std::uint32_t>() };
            s.searchHistory = Newest(j.value("searchHistory", std::vector<std::string>{}));
            s.commandHistory = Newest(j.value("commandHistory", std::vector<std::string>{}));
        }
        catch (const nlohmann::json::exception& e)
        {
            return std::unexpected(std::string("vim-state: ") + e.what());
        }
        return s;
    }

    namespace
    {
        // One named table (registers, global marks): theirs, then every entry this session changed since base
        // (or that theirs lacks) on top.
        template <typename V>
        std::vector<std::pair<char32_t, V>> MergeNamed(const std::vector<std::pair<char32_t, V>>& base,
                                                       const std::vector<std::pair<char32_t, V>>& ours,
                                                       const std::vector<std::pair<char32_t, V>>& theirs)
        {
            std::map<char32_t, V> was, out;
            for (const auto& [name, value] : base) was[name] = value;
            for (const auto& [name, value] : theirs) out[name] = value;
            for (const auto& [name, value] : ours)
            {
                const auto before = was.find(name);
                const bool changedHere = before == was.end() || !(before->second == value);
                if (changedHere || !out.contains(name)) out[name] = value;
            }
            return { out.begin(), out.end() };
        }

        std::vector<std::string> MergeHistory(const std::vector<std::string>& base, const std::vector<std::string>& ours,
                                              const std::vector<std::string>& theirs)
        {
            std::vector<std::string> h = theirs;
            for (const std::string& entry : ours)
                if (std::find(base.begin(), base.end(), entry) == base.end())   // typed in this session
                {
                    std::erase(h, entry);
                    h.push_back(entry);
                }
            return Newest(h);
        }
    }

    VimPersistedState MergeVimState(const VimPersistedState& base, const VimPersistedState& ours, const VimPersistedState& theirs)
    {
        VimPersistedState out;
        out.registers = MergeNamed(base.registers, ours.registers, theirs.registers);
        out.globalMarks = MergeNamed(base.globalMarks, ours.globalMarks, theirs.globalMarks);
        out.fileMarks = theirs.fileMarks;
        for (const auto& [path, marks] : ours.fileMarks)
        {
            const auto before = base.fileMarks.find(path);
            const bool changedHere = before == base.fileMarks.end() || before->second != marks;
            if (changedHere || !out.fileMarks.contains(path)) out.fileMarks[path] = marks;
        }
        out.searchHistory = MergeHistory(base.searchHistory, ours.searchHistory, theirs.searchHistory);
        out.commandHistory = MergeHistory(base.commandHistory, ours.commandHistory, theirs.commandHistory);
        return out;
    }
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimPersistence.hpp
#pragma once

// vim-state.json in the editor user folder (spec s6.4): load/save around
// VimGlobals, gated by editor.text.vim.persistState. DetachedVimHost is the
// do-nothing IVimHost the capture/restore use when no view is attached.

#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimPersist.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <optional>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    // <EditorUserDir>/TextEditor/vim-state.json; just the file name when there is no user dir (Dist).
    [[nodiscard]] std::filesystem::path VimStateFilePath();

    // Loaded / Missing: this session may write the file. Refused (unreadable, corrupt, a newer version) or
    // Disabled: it must not (finding 5d.4).
    enum class VimPersistLoad : std::uint8_t { Disabled, Missing, Loaded, Refused };
    struct VimPersistLoadResult
    {
        VimPersistLoad status = VimPersistLoad::Disabled;
        Text::VimPersistedState base;   // what the load applied: the merge base of the next save ({} when Missing)
    };
    [[nodiscard]] VimPersistLoadResult LoadVimPersistence(Text::VimGlobals& globals, const std::filesystem::path& file, bool enabled);
    // Re-reads the file and merges (MergeVimState) before writing; returns what was written (the next base),
    // or nullopt when nothing was written (disabled, no user dir, the file no longer parses, the write failed).
    [[nodiscard]] std::optional<Text::VimPersistedState> SaveVimPersistence(const Text::VimGlobals& globals, const std::filesystem::path& file,
                                                                            bool enabled, const Text::VimPersistedState& base);

    class DetachedVimHost final : public Text::IVimHost
    {
    public:
        void SetCursorShape(Text::VimCursorShape) override {}
        void SetLineMode(bool) override {}
        void SetInputEnabled(bool) override {}
        void SetClipAtLineEnds(bool) override {}
        void SetKeyboard(const Text::VimKeyboardState&) override {}
        std::uint32_t FirstVisibleRow() const override { return 0; }
        std::uint32_t VisibleRows() const override { return 1; }
        void ScrollToRow(std::uint32_t) override {}
        std::string ReadClipboard() override { return {}; }
        void WriteClipboard(std::string_view) override {}
        void ShowMessage(std::string_view, bool) override {}
        void ShowListing(std::string_view, std::span<const std::string>) override {}
        void SetCommandLine(std::string_view, std::size_t) override {}
        void SetSearchHighlight(std::string_view) override {}
        Text::VimHostResult RunFileCommand(Text::VimFileCommand, std::string_view, bool) override { return { false, "no view" }; }
        Text::VimHostResult RunWindowCommand(Text::VimWindowCommand) override { return { false, "no view" }; }
        std::optional<std::string> ReadFileText(std::string_view) override { return std::nullopt; }
        std::string DocumentPath() const override { return {}; }
        std::vector<std::string> BufferList() override { return {}; }
        bool OpenAt(std::string_view, Text::Point) override { return false; }
        Text::VimHostResult SetSessionOption(const Text::VimSessionOption&) override { return { false, "no view" }; }
    };
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimPersistence.cpp
#include "TextEditor/View/VimPersistence.hpp"

#include "Project/AssetFileOps.hpp"   // WriteTextFileAtomic

#include <Arcane/Base/Log.hpp>
#include <Arcane/Platform/Paths.hpp>

#include <fstream>
#include <sstream>
#include <system_error>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    std::filesystem::path VimStateFilePath()
    {
        const std::filesystem::path user = Paths::Get(Paths::Location::EditorUserDir);
        if (user.empty()) return std::filesystem::path("vim-state.json");
        return user / "TextEditor" / "vim-state.json";
    }

    namespace
    {
        std::optional<std::string> ReadAll(const std::filesystem::path& file)
        {
            std::ifstream in(file, std::ios::binary);
            if (!in) return std::nullopt;
            std::stringstream ss;
            ss << in.rdbuf();
            return ss.str();
        }
    }

    std::optional<Text::VimPersistedState> SaveVimPersistence(const Text::VimGlobals& globals, const std::filesystem::path& file,
                                                              bool enabled, const Text::VimPersistedState& base)
    {
        if (!enabled || !file.has_parent_path()) return std::nullopt;   // Dist (no user dir) and persistState off write nothing
        std::error_code ec;
        std::filesystem::create_directories(file.parent_path(), ec);
        if (ec) return std::nullopt;
        DetachedVimHost host;
        Text::VimPersistedState state = Text::CaptureVimState(globals, host, Text::VimOptions{});
        if (const std::optional<std::string> onDisk = ReadAll(file))   // another instance may have saved since
        {
            const auto theirs = Text::ParseVimState(*onDisk);
            if (!theirs)
            {
                ARC_WARN("vim: {} left as it is ({}); this session's vim state is not saved", file.string(), theirs.error());
                return std::nullopt;                                     // never clobber a newer or broken file
            }
            state = Text::MergeVimState(base, state, *theirs);
        }
        if (!WriteTextFileAtomic(file, Text::SerializeVimState(state))) return std::nullopt;
        return state;
    }

    VimPersistLoadResult LoadVimPersistence(Text::VimGlobals& globals, const std::filesystem::path& file, bool enabled)
    {
        if (!enabled) return VimPersistLoadResult{ VimPersistLoad::Disabled, {} };
        const std::optional<std::string> text = ReadAll(file);
        if (!text)
        {
            std::error_code ec;
            if (std::filesystem::exists(file, ec)) return VimPersistLoadResult{ VimPersistLoad::Refused, {} };   // there but unreadable
            return VimPersistLoadResult{ VimPersistLoad::Missing, {} };
        }
        const auto state = Text::ParseVimState(*text);
        if (!state)
        {
            ARC_WARN("vim: {} not loaded ({}); it will not be overwritten this session", file.string(), state.error());
            return VimPersistLoadResult{ VimPersistLoad::Refused, {} };
        }
        DetachedVimHost host;
        Text::RestoreVimState(globals, *state, host, Text::VimOptions{});
        return VimPersistLoadResult{ VimPersistLoad::Loaded, *state };
    }
}
```

(`ARC_WARN` is defined in `ArcaneCore/src/Arcane/Base/Log.hpp:173`; `Window.cpp:4` includes it the same way.)

In `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/View/VimEditorRuntime.hpp` (TE5a-23), add to the public section:

```cpp
        // TE5d-6: vim-state.json (editor.text.vim.persistState). Load runs once per process.
        void LoadPersistedStateOnce();
        void SavePersistedState();
```

and the private members `bool m_persistTried = false;`, `bool m_persistWritable = false;`, `Text::VimPersistedState m_persistBase;`. In `VimEditorRuntime.cpp` (`#include "TextEditor/View/VimPersistence.hpp"`):

```cpp
    void VimEditorRuntime::LoadPersistedStateOnce()
    {
        if (m_persistTried) return;
        m_persistTried = true;
        VimPersistLoadResult r = LoadVimPersistence(Globals(), VimStateFilePath(), Settings<TextVimSettings>().persistState);
        // only a file this session read (or that does not exist yet) may be written: a Refused file -- newer
        // version, corrupt, unreadable -- is left alone for the whole session (finding 5d.4)
        m_persistWritable = r.status == VimPersistLoad::Loaded || r.status == VimPersistLoad::Missing;
        m_persistBase = std::move(r.base);
    }

    void VimEditorRuntime::SavePersistedState()
    {
        if (!m_persistWritable) return;
        if (std::optional<Text::VimPersistedState> written =
                SaveVimPersistence(Globals(), VimStateFilePath(), Settings<TextVimSettings>().persistState, m_persistBase))
            m_persistBase = std::move(*written);   // the next save merges against what is on disk now
    }
```

While vim is on, a text document gives some chords to vim instead of the action table (the s6.6 table; with `handleCtrlKeys` off only `Esc` and `Ctrl+[`). The page says so beside each action whose bound chord vim claims in at least one mode: "Normal: half page down; Visual: half page down; Insert: outdent line" -- the modes listed are exactly those where `VimClaimsChord` is true, so the column follows `handleCtrlKeys` and any later change to the table. In `ArcaneEditor/src/Settings/ShortcutsPage.cpp` (`#include "TextEditor/TextSettings.hpp"` and `#include <Arcane/Config/Settings.hpp>` join the includes), add above `BuildShortcutRows`:

```cpp
    std::string FormatVimChordMeaning(const Arcane::Text::VimChordRow& row, const Arcane::Text::VimOptions& options)
    {
        using Arcane::Text::VimMode;
        std::string out;
        const auto add = [&](VimMode mode, std::string_view label, std::string_view meaning) {
            if (!Arcane::Text::VimClaimsChord(row.chord, mode, options)) return;
            if (!out.empty()) out += "; ";
            out += std::string(label) + ": " + std::string(meaning);
        };
        add(VimMode::Normal, "Normal", row.normal);
        add(VimMode::Visual, "Visual", row.visual);
        add(VimMode::Insert, "Insert", row.insert);
        return out;
    }

    std::string VimMeaningOfChord(const KeyChord& chord, const Arcane::Text::VimOptions& options)
    {
        if (!chord.Bound() || chord.type != KeyType::Labelled || chord.alt || chord.super || chord.shift) return {};
        Arcane::Text::VimKey key;
        if (!chord.ctrl && chord.key == Arcane::Keys::kEscape) key = Arcane::Text::VimKey::Named(Arcane::Text::VimNamedKey::Esc);
        else if (chord.ctrl && ((chord.key >= 'a' && chord.key <= 'z') || chord.key == '['))
            key = Arcane::Text::VimKey::Ctrl(static_cast<char32_t>(chord.key));   // a Labelled letter is its Latin letter (spec s5.5)
        else return {};
        for (const Arcane::Text::VimChordRow& row : Arcane::Text::VimChordTable())
            if (row.chord == key) return FormatVimChordMeaning(row, options);
        return {};
    }
```

### Task TE5d-8: The hand-written multi-cursor vim table (spec s11.3 "Multi-cursor vim cases are hand-written")

**Files:**
- Create: `ArcaneTests/data/vim/multicursor.vimcases`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/VimMulticursorTableTest.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the `.vimcases` format and runner (TE5a-6; `in:` may hold several cursors only in an `@handwritten` file), `ParseVimCaseFile`, `ParseVimMarked`; the multi-cursor behaviour of every TE5a-TE5c command it exercises; TE5b-1's paste distribution.
- Produces: `ArcaneTests/data/vim/multicursor.vimcases` (33 cases), the `[text-vim-multicursor]` structural test.

Neovim has no multi-cursor, so these expectations are derived by hand from one rule: **each cursor behaves as a single-cursor vim would on its own text, then selections merge** (spec s2.1, s6.2, s11.3) -- with the two multi-cursor register rules of s6.3 (a yank stores one entry per cursor; a paste with an equal cursor count distributes, otherwise every cursor pastes the whole register). Where two cursors' operator ranges are identical or overlap (two cursors in one word, two on one line), the edits collapse before they apply -- identical ranges once, overlapping deletions as their union (`VimText::DisjointOps`, TE5b-6; finding 5d.7) -- which is what running each cursor on its own text and merging gives. The derivation of every case is written in its name. The oracle skips the file (`@handwritten`, TE5a-7); TE5d-9 reviews it as its own task.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** -- the table:

```
# ArcaneTests/data/vim/multicursor.vimcases
# Hand-written (spec s11.3): Neovim has no multi-cursor. Rule: each cursor behaves as a single-cursor vim
# would on its own text, then selections merge (spec s2.1, s6.2). Registers (s6.3): a yank keeps one entry per
# cursor; a paste with an equal cursor count distributes them, otherwise each cursor pastes the whole register.
@handwritten
@grammar plain
@set tabstop=4 shiftwidth=4 expandtab

=== x: each cursor deletes its own character
keys: x
in: "ˇabc\nˇdef"
out: "ˇbc\nˇef"
mode: n

=== x: adjacent cursors each delete one char, then land on one position and merge
keys: x
in: "ˇaˇbc"
out: "ˇc"
mode: n

=== dw: two cursors on one line each delete their word
keys: dw
in: "ˇfoo bar ˇbaz qux"
out: "ˇbar ˇqux"
mode: n

=== w: each cursor moves to its next word
keys: w
in: "ˇfoo bar\nˇbaz qux"
out: "foo ˇbar\nbaz ˇqux"
mode: n

=== 2w: the count applies per cursor
keys: 2w
in: "ˇa b c\nˇd e f"
out: "a b ˇc\nd e ˇf"
mode: n

=== $: each cursor goes to its own line end
keys: $
in: "ˇab\nˇcdef"
out: "aˇb\ncdeˇf"
mode: n

=== k: the top cursor cannot move, the other reaches it, they merge
keys: k
in: "ˇa\nˇb"
out: "ˇa\nb"
mode: n

=== 0: two cursors on one line both reach column 0 and merge
keys: 0
in: "aˇbˇc"
out: "ˇabc"
mode: n

=== f,: each cursor finds the comma on its line
keys: f,
in: "ˇa,b\nˇc,d"
out: "aˇ,b\ncˇ,d"
mode: n

=== ciw: each word changes, the same text is typed at every cursor
keys: ciwX<Esc>
in: "ˇfoo bar\nˇbaz"
out: "ˇX bar\nˇX"
mode: n

=== A: each cursor appends at its own line end
keys: A;<Esc>
in: "ˇa\nˇb"
out: "aˇ;\nbˇ;"
mode: n

=== I: each cursor inserts before its own first non-blank
keys: I// <Esc>
in: "  ˇa\nˇb"
out: "  //ˇ a\n//ˇ b"
mode: n

=== o: each cursor opens a line below its own
keys: ox<Esc>
in: "ˇa\nˇb"
out: "a\nˇx\nb\nˇx"
mode: n

=== a Enter: each cursor splits its line
keys: a<CR><Esc>
in: "ˇab\nˇcd"
out: "a\nˇb\nc\nˇd"
mode: n

=== dd: both lines go, both cursors land on the remaining line and merge
keys: dd
in: "ˇa\nˇb\nc"
out: "ˇc"
mode: n

=== Vd: each cursor's line goes; the cursors stay on the lines that moved up
keys: Vd
in: "ˇa\nb\nˇc\nd"
out: "ˇb\nˇd"
mode: n

=== yy p: one register entry per cursor, distributed to the same cursor count
keys: yyp
in: "ˇa\nˇb"
out: "a\nˇa\nb\nˇb"
mode: n

=== yiw w P: each cursor pastes the word it yanked
keys: yiwwP
in: "ˇfoo bar\nˇbaz qux"
out: "foo foˇobar\nbaz baˇzqux"
mode: n

=== "ap: a one-entry register is pasted whole at every cursor
setreg: a v "X"
keys: "ap
in: "ˇab\nˇcd"
out: "aˇXb\ncˇXd"
mode: n

=== x then .: the repeat runs at every cursor
keys: x.
in: "ˇa b\nˇc d"
out: "ˇb\nˇd"
mode: n

=== ix Esc then .: the inserted text repeats at every cursor
keys: ix<Esc>.
in: "ˇa\nˇb"
out: "ˇxxa\nˇxxb"
mode: n

=== >>: each cursor indents its own line
keys: >>
in: "ˇa\nˇb"
out: "    ˇa\n    ˇb"
mode: n

=== gUiw: each word under a cursor is uppercased
keys: gUiw
in: "ˇfoo bar ˇbaz"
out: "ˇFOO bar ˇBAZ"
mode: n

=== ~: each cursor toggles its character and steps right
keys: ~
in: "ˇab\nˇcd"
out: "Aˇb\nCˇd"
mode: n

=== rx: each cursor's character is replaced
keys: rx
in: "ˇab\nˇcd"
out: "ˇxb\nˇxd"
mode: n

=== J: each cursor joins its line with the next
keys: J
in: "ˇa\nb\nˇc\nd"
out: "aˇ b\ncˇ d"
mode: n

=== viwd: each cursor selects and deletes its own word
keys: viwd
in: "ˇfoo bar\nˇbaz qux"
out: "ˇ bar\nˇ qux"
mode: n

=== vl: Visual keeps one selection per cursor
keys: vl
in: "ˇabc\nˇdef"
out: "«aˇbc\n«dˇef"
mode: v

=== gb gb: the word under the cursor, then its next occurrence
keys: gbgb
in: "ˇfoo x foo y foo"
out: "«foˇo x «foˇo y foo"
mode: v

=== gb gb c: both occurrences change together
keys: gbgbcbar<Esc>
in: "ˇfoo x foo y foo"
out: "baˇr x baˇr y foo"
mode: n

=== diw: two cursors in one word delete it once (identical ranges collapse), then merge
keys: diw
in: "ˇfoˇo bar"
out: "ˇ bar"
mode: n

=== dd: two cursors on one line delete it once, then merge
keys: dd
in: "aˇbˇc\nd"
out: "ˇd"
mode: n

=== d2w: overlapping deletions from two cursors become their union, then merge
keys: d2w
in: "ˇa ˇb c d"
out: "ˇd"
mode: n
```

### Task TE5d-9: Review of the multi-cursor table, as its own task (spec s11.3 "reviewed as their own task")

**Files:**
- Create: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/VimMulticursorDeriveTest.cpp`
- Modify (only if the review finds a wrong derivation): `ArcaneTests/data/vim/multicursor.vimcases`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `multicursor.vimcases` (TE5d-8), `ParseVimCaseFile`, `ParseVimMarked`, `FormatVimMarked`, `VimRig`, `ApplyVimSet`, `VimCaseLanguage` (TE5a-6).
- Produces: the `[text-vim-multicursor-derive]` mechanical cross-check and the review record (in the task report).

The reviewer is not the author of TE5d-8 (a different agent or person). The review has two halves. **Mechanical:** for every case whose cursors all start on different lines, whose keys are line-local (no registers, paste, repeat, `gb`, joins, opens or line deletes) and whose line count does not change, the test runs a single-cursor rig on each line alone and checks that the multi-cursor result line equals it -- the rule, executed. **Manual,** for every case, recorded as one verdict line per case in the report: (1) the derivation in the case name matches the rule; (2) where cursors meet, the expected merge is what SelectionSet's merge rule produces (s3.4: overlapping, same start, or touching); (3) register cases follow s6.3 (per-cursor entries; distribute on equal count, else whole register at each cursor); (4) the same keys on a single cursor agree with the oracle tables (`te5a`/`te5b`/`te5c`) wherever those tables hold the same command; (5) the categories are covered: motions, operators, text objects, registers/paste distribution, dot-repeat, Insert typing, `gb`, Visual, merge on collision, identical and overlapping operator ranges (finding 5d.7). A disagreement is fixed in the table (or, when the table is right, in the command) before the commit.

```cpp
namespace
{
    bool OneCursorPerLine(const std::string& marked)
    {
        const MarkedText m = ParseVimMarked(marked);
        std::set<std::ptrdiff_t> rows;
        for (const VimCursor& c : m.cursors)
            if (!rows.insert(std::count(m.text.begin(), m.text.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(c.head), '\n')).second) return false;
        return true;
    }

    std::vector<std::string> SplitLines(const std::string& s)
    {
        std::vector<std::string> out(1);
        for (const char c : s) { if (c == '\n') out.emplace_back(); else out.back().push_back(c); }
        return out;
    }

    // Keys whose effect stays on the cursor's own line and never reads another cursor's work.
    bool LineLocal(std::string_view keys)
    {
        for (const std::string_view bad : { "y", "p", "P", "\"", ".", "gb", "J", "o", "O", "dd", "<CR>", "V" })
            if (keys.find(bad) != std::string_view::npos) return false;
        return true;
    }

    // The case text split per line, with each line's cursor (if any) as a marked single-cursor line.
    std::vector<std::string> MarkedLines(const std::string& marked)
    {
        const MarkedText m = ParseVimMarked(marked);
        const std::vector<std::string> lines = SplitLines(m.text);
        std::vector<std::string> out;
        ByteOffset lineStart = 0;
        for (const std::string& line : lines)
        {
            std::vector<VimCursor> here;
            for (const VimCursor& c : m.cursors)
                if (c.head >= lineStart && c.head <= lineStart + line.size()) here.push_back(VimCursor{ c.head - lineStart, c.head - lineStart });
            out.push_back(here.size() == 1 ? FormatVimMarked(line, here, false) : line);
            lineStart += line.size() + 1;
        }
        return out;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("multi-cursor table: line-local cases equal one single-cursor run per line", "[text-vim-multicursor-derive]")
{
    std::ifstream in(RepoRoot() / "ArcaneTests" / "data" / "vim" / "multicursor.vimcases", std::ios::binary);
    REQUIRE(in.good());
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << in.rdbuf();
    const VimCaseFile f = ParseVimCaseFile(ss.str(), "multicursor.vimcases");
    std::size_t derived = 0;
    for (const VimCase& c : f.cases)
    {
        const MarkedText before = ParseVimMarked(c.in);
        const MarkedText after = ParseVimMarked(c.out);
        const std::vector<std::string> inLines = MarkedLines(c.in), outLines = MarkedLines(c.out);
        if (!LineLocal(c.keys) || c.out.find("\xC2\xAB") != std::string::npos || !c.setregs.empty()) continue;
        if (inLines.size() != outLines.size() || before.cursors.size() != after.cursors.size()) continue;
        if (!OneCursorPerLine(c.in) || !OneCursorPerLine(c.out)) continue;
        ++derived;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < inLines.size(); ++i)
        {
            if (inLines[i].find("\xCB\x87") == std::string::npos) continue;
            VimOptions options;
            for (const std::string& s : f.sets) REQUIRE(ApplyVimSet(options, s));
            VimRig single(inLines[i], VimCaseLanguage(c.grammar), options);
            single.Keys(c.keys);
            INFO(c.line << " " << c.name << " -- line " << i);
            CHECK(single.Marked() == outLines[i]);
        }
    }
    CHECK(derived >= 10u);   // the table keeps a real body of mechanically derived cases
}
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("vim coverage: the command probe sees parsed commands only", "[text-vim-coverage]")
{
    std::vector<std::pair<VimCmdKind, std::uint16_t>> ran;
    VimState::SetCommandProbe([&ran](VimCmdKind kind, std::uint16_t id) { ran.emplace_back(kind, id); });
    struct ProbeOff { ~ProbeOff() { VimState::SetCommandProbe({}); } } off;   // never leak into a later case
    VimRig r("\xCB\x87" "ab");
    r.Keys("ixq<Esc>");                                   // Insert text: no x, no q command
    const auto has = [&ran](VimCmdKind k, auto id) {
        return std::find(ran.begin(), ran.end(), std::make_pair(k, static_cast<std::uint16_t>(id))) != ran.end();
    };
    CHECK(has(VimCmdKind::Action, VimActionId::InsertBefore));
    CHECK_FALSE(has(VimCmdKind::Action, VimActionId::DeleteChar));
    CHECK_FALSE(has(VimCmdKind::Action, VimActionId::RecordMacro));
    r.Keys("dw");                                         // an operator command reports its motion and its operator
    CHECK(has(VimCmdKind::Operator, VimOperatorId::Delete));
    CHECK(has(VimCmdKind::Motion, VimMotionId::WordFwd));
}

TEST_CASE("vim coverage: every command in the key table is run by an oracle case", "[text-vim-coverage]")
{
    std::set<std::pair<VimCmdKind, std::uint16_t>> covered, all;
    VimState::SetCommandProbe([&covered](VimCmdKind kind, std::uint16_t id) { covered.emplace(kind, id); });
    struct ProbeOff { ~ProbeOff() { VimState::SetCommandProbe({}); } } off;
    for (const auto& e : std::filesystem::directory_iterator(RepoRoot() / "ArcaneTests" / "data" / "vim"))
    {
        if (e.path().extension() != ".vimcases") continue;
        std::ifstream in(e.path(), std::ios::binary);
        std::stringstream ss;
        ss << in.rdbuf();
        const VimCaseFile f = ParseVimCaseFile(ss.str(), e.path().filename().string());
        if (f.handwritten) continue;                      // multicursor.vimcases is not an oracle table
        for (const VimCase& c : f.cases)
        {
            INFO(e.path().filename().string() << ":" << c.line << " " << c.name);
            RunVimCase(f, c);                             // runs (and checks) the case; the probe records its commands
        }
    }
    const auto bindings = VimBindings();
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < bindings.size(); ++i) all.emplace(bindings[i].kind, bindings[i].id);
    std::string missing;
    for (const auto& id : all)
        if (!covered.contains(id) && !kExempt.contains(id))
        {
            std::string sample;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < bindings.size(); ++i)
                if (bindings[i].kind == id.first && bindings[i].id == id.second) { sample = std::string(bindings[i].keys); break; }
            missing += "  " + sample + "\n";
        }
    INFO("commands no oracle case runs (add one to the owning pass's table, oracle-verified):\n" << missing);
    CHECK(missing.empty());
}
```

### Chunk TE5 integration notes (read before executing any TE5 task)

The passes were written against one cross-pass contract; these reconciliations are already applied to the task text above and override the contract wording where they differ:

1. **Linewise ranges use the content form.** A `MotionKind::Linewise` `VimOpTarget` or `VimObjectRange` is `[LineStart(first), LineEnd(last))`, built with `VimLinewiseTarget` and read back with `VimLinewiseRows` (TE5a-12). `RunOperator` expands it to `VimCursorModel::LinewiseDeleteRange` itself. The delete form cannot be told apart from a range that ends next to an empty row. TE5a-16 (`ip`/`ap`, `LinewiseRows`), TE5a-17 (whole-line inner blocks) and TE5a-18 (VisualLine object targets) use it. TE5c-7's `:d`/`:y` compute `LinewiseDeleteRange` directly and apply it without `RunOperator`, which is consistent.
2. **Operator + text object** goes through `VimState::ExecuteObjectOperator` (TE5a-16). It handles the outcome exactly as `ExecuteOperator` does (failure beep, `autoIndentPending`). TE5a-12's `TextObject` branch inside `ExecuteOperator` stays as a beep that `Execute`'s routing never reaches.
3. **Registers.** TE5b-1's full rewrite keeps `VimRegisters::Preload` (the `.vimcases` `setreg:` column and TE5d-6's restore). Its new file is `VimPutRegister.cpp`, because `VimPut.cpp` belongs to TE5a-12. `VimUsesRegisterOne` also covers `* # g* g#`, which run through vim's `normal_search` like `/` and `n`.
4. **Insert undo.** TE5b-3 replaces the two `InsertUndoRedo` calls in `HandleInsertCtrl` (TE5a-20) with `UndoCommand(1)` / `RedoCommand(1)` and deletes `InsertUndoRedo`.
5. **Status strip.** TE5b-5a (serial, after TE5a-22; D-R11 X2) adds "recording @q" inside `VimViewAdapter::PublishStatus` (TE5a-22) through `VimRecordingStatusText`; TE5b-5 (lane L7) only provides `RecordingRegister()`.
6. **Host interface.** TE5d-2 adds the pure virtual `IVimHost::SetSessionOption`. The same task updates `FakeVimHost`, `VimViewAdapter` and TE5d-6's `DetachedVimHost`.
7. **Command-line editor.** It lands in TE5c-5 (`/` and `?` need it first). TE5c-6 adds `:`. Per TE5a-20, a command line that returns to Normal calls `MaybeRestartInsert()`, so `Ctrl-O :cmd<CR>` returns to Insert.
8. **Two join implementations.** `:j` (TE5c-7, `JoinRowsText`) and `J`/`gJ` (TE5a-13) implement vim's `do_join` separately, and the oracle cases for both pin the same rules. The TE5c-7 reviewer checks the two against each other. Merging them into one function is the first follow-up after VIM-GATE.
9. **Deferred document operations.** Every document or window operation vim asks for (`:q`, `:e`, splits, `:bn`, global marks into another file) is queued by `VimViewAdapter` and run once per frame after `DocumentHost::DrawAll` (TE5a-22). Running it inside the key dispatch could destroy the `VimState` that is still on the call stack.

**Not placed, or placed as documented divergences** (each is listed in `VimDivergences()` (TE5c-16) and the oracle's divergence notes):
- `=` uses the grammar's indent rules (a divergence the spec declares).
- Two-cell wide glyphs: one cell per grapheme (`virtual columns`). (Neovim's per-script CJK / emoji word classes and Latin-1 `iskeyword` are PORTED by TE5a-3's `VimCharClass`, so they are no longer divergences.)
- `%` ignores `/* */` and `#if`. Paragraph boundaries ignore nroff macros. `J` removes only the grammar's line-comment leader, not Neovim's whole `comments` list.
- Text objects do not skip brackets inside strings. A block edge inside a tab is not split. Visual `I`/`A` outside VisualBlock beep.
- A macro in a register reads `<Esc>`, not the raw byte. A line break in register text runs as `<CR>`. `'A` into a closed file lands on column 0. Blockwise put uses the primary cursor only.
- `:s///c` inside `:g` is refused in v1. `\%V` in VisualBlock is approximated by the block's charwise span. `'report'` messages are approximated.
- Spec gaps:
  - s6.4 (amended, CANON D26): shift width IS `editor.text.tabSize` (one indent width). `ts` and `sw` both map onto it and move together.
  - s6.4 sets no caps for persisted state. TE5d-6 uses Neovim's `shada` sizes as `ARC_CONSTANT`s.
  - s4.2's windowed matching of lines past `longLineMaxBytes` is not done on the vim search path: it copies the whole row, correctness first. Windowed matching stays the find bar's job (TE4).
- Jumps made by an operator's motion (`dG`, `d/foo`) do not enter the jump list. Search jumps do, through `RecordJump`.
- Plan revision 2 (finding 5c.8, 5c.2, TE5a's 5a.6) added eight `VimDivergences()` rows -- `Visual * and #`, `Visual @ and Q`, `position predicates` (no backtracking into another alternative), `:s flag` (`n p # l r`), the `:s` replacement `\=` row, `:sort flag` (`x o b f`), `backwards range`, `:normal key notation` -- and reworded `smartcase` (non-ASCII capitals beyond VimMapCase's table): 49 rows, and TE5c-16's behaviour-rows test lists 20 items. A named key or chord with no vim meaning that a mapping produces in Insert is dropped (Neovim would insert an unknown control character literally).
- `<Insert>` reaches vim (cross-fix X24; TE5a-19 toggles Insert/Replace in one session). Two edges are Arcane's own rule rather than oracle-checked: `.` after a session that toggled repeats its start command with the captured text (TE5b-4's record), not the toggle key by key, and Backspace after a toggle restores only what the current Replace part overtyped.

```cpp
// ArcaneTests/src/Text/TextViewStateTest.cpp
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
#include "TextEditor/Document/TextViewState.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <string>

using namespace Arcane::Editor;

TEST_CASE("view state store: round-trips every field through the file", "[text-viewstate]")
{
    const auto file = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "arcane-viewstate" / "TextViewState.json";
    std::filesystem::remove_all(file.parent_path());
    TextViewStateStore store;
    TextViewState s;
    s.cursorRow = 41; s.cursorCol = 7; s.topRow = 30;
    s.folds = { { 3, 9 }, { 50, 60 } };
    s.split = true; s.splitVertical = false; s.splitTopRow = 400;
    s.encoding = "windows-1252";
    s.lastUsed = 1000;
    store.Put("D:/Proj/Config/Game.INI", s);
    REQUIRE(store.Save(file));

    const TextViewStateStore back = TextViewStateStore::Load(file);
    const auto got = back.Get("d:/proj/config/game.ini");                  // case-insensitive key
    REQUIRE(got);
    CHECK(got->cursorRow == 41); CHECK(got->cursorCol == 7); CHECK(got->topRow == 30);
    CHECK(got->folds == s.folds);
    CHECK(got->split); CHECK_FALSE(got->splitVertical); CHECK(got->splitTopRow == 400);
    CHECK(got->encoding == "windows-1252");
}

TEST_CASE("view state store: prune keeps the most recently used", "[text-viewstate]")
{
    TextViewStateStore store;
    for (std::uint64_t i = 0; i < 10; ++i)
    {
        TextViewState s;
        s.lastUsed = i;
        store.Put("C:/f" + std::to_string(i) + ".txt", s);
    }
    store.Prune(3);
    CHECK(store.Size() == 3);
    CHECK(store.Get("C:/f9.txt"));
    CHECK(store.Get("C:/f7.txt"));
    CHECK_FALSE(store.Get("C:/f6.txt"));
}

TEST_CASE("view state store: a missing or corrupt file loads empty, never throws", "[text-viewstate]")
{
    const auto dir = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "arcane-viewstate-bad";
    std::filesystem::create_directories(dir);
    CHECK(TextViewStateStore::Load(dir / "nope.json").Size() == 0);
    { std::ofstream(dir / "bad.json") << "{ not json"; }
    CHECK(TextViewStateStore::Load(dir / "bad.json").Size() == 0);
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Document/TextViewState.hpp
#pragma once
// Per-file view state (text editor spec s5.3 "Session restore"): cursor,
// scroll, folds, split, chosen encoding -- one JSON file in the editor user
// dir (Paths EditorUserDir), keyed by the canonical path, LRU-capped by
// editor.text.viewStateMaxFiles. Written atomically; a bad file loads empty.
#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <map>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    struct TextViewState
    {
        std::uint32_t cursorRow = 0, cursorCol = 0;   // primary caret, byte column
        std::uint32_t topRow = 0;                     // first visible buffer row, primary view
        // Closed folds of the primary view as { headerRow, lastRow } buffer rows
        // (Text::FoldRange; the fold hides headerRow+1..lastRow).
        std::vector<std::pair<std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t>> folds;
        bool          split = false;
        bool          splitVertical = true;
        std::uint32_t splitTopRow = 0;                // first visible buffer row, secondary view
        std::string   encoding;                       // Text::EncodingId ("utf-8", "windows-1252", ...); "" = detect on open
        std::uint64_t lastUsed = 0;                   // unix seconds
    };

    class TextViewStateStore
    {
    public:
        [[nodiscard]] static TextViewStateStore Load(const std::filesystem::path& file);
        bool Save(const std::filesystem::path& file) const;
        [[nodiscard]] std::optional<TextViewState> Get(std::string_view canonicalPath) const;
        void Put(std::string_view canonicalPath, TextViewState state);
        void Prune(std::size_t maxFiles);
        [[nodiscard]] std::size_t Size() const noexcept { return m_states.size(); }

    private:
        static std::string Key(std::string_view path);
        std::map<std::string, TextViewState> m_states;
    };

    [[nodiscard]] std::filesystem::path TextViewStateFile();   // <EditorUserDir>/TextViewState.json; empty in Dist
}
```

```cpp
// ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Document/TextViewState.cpp
#include "TextEditor/Document/TextViewState.hpp"

#include <Arcane/Platform/Paths.hpp>
#include <Json.hpp>

#include <algorithm>
#include <fstream>
#include <sstream>

#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <Windows.h>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    std::string TextViewStateStore::Key(std::string_view path)
    {
        std::string k(path);
        std::replace(k.begin(), k.end(), '\\', '/');
        for (char& c : k) c = static_cast<char>(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)));
        return k;
    }

    std::filesystem::path TextViewStateFile()
    {
        return Paths::Join(Paths::Location::EditorUserDir, Paths::Current(), "TextViewState.json");
    }

    TextViewStateStore TextViewStateStore::Load(const std::filesystem::path& file)
    {
        TextViewStateStore store;
        std::ifstream f(file, std::ios::binary);
        if (!f) return store;
        std::stringstream ss;
        ss << f.rdbuf();
        const nlohmann::json j = nlohmann::json::parse(ss.str(), nullptr, false);
        if (!j.is_object() || j.value("version", 0) != 1 || !j.contains("files") || !j["files"].is_object())
            return store;
        for (const auto& [key, v] : j["files"].items())
        {
            if (!v.is_object()) continue;
            TextViewState s;
            s.cursorRow = v.value("cursorRow", 0u);
            s.cursorCol = v.value("cursorCol", 0u);
            s.topRow = v.value("topRow", 0u);
            if (v.contains("folds") && v["folds"].is_array())
                for (const auto& r : v["folds"])
                    if (r.is_array() && r.size() == 2 && r[0].is_number_unsigned() && r[1].is_number_unsigned())
                        s.folds.emplace_back(r[0].get<std::uint32_t>(), r[1].get<std::uint32_t>());
            s.split = v.value("split", false);
            s.splitVertical = v.value("splitVertical", true);
            s.splitTopRow = v.value("splitTopRow", 0u);
            s.encoding = v.value("encoding", std::string{});
            s.lastUsed = v.value("lastUsed", std::uint64_t{ 0 });
            store.m_states[key] = std::move(s);
        }
        return store;
    }

    bool TextViewStateStore::Save(const std::filesystem::path& file) const
    {
        if (file.empty()) return false;
        nlohmann::json j;
        j["version"] = 1;
        j["files"] = nlohmann::json::object();
        for (const auto& [key, s] : m_states)
        {
            nlohmann::json folds = nlohmann::json::array();
            for (const auto& [a, b] : s.folds) folds.push_back({ a, b });
            j["files"][key] = { { "cursorRow", s.cursorRow }, { "cursorCol", s.cursorCol }, { "topRow", s.topRow },
                                { "folds", folds }, { "split", s.split }, { "splitVertical", s.splitVertical },
                                { "splitTopRow", s.splitTopRow }, { "encoding", s.encoding }, { "lastUsed", s.lastUsed } };
        }
        std::error_code ec;
        std::filesystem::create_directories(file.parent_path(), ec);
        const std::filesystem::path tmp = file.string() + ".tmp";
        {
            std::ofstream out(tmp, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
            if (!out) return false;
            out << j.dump(1);
            if (!out) return false;
        }
        return ::MoveFileExW(tmp.c_str(), file.c_str(), MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH) != 0;
    }

    std::optional<TextViewState> TextViewStateStore::Get(std::string_view canonicalPath) const
    {
        const auto it = m_states.find(Key(canonicalPath));
        if (it == m_states.end()) return std::nullopt;
        return it->second;
    }

    void TextViewStateStore::Put(std::string_view canonicalPath, TextViewState state)
    {
        m_states[Key(canonicalPath)] = std::move(state);
    }

    void TextViewStateStore::Prune(std::size_t maxFiles)
    {
        if (m_states.size() <= maxFiles) return;
        std::vector<std::pair<std::uint64_t, std::string>> byAge;
        for (const auto& [k, s] : m_states) byAge.emplace_back(s.lastUsed, k);
        std::sort(byAge.begin(), byAge.end());
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i + maxFiles < byAge.size(); ++i)
            m_states.erase(byAge[i].second);
    }
}
```

`TextDocument.cpp` (add `#include "TextEditor/Core/Graphemes.hpp"`, `<algorithm>`, `<chrono>`):

```cpp
    TextDocument::~TextDocument()
    {
        if (m_services.saveViewState)
            m_services.saveViewState(CanonicalPath(), CaptureViewState());
    }

    TextViewState TextDocument::CaptureViewState()
    {
        TextViewState s;
        Model().SyncDisplay();                                     // folds -> display map before reading rows
        const Text::Rope& rope = Buffer().Text();
        TextEditorView& view = View();
        const Text::Point head = rope.OffsetToPoint(view.Selections().Primary().head);
        s.cursorRow = head.row;
        s.cursorCol = head.col;                                    // bytes (Text::Point)
        s.topRow = view.Display().DisplayRowToBuffer(view.FirstVisibleDisplayRow());
        for (const Text::FoldRange& f : view.Folds().Folded(rope))
            s.folds.emplace_back(f.headerRow, f.lastRow);
        s.split = SplitOpen();
        s.splitVertical = SplitVertical();
        if (TextEditorView* second = SecondaryView())
        {
            ModelOf(*second).SyncDisplay();
            s.splitTopRow = second->Display().DisplayRowToBuffer(second->FirstVisibleDisplayRow());
        }
        s.encoding = std::string(Text::EncodingId(Encoding()));
        s.lastUsed = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::seconds>(
            std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count());
        return s;
    }

    void TextDocument::ApplyViewState(const TextViewState& s)
    {
        // 1. Encoding first: the rows below are counted in the decoded text.
        if (const std::optional<Text::TextEncoding> enc = Text::EncodingFromId(s.encoding); enc && *enc != Encoding())
        {
            const bool hadNote = !Note().empty();
            if (ReopenWithEncoding(*enc) && !hadNote)
                ShowNote("");                                      // its "undo history cleared" note means nothing on a fresh open
            // A refused reopen keeps the detected encoding; the rest still applies.
        }

        const Text::Rope& rope = Buffer().Text();
        const std::uint32_t lastRow = rope.LineCount() - 1;

        // 2. Cursor: clamp the row, clamp the byte column to the line, snap back
        //    to the grapheme boundary at or before it (a shrunk or re-decoded
        //    line may put the old column inside a character).
        const std::uint32_t row = std::min(s.cursorRow, lastRow);
        const Text::ByteOffset lineStart = rope.LineStart(row);
        const Text::ByteOffset want = lineStart + std::min(s.cursorCol, rope.LineLength(row));
        Text::ByteOffset at = lineStart;
        while (at < want)
        {
            const Text::ByteOffset next = Text::NextGraphemeBoundary(rope, at);
            if (next > want) break;
            at = next;
        }
        Model().selections.SetSingle(at, at);

        // 3. Folds (primary view): { headerRow, lastRow } pairs still inside the file.
        Text::FoldModel& folds = View().Folds();
        for (const auto& [headerRow, foldLastRow] : s.folds)
            if (headerRow < foldLastRow && foldLastRow <= lastRow)
                (void)folds.Fold(rope, Text::FoldRange{ headerRow, foldLastRow }, Text::FoldSource::Manual);
        Model().SyncDisplay();

        // 4. Top row (a buffer row) -> the display row under the restored folds.
        TextEditorView& view = View();
        view.SetFirstVisibleDisplayRow(view.Display().BufferRowToDisplay(std::min(s.topRow, lastRow)));

        // 5. Split + its top row.
        if (s.split && !SplitOpen())
            OpenSplit(s.splitVertical);
        if (s.split)
            if (TextEditorView* second = SecondaryView())
            {
                ModelOf(*second).SyncDisplay();
                second->SetFirstVisibleDisplayRow(second->Display().BufferRowToDisplay(std::min(s.splitTopRow, lastRow)));
            }
    }
```

```cpp
    void EditorApp::AddTextViewStateServices(Arcane::Editor::TextDocumentServices& sv)
    {
        // Gated when called, so toggling editor.text.rememberViewState applies
        // to the next open / close without re-registering the factories.
        sv.loadViewState = [this](const std::filesystem::path& p) -> std::optional<Arcane::Editor::TextViewState>
        {
            if (m_config.headless || !Arcane::Settings<Arcane::Editor::TextSettings>().rememberViewState)
                return std::nullopt;
            return m_textViewStates.Get(p.generic_string());
        };
        sv.saveViewState = [this](const std::filesystem::path& p, Arcane::Editor::TextViewState s)
        {
            if (m_config.headless || !Arcane::Settings<Arcane::Editor::TextSettings>().rememberViewState)
                return;
            m_textViewStates.Put(p.generic_string(), std::move(s));
        };
    }
```

### Task TE6-26: Vim goldens -- Normal and Visual; automation keys reach vim as typed keys through `HandleKey` (spec s11.4) [after TE5d + TE6-23; consumed by VIM-GATE]

TE6-23's `editor.text.automation.keys` injects plain characters into the view (`TextEditorView::InjectCharacters`). That is the wrong door for vim: injected characters arrive on the next `Draw` through the view's character stream, vim key notation (`<Esc>`, `<C-v>`) would be typed literally, and the result would depend on frame timing. With vim attached, the automation keys are typed one at a time through the entry a real keystroke uses: for each key of `*ParseKeys(keys)`, `VimEditorRuntime::Get().AdapterFor(view)->Vim().HandleKey(key, now)` (remap on, because after TE5d-3 `HandleKey` calls `FeedMapped`), synchronously, before the first capture. A beep ends only that key; the next key is a new `HandleKey` and still runs (D-R12). With vim off, TE6-23's `InjectCharacters` path is unchanged.

```cpp
// ArcaneTests/src/Text/TextAutomationVimTest.cpp
// TE6-26: editor.text.automation.keys reach vim through VimState::HandleKey
// (one typed key at a time; remap stays on because HandleKey calls FeedMapped),
// not through the view's character stream. With vim off there is no adapter
// and the caller injects characters. A beep does not drop the keys after it.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Helpers/SettingsSweep.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Document/TextDocument.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/TextAutomation.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/VimEditorRuntime.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/VimViewAdapter.hpp"

#include <filesystem>

#include <string_view>

using namespace Arcane;
using namespace Arcane::Editor;

namespace
{
    // Row 0 "alpha", row 1 "beta gamma", row 2 "delta epsilon": jjw lands on "epsilon".
    constexpr std::string_view kSample = "alpha\nbeta gamma\ndelta epsilon\n";
    constexpr Text::ByteOffset kEpsilon = 6 + 11 + 6;

    struct TempTextFile
    {
        std::filesystem::path path;
        explicit TempTextFile(std::string_view bytes)
            : path(std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "arcane-te6-26-automation.txt")
        {
            std::ofstream out(path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
            out.write(bytes.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));
        }
        ~TempTextFile()
        {
            std::error_code ec;
            std::filesystem::remove(path, ec);
        }
    };

    std::unique_ptr<TextDocument> OpenDoc(const std::filesystem::path& p)
    {
        std::string error;
        std::unique_ptr<TextDocument> doc = TextDocument::Open(p, TextDocumentServices{}, error);
        INFO("open error: " << error);
        REQUIRE(doc != nullptr);
        return doc;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("automation keys: with vim on they run as vim keys (jjw moves, nothing is typed)", "[text-vim-automation]")
{
    const Test::ScopedCodeRung vimOn("editor.text.vim.enabled", CVarValue::Bool(true));
    const TempTextFile file(kSample);
    std::unique_ptr<TextDocument> doc = OpenDoc(file.path);
    VimViewAdapter* adapter = VimEditorRuntime::Get().AdapterFor(doc->View());
    REQUIRE(adapter != nullptr);

    CHECK(FeedAutomationKeysToVim(doc->View(), "jjw"));
    CHECK(adapter->Vim().Mode() == Text::VimMode::Normal);
    const std::vector<Text::VimCursor> cursors = adapter->Vim().Cursors();
    REQUIRE(cursors.size() == 1u);
    CHECK(cursors.front().head == kEpsilon);
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());                 // the letters were commands, not text
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().CanUndo());
}

    REQUIRE(adapter != nullptr);

    CHECK(FeedAutomationKeysToVim(doc->View(), "jjwv"));

    CHECK(adapter->Vim().Mode() == Text::VimMode::Normal);
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
}

    CHECK(VimEditorRuntime::Get().AdapterFor(doc->View()) == nullptr);
    CHECK_FALSE(FeedAutomationKeysToVim(doc->View(), "jjw"));
    CHECK_FALSE(doc->Buffer().Dirty());
}
```

```cpp
#pragma once
// Headless automation for the text goldens (TE6-23/24/26): Dev|Hidden cvars
// read ONCE on the first UI frame (after --set), like editor.settings.openAtBoot.
#include <string>
#include <string_view>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    class TextEditorView;

    struct TextAutomationRequest
    {
        std::string openFile;    // relative to the project root
        std::string findQuery;   // opens the find bar with this query
        std::string split;       // "" | "vertical" | "horizontal"
        std::string keys;        // vim key notation when vim is attached, else ASCII characters injected into the view
    };
    [[nodiscard]] TextAutomationRequest ReadTextAutomation();

    // TE6-26: runs `keys` one at a time through VimState::HandleKey, the typed path a
    // real keystroke uses. Remap stays on: HandleKey calls FeedMapped (TE5d-3). A beep
    // clears only that call; the next key still runs (D-R12). Returns true when a vim
    // adapter is attached to `view`. Returns false when vim is not attached, so the
    // caller injects the keys as characters (TextEditorView::InjectCharacters).
    // Notation ParseKeys refuses (truncated UTF-8) feeds nothing and still returns true.
    [[nodiscard]] bool FeedAutomationKeysToVim(TextEditorView& view, std::string_view keys);
}
```

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/TextAutomation.cpp` -- add the includes and the function below TE6-23's `ReadTextAutomation` (the four `ARC_CVAR` declarations and `ReadTextAutomation` stay exactly as TE6-23 wrote them):

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/View/VimEditorRuntime.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/View/VimViewAdapter.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimKey.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimState.hpp"

#include <optional>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Editor
{
    bool FeedAutomationKeysToVim(TextEditorView& view, std::string_view keys)
    {
        VimViewAdapter* adapter = VimEditorRuntime::Get().AdapterFor(view);
        if (!adapter) return false;                                         // vim off: characters instead
        const std::optional<std::vector<Text::VimKey>> parsed = Text::ParseKeys(keys);
        if (!parsed) return true;                                           // nothing vim can run; inject nothing either
        double now = 0.0;
        for (const Text::VimKey& key : *parsed)
            (void)adapter->Vim().HandleKey(key, now += 0.001);              // typed path: the next key still runs after a beep
        return true;
    }
}
```

`ArcaneTests/src/Text/VimDivergenceNotesTest.cpp`:

```cpp
// VIM-GATE (findings 6.3, 6.4): the oracle's divergence notes, checked
// mechanically. Every `divergence:` note starts with "[<id>] " where <id> is a
// VimDivergences() item (the list the vim help page shows), and the set of
// cited ids equals the gate's reviewed list. A new or dropped divergence fails
// here until this list -- and, for a new id, VimDivergences() -- change on purpose.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Helpers/ConstantScan.hpp"            // RepoRoot()
#include "Text/Helpers/VimCases.hpp"           // ParseVimCaseFile (TE5a-6)
#include "TextEditor/Vim/VimDivergences.hpp"   // VimDivergences (TE5c-16)

#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <iterator>
#include <set>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>

using namespace Arcane;

namespace
{
    // The divergence ids reviewed at VIM-GATE (Neovim v0.12.5, D-R12).
    const std::set<std::string> kGateDivergenceIds = {
        "/pat/e", "\\%[", "\\n in a :s replacement", "\\u \\U \\l \\L", "\\ze",
        "macro key text", "opened folds", "zc on indentation folds",
    };

    // "[<id>] <why>" -> <id>; "" when the note does not start with a bracketed id.
    std::string NoteId(std::string_view note)
    {
        if (!note.starts_with('['))
            return {};
        const std::size_t close = note.find("] ");
        return close == std::string_view::npos ? std::string{} : std::string(note.substr(1, close - 1));
    }
}

TEST_CASE("vim gate: every divergence note cites a VimDivergences id, and the cited ids are the reviewed set", "[text-vim-divergence]")
{
    std::set<std::string> listed;
    for (const Text::VimDivergence& d : Text::VimDivergences())
        listed.insert(std::string(d.item));

    std::set<std::string> cited;
    std::size_t divergentCases = 0;
    for (const auto& e : std::filesystem::directory_iterator(Test::RepoRoot() / "ArcaneTests" / "data" / "vim"))
    {
        if (e.path().extension() != ".vimcases")
            continue;
        std::ifstream in(e.path(), std::ios::binary);
        const std::string text{ std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>() };
        const Test::VimCaseFile file = Test::ParseVimCaseFile(text, e.path().generic_string());
        for (const Test::VimCase& c : file.cases)
        {
            if (c.divergence.empty())
                continue;
            ++divergentCases;
            INFO(e.path().filename().string() << ": " << c.name << " -- divergence: " << c.divergence);
            const std::string id = NoteId(c.divergence);
            CHECK_FALSE(id.empty());                   // "divergence: [<id>] <why>"
            CHECK(listed.contains(id));                // documented in VimDivergences()
            cited.insert(id);
        }
    }
    WARN("divergent cases: " << divergentCases);       // VIM-GATE Step 3 compares it with the oracle's skipped total
    CHECK(cited == kGateDivergenceIds);
}
```

The ids are `VimDivergence::item` exactly (the C++ literal `"\\%["` is the text `\%[`). `macro key text` is TE5c-16's row `{ "macro key text", "a macro register holds Arcane key notation (<Esc>), not raw bytes", "macros are key text (spec s6.3); Neovim stores the raw ESC byte" }` (added at the plan-revision-2 reconcile, G5).

Build, then run `.\ArcaneTests.exe "[text-vim-divergence]" -s -r compact` from the Debug exe dir. Expected: 1 case green, and the WARN line `divergent cases: 8` (or the count after any justified additions).
